*Insanity Heaven*
*A troubadour wandering the shrouded recesses of a dark forest. Mindless automatons toiling amidst walls long perished to the ages. A girl of gentle years weeping under the glow of dusk.*
*It all began with the day of twilight.*
*Brrnnnnng. Brrnnnnng. Brrnnnnnnnnnng—*
Sorami: "...mhm..."
*A shrill sound jolted my fleeting consciousness back to reality, making me feel like a spinning top forcefully put to a halt. Not the most pleasant of feelings, all things considered.*
Sorami: "What...?"
*A tingling numbness crawled along my left cheek and arm. I had given up on forming sensible thoughts until my brain finished rebooting.*
*Brrnnnnng. Brrnnnnng. Brrnnnnnnnnnng—*
*Yet the ringing noise refused to cease, eventually growing painful in my ears and irritating my senses.*
*If I had to compare it to anything, I'd say the sensation was akin to a screwdriver drilling into my eyeballs. Ugh, that'd surely leave a mark in the morning.*
Sorami: "K-Keep it... down..."
*With the rebooting of my brain finally complete, I lifted my head and cast a drowsy look at my surroundings, finding their vague contours enveloped by an orange glow.*
Sorami: What... was this place, again...?
After a number of hasty blinks, I finally began taking in my surroundings: wooden desks and chairs ordered into neat lines, a blackboard, and a notice board with a bunch of notes stuck to it.
*It was a classroom. Mhm. I must've fallen asleep and my head was still trying to figure out what was what.*
Sorami: So nobody even bothered to wake me up after class, huh...
*I spent a few moments grumbling over my situation. Some friends I had. Wait, forget my friends; wasn't it normally a teacher's job to wake sleeping students...?*
*Brrnnnnng. Brrnnnnng. Brrnnnnnnnnnng—*
Sorami: My god, will you give that a rest already?!
*Irritated, I jumped out of my seat and glanced around the room.*
Sorami: Wait a second! Why is nobody answering the damn phone? I was trying to catch up on some beauty sleep over here!
*...And then I finally realized something that should have been obvious from the start.*
Sorami: What the...?
*The classroom was empty.*
*There wasn't a single soul in the room, save for me. Well, that by itself wasn't particularly strange. I guess everyone just decided to abandon me in my sleep, and I couldn't exactly blame them for it.*
*I then spotted yet another abnormality in the room.*
*Brrnnnnng. Brrnnnnng. Brrnnnnnnnnnng—*
Sorami: Why would a phone be there...?
*This was a classroom... so why would I be hearing a ringing sound in here? Whence comest thou, O sound?*
I spotted the culprit in question with little to no effort: an ancient-looking black phone rested conspicuously atop the teacher's desk.
Sorami: Are you kidding me...? Who the hell left this here?
*Yet there it was, without a shred of doubt, filling the room with its shrill tone like it was the most normal thing in the world.*
*It made my head hurt to the point where I thought the sound was physically tampering with my brain in some way. My body felt heavy and sluggish, like I had caught a cold or something.*
*I certainly thought the situation was strange, but right now, the pain was my utmost concern.*
*Argh, enough of your damn ringing already! I finally got close enough to pick up the receiver and put an end to this auditory nightmare.*
Sorami: Hello?
*My frustration slipped into my tone; the person on the other end could no doubt make out the belligerent crudeness of it.*
*The headache was seriously killing me. And the dizziness... Almost like I had a fever.*
*It was so bright... I attempted closing my eyes, but the orange rays still pierced through my eyelids, making me feel as if my brain itself was illuminated by its flickering lights.*
*However... The person on the other end of the line showed no sign of surprise whatsoever. His voice was dispassionate, cold as ice.*
Setsuna: "My name is Tendou Setsuna. Yours?"
*His mechanical tone instantly dispelled the haze enveloping my mind.*
Sorami: Eh? Wha... What?
Setsuna: "Your... name."
*My name. My name was... My name was... um... let's see... hmm...*
Sorami: Sora... mi.
*Yes, my name was Kugutsu Sorami. I really wished my parents had picked something more feminine-sounding, but there you had it.*

*Killed?*
*I spent a few moments trying to process the word before answering him.*
Sorami: ...What?

*I was now standing in a long, straight hallway, with no idea where to go.*

*I was going to be killed.*

*I needed a place where I could be alone. Somewhere I could hide.*
Sorami: Hahh...

*I was... simply scared. To realize that I would be next — to know my life was in the crosshairs — paralyzed me with fear.*

*At this point, I couldn't think of it as anything more than just a dream — the kind that rears its ugly head numerous times during people's lives.*
*A dream where you're being chased by someone or something.*
Teacher / Belial: Hmm, being chased by something, huh... Strange, I don't recall giving you that much homework.
Sorami: Crap. There was homework?
*It had completely slipped my mind.*
Teacher / Belial: Sure there was. The kind that I very much doubt you could finish in just one day. Well, I did give you the assignment last week, though.
Sorami: ......
*His expression shifted into that of a teacher looking at a soon-to-be dropout.*
Teacher / Belial: You can't remember it? Seriously, what am I going to do with you...?
*It seemed like he did consider me to be on the level of a dropout.*
Sorami: I am utterly and thoroughly ashamed, Sir.
*I scratched the back of my head. It wasn't like I could really help it; after all, I had no memories to work with.*
*Wait a second. I _did_ have memories.*
Sorami: ...Oh.
Teacher / Belial: What's wrong?
Sorami: Ah, nothing. I just remembered the assignment. An essay in English, right?
Teacher / Belial: Huh, you're not completely beyond help, I see. So? Think you can pull it off?
Sorami: I do. In fact, I'll finish all of it. Um, let's see—
*Yeah. I was going to hand in some sorry excuse for a rough draft.*
Sorami: I was planning to give it some extra polish today, then hand it in first thing in the morning tomorrow.
Teacher / Belial: Well, aren't you the model student.
Sorami: Yup, I sure am. That's just how things are!
Teacher / Belial: I'd say it's proof of your hardworking spirit.
Sorami: I never really considered myself a model student, really...
Teacher / Belial: I see. Well, let's leave it at that. The important part is that you don't forget to hand in your assignment tomorrow. And try not to have any more nightmares, alright?
Sorami: Yeah, um, controlling what dreams I have is beyond impossible, even for someone like me...
Teacher / Belial: Someone like you? Just how high of an opinion do you have of yourself, hm? Well, whatever. Maybe try stuffing something cheery under your pillow.
Sorami: Oh, then I might try one of The Noodles' DVDs.
*The Noodles were a comic duo known not for their TV performances, but rather their stage appearances. And though I was not able to go see them live at a theater, I did end up buying their sketches on DVD.*
*Well, I realize my constant praising may not change too many minds, so go check 'em out yourself. And that's it for my brief PSA.*
Teacher / Belial: A few sketches have horror elements in them, so be careful.
Sorami: ...You seem awfully well-versed on this subject, Professor.
*After spending a good ten minutes losing myself in a heated discussion with Professor Kumamoto over the merits of this or that comedic duo, I decided to finally excuse myself and be on my way.*
*Well then.*
*No doubt owing to my mind beginning to be fully liberated from the haunting memories of that nightmare, I sensed a fresh surge of memories washing over me in fierce waves.*
*My name was Kugutsu Sorami. I had both of my parents and a sister called Shiina. She attended the same school and would always accompany me on my way home.*
*Yup, so far, so good. My memories began to return at the smooth pace of a well-oiled cogwheel.*
*I recalled memories of my youth. Times when I was happy. Times when I was sad. Joy and sorrow, pain and anger.*
*Certain details were still vague, but I figured that to be within the bounds of what could still be considered natural.*
*Around the same time I remembered last night's dinner — a plate of rice omelette — I heard a female voice call out to me.*
Schoolgirl C / Messenger: Ah, Kugutsu. Hello. On your way home, I presume?
Sorami: Ah, um... yep. I... think so.
Schoolgirl C / Messenger: Don't let me keep you, then. Your sister's waiting.
Sorami: ...Um, can I ask you something? Who... are you?
*The girl cocked her head to the side, staring back at me with the expression of someone who had just been deeply insulted.*
*She bore a slight resemblance to a certain white-robed ghost from a horror flick that was all the rage just a few years back. In any event, she gave me the chills.*
*She was certainly beautiful, yet her unusually long hair spilled forward in unkempt strands, lending her a positively Sadako-ish aura.*
Schoolgirl C / Messenger: Oh? Don't you recognize me?
Sorami: ...G-Gimme a sec, I'll totally remember it!
*She's... uh...*
Sorami: Saddy!
Schoolgirl C / Messenger: That's just my nickname, though. Not my real name.
Sorami: S-Sorry! Um... let's see...
*Suddenly, it came to me.*
*Wait, no. It didn't _quite_ feel like remembering something.*
Sorami: You're Urushibara Aomi... right?
*Aomi nodded, her features loosening into a lovely smile.*
Schoolgirl C / Messenger: Yup, you got it! I'm so happy! I'm Urushibara from the Broadcasting Club. Nice to meet you!
Sorami: Oh, so we _were_ strangers.
Schoolgirl C / Messenger: Yes, we were, Miss Amnesiac.
Sorami: Ah, actually... my memories came back just fine. I sort of just needed to, y'know, get my act together and stuff.
Schoolgirl C / Messenger: Aw, that's no fun.
Sorami: I fell asleep in the middle of class and had this pretty vile nightmare. Kinda ruffled my senses, to say the least. But that's all behind me now.
*I'd take all those haunting memories, chuck them in a room and swallow the key; be done with them, so to speak. But just like a stubborn piece of chewing gum refusing to let go of one's shoe, they kept tormenting me, even now.*
*I wondered if "torment" would truly be the right word to describe it. _What if they were a warning?_*
Schoolgirl C / Messenger: So what kind of dream was—
Sorami: No idea! Totally forgot about it, yup! It's all gone, poof. Just like that. Overwritten. No backups.
Schoolgirl C / Messenger: I keep telling people to use the "Save As" function, though...
Sorami: Not me, that's for sure. I mean, we'd just met.
Schoolgirl C / Messenger: Ah, true enough.
*She gave a comprehending nod. Our conversation was really having a tough time moving forward. It felt kinda odd.*
Sorami: Anyway, did you need something from me?
Schoolgirl C / Messenger: Um... well, I sort of felt like talking to you.
Sorami: Me?
Schoolgirl C / Messenger: Yes, you.
*Another lovely smile — the kind that could heal the sick. She really should try and make that her default expression, because the moment she shifted to that frigid glare of hers, it was back to creepy ghost mode all over again.*
*...Boy, I was really being rude to her in my mind. And I'd just met her!*
Sorami: Well, fine. What do we talk about?
Schoolgirl C / Messenger: Nice weather we're having, don't you think?
Sorami: Th-That's where you wanna start? I mean, sure, the weather's... nice... and... stuff...
I couldn't finish the rest of the sentence as the blinding orange of dusk invaded the corridor through the windows. All of a sudden, I recalled the nightmare. That's right: back in the dream, I was sleeping at my desk in the classroom.
Sorami: A phone...
Schoolgirl C / Messenger: Huh?
Sorami: Ah, I just remembered bits and pieces of my dream. It included a ringing phone.
Schoolgirl C / Messenger: Oh? That's news to me.
Sorami: Well, duh. It was in my dream, after all. Anyway, it sat upon the teacher's podium — one of those ancient models.
*...The memories of my dream came trickling back into my mind in gradual fragments. Still, I had neither the time, willingness, or obligation to go over each and every detail.*
Schoolgirl C / Messenger: Could you go into more detail about that?
Sorami: Ah, sorry, but I really shouldn't keep my sister waiting. I'll fill you in tomorrow once I've remembered everything, okay?
*I gave her a brief wave of my hand and turned to be on my way.*
Sorami: Anyway, I'll see you later!
*I ran and ran, breaking into a dash — if not a full-on sprint — sure to put my trusty legs to work as I bolted down a whole set of stairs.*
*It actually made me recall how I spent a decent amount of time rushing up and down flights of stairs in my dream.*
*In any case, the laws of physics weren't completely flipped upside-down anymore. Back in the dream, I recalled going up seven floors, then down ten. That school was like a fortress.*
*Needless to say, the classroom I needed to reach didn't require a herculean effort of that caliber. In fact, I arrived within a minute — Class 1-3.*
Sorami: Let's see... ah, found ya.
*I carefully slid the door open and inspected the classroom — and there she was, gazing idly out the window.*
*It appeared she had yet to notice me... Or maybe not. She abruptly turned around, meeting my gaze.*
Shiina / Gethel: C'mon, Sis, you took forever!
*I met her smile with a few rapid sorries, then gave her hair a sisterly ruffle.*
Shiina / Gethel: Your punishment is having to buy me ice cream from Baldatz!
Sorami: Wait a sec. You have any idea how much they charge for stuff over there? I'm only getting you a hundred-yen cone, missy.
*The "Baldatz" was one of those posh ice cream shops in town, boasting astronomical prices compared to what the average person would expect an ice cream to cost.*
*You would no doubt expect the flavor to make up for that, but in my humble opinion, the price didn't quite match the experience. Or maybe my tongue was simply too indoctrinated to only be able to enjoy average, homely flavors.*
*I was also not a huge fan of that creepy-looking vulture they had as a mascot. Seriously, who thought to make a profit with that thing?*
Shiina / Gethel: Ugh, you're such a stingy old bum, Sis.
Sorami: Hehe! And proud of it, too!
*I struck a pose, placing the back of my hand to one cheek, giggling like some spoiled princess. Shiina, in turn, eyeballed me like I was a being from another dimension.*
Shiina / Gethel: Well, whatever. Shall we go?
*Good idea. We'd go home, change out of our school uniforms and into comfy sweatshirts while enjoying Mom's homemade dinner.*
*A crude image flashed before my eyes, though I wondered if calling it a vision may be more appropriate of an expression.*
*Fragments of that grotesque nightmare blossomed into view, staying for no longer than a second.*
Sorami: Ah—
*A ravaged, worn down classroom in complete disorder, fallen victim to the jaws of decay, its very air reeking of corruption.*
*The stench of shriveled corpses. Or that of skeletal remains, strands of decayed flesh still clinging to their bones.*
Sorami: Nngh...
*I shook my head and the world was once again back to normal.*
Shiina / Gethel: What's wrong?
Sorami: Wow, that dream really did a number on me...
Shiina / Gethel: What dream?
Sorami: The kind where I was being chased by someone.
*It was like watching TV and seeing a momentary flash of static flicker on-screen — almost as if someone was jamming my vision.*
*Every time it happened, my eyes would see through the veil of a clean, ordered world...*
*...and gaze deep into a hellish abyss in all its wretched glory.*
Sorami: ......
*Dozens upon dozens of corpses littered the hallways under the scarlet rays of dusk — the tortured, mutilated remains of people massacred by this world's omnipotent tyrant.*
*Brrnnnnng.*
*The sheer volume of the audiovisual stimuli flooding my senses left my mind a complete and utter wreck.*
Sorami: Ugh...
*I fell to my knees in the middle of the hallway as an oppressive feeling of nausea overcame me, the kind that could make one's stomach entirely too eager to part with its contents.*
*Brrnnnnng. Brrnnnnng. Brrnnnnnnnnnng—*
*The phone's incessant ringing wouldn't let up, its shrill like the echo of distant thunder.*
Shiina / Gethel: S-Sis, you okay?!
*We needed to get out of here, and fast. However, _we couldn't stray too far_.*
*We still had... um... ah, right.*
Sorami: An hour.
*We had to stay within these walls for a whole hour.*
Shiina / Gethel: Hm? An hour?
*Shiina gave me a puzzled look. I took her hand, driven by a sisterly feeling of responsibility to protect her.*
Sorami: ...Anyway, we need to get out of here.
Shiina / Gethel: But why?
Sorami: No buts!
I took off, forcibly pulling Shiina behind me as the two of us raced through long hallways, swiftly yet with no particular destination in mind, focusing on one thing only: escape.
*Soon enough, the world around us began to shift and distort. I turned around, only to witness the hallway behind us being painted anew in midnight colors, its walls viciously eroded by darkness the hue of tar.*
Shiina / Gethel: Huh? Huuuh?
*The sun abruptly vanished, allowing the frigid night to take over its domain. I inhaled a lungful of the stagnant air, detecting — ever so faintly — the acrid stench of decay.*
Sorami: Shiina, I want you to be a good girl and just do what I say!
Realization dawned upon me: what I had experienced before waking up was no mere nightmare, but a palpable, tangible reality. Or could _this_ be the dream?
*An eerie darkness shrouded the hallway in gloom, thick enough that I was having difficulty making out Shiina's face. The moment I placed a foot on the floor, I felt my balance slipping.*
Sorami: ...!
*The linoleum flooring beneath my feet had _rotted away_, catching one of my legs in a chasm of impenetrable blackness.*
Shiina / Gethel: S-Sis!
Sorami: S-Sorry. Pull me up!
*Shiina wasted no time in rushing to my aid, attempting to pull me up by the arm as I steadied myself with the leg I still had free. As she did, I felt a jolt of pain in my ankle — the one lodged in the floor.*
Sorami: Ow...!
Shiina / Gethel: Just a bit more...!
*Suddenly, my body slipped free and I collapsed on the floor behind me. Whatever had been locking my ankle in place finally let up.*
*I ended up tackling Shiina with my back, pinning her on the ground.*
Shiina / Gethel: H-Hey, that hurt...
Sorami: S-Sorry, I'll get up in a sec.
*As I placed both hands on the ground and was about to push myself up, I felt an odd sensation at my ankle, the same one that had just been rescued.*
Shiina / Gethel: S-Sis! Your leg!
Sorami: ......
*What I saw there completely petrified me. _A decayed human hand_ was latching onto my ankle.*
Shiina / Gethel: U-Ughh...
*Shiina staggered backwards with an expression of pure disgust. I attempted to shake off the hand, but all my efforts proved fruitless — it refused to let go.*
Sorami: Persistent little...!
*I put my free leg to use without hesitation, launching a fierce kick to rid myself of the stubborn limb.*
Shiina / Gethel: Whoa...
*Shiina assumed a safe distance between the two of us. Oh, come on. Did she think I was doing this because I wanted to?*
Shiina / Gethel: U-Um... Sis? Wh-What is that thing?
Sorami: Well, it looks like a rotten hand to me. H-Hopefully a fake one, haha...
*Unfortunately, my instincts were telling me that it was very much real.*
Shiina / Gethel: A-And what's a thing like that doing here at school...?
*Shiina's tone was audibly — and unsurprisingly — laden with fear. Well, no wonder. I myself was just as terrified, just as chilled to the core as her.*
*...And then I noticed something I genuinely wished to ignore.*
Sorami: ......
*Numerous green blemishes pockmarked the hand's decaying skin. I simply sat and gazed at it in silence while struggling not to vomit.*
*I was at a complete loss, unable to process the situation. In the end — my whole body trembling at the sheer thought of what I was about to do — I slowly lowered my hands into the hole on the floor.*
Shiina / Gethel: S-Sis?!
Sorami: Ugh... Gh...!
*My fingers caught something. I poured strength into my arms, lifting the soft, decayed _thing_.*
*It was certainly not light; in fact, it felt quite heavy, though the fact it was only a torso worked in my favor. In any event, I dragged _it_ out of the hole.*
Shiina / Gethel: ...!
Shiina was paralyzed by the sight: that is, a corpse with its hand torn clean off.
*The body had undergone partial skeletonization, with patches of decayed flesh still loosely clinging onto it here and there; I assumed it to be the body of a girl. I was no doctor, yet two primary things still caught my attention.*
*The first concerned the skull, particularly the way it had been sliced in half diagonally.*
*The corpse's normally round head was therefore missing a considerable chunk due to the nightmarish work of a sharp, bladed weapon of some kind. Whether or not this constituted the cause of death remained unclear.*
*The second thing felt far more noteworthy to me personally, as it had just proven something of critical importance.*
*The corpse was clothed in the very same kind of school uniform I wore.*
Sorami: Ugh...
*There was something particularly gut-wrenching about seeing a decaying corpse wearing a school uniform. It wasn't just the kind of dead body one would commonly encounter in movies or manga.*
*This body was here, in the flesh, right before my very eyes. Wearing a school uniform. The same kind as mine. In short, she was most likely around my age.*
*Her young life had been ended by someone lacking even a shred of compassion. In fact, the deed happened not so far from the two of us.*
*The grisly sight of a schoolgirl's lifeless body left me terrified beyond comprehension; I felt my chest being gnawed at from the inside by sheer dread.*
*Almost like I was staring my very own future in the eye.*
*Only the low thrum of my own heartbeat pierced the silence. Our sole relief — the ringing of that phone — was nowhere to be heard.*
Shiina / Gethel: Sis... wasn't this girl one of your classmates?
Sorami: What?
Shiina / Gethel: I mean, look...
*Shiina scooped up an ID card from the ground nearby and held it up so I could have a better look.*
*The name written on it made the final strand of reason I was still clinging onto in my mind evaporate in an instant.*
*"Nagumo Yuuri"*
Sorami: This can't be real...
I had two reasons to feel that way. First off: the Nagumo Yuuri I knew wouldn't die like this.
And second: even assuming she was dead, that she was murdered...
*...there was no way her body would be in such an advanced state of decay. After all, it hadn't been that long since we last talked and said goodbye to each other.*
*I refused to believe this hollow, withered husk of a human being would be my friend...!*
Shiina / Gethel: Sis...
*Shiina's voice restored a semblance of order to my panic-stricken thoughts.*
Sorami: ...Let's go. We need to get out of here.
Shiina / Gethel: Wh-What's even going on here? Sis! I'm scared...
Sorami: Let's just _go_! You can cry all you want once this is over!
Shiina / Gethel: ......
*Shiina gave me a silent nod. Good girl. If she had broken down crying, I wasn't confident I could have held back the tears either.*
*I was afraid. Terrified to my very core.*
*There was something in the air — a dense, near-suffocating presence of ill will.*
*It was neither mere bloodlust, nor pure hatred. Instead, I felt the vicious playfulness of a predator wondering how best to torment and toy around with its prey.*
*I could feel that very predator's eyes on my skin. And so I ran — through long hallways, down the stairs, then back up and down again.*
*There was no sign of any life around us, the once-crowded campus now utterly devoid of its former bustle of students coming and going.*
*This had to be a continuation of that nightmare. Were my dreams invading reality itself, or was it the other way around? Had I merely been having a long, long dream, one that I was now waking up from?*
*I couldn't tell. The memories I once thought clear and definite began to blur, drifting farther and farther into obscurity.*
I considered the worst: that I had gone completely mad. What if I was actually locked up in a hospital room somewhere?
*What if this was all just the figment of my own imagination? A vivid hallucination, nothing more?*
*The very thought robbed my knees of all strength.*
*I led Shiina onward, driven by an unquenchable sense of duty and responsibility. The warmth of her hand in mine, moist from traces of sweat; the common memories we shared — those were the only things still clear in my mind.*
Shiina / Gethel: Sis, we should stay in that classroom!
*I felt her pulling on my arm. It wasn't a bad idea — a classroom certainly was more appealing than an endless trek through the hallways.*
*I flung the classroom door open and darted inside. That may have proven to be a fatal mistake.*
Shiina / Gethel: ...!
*Both Shiina and I were left speechless by what we found inside. Numerous corpses — their heads sliced clean off — were neatly lined up next to each other.*
*There were roughly an even number of male and female students among the bodies, each wearing a school uniform.*
Sorami: Ah... kh...!
*Tears began to trickle down my cheeks.*
Sorami: P-Professor...
*Professor Kumamoto was up on the podium — _only his torso, though_. His features contorted into an expression of hellish pain, hiding very little of the sheer anguish he must have gone through in his final moments.*
Two decapitated heads hung from the ceiling: Ada and his girlfriend. The former wore a mask of silent terror, while the latter's features reflected grim acceptance.
*A sight befitting only the cruelest of nightmares — yet here it was before my very eyes, in all its hellish reality.*
Shiina / Gethel: Sis...
*Shiina huddled closer to me; I immediately regretted not telling her earlier to avert her gaze.*
Sorami: We probably shouldn't stare at them for too long...
*Shiina coiled her arms around mine. I gave each of the bodies a long, careful look while making absolutely sure not to breathe through my nose.*
*I timidly drew closer to the podium to inspect Professor Kumamoto's body — the blood had dried.*
I reached out to touch the head dangling from the ceiling: it was the same, just like I had expected.
*In an act of trying to block out the sheer abnormality of the situation, the cogwheels in my brain began to turn.*
*Something felt off.*
*There was something odd about all the decayed corpses we came across, including these ones. In fact, the whole situation reeked of foul play.*
*How come all the blood had _already dried_? How could that even be possible? It hadn't been ten minutes since I'd last talked to Professor Kumamoto.*
*The corpse's skin felt more than just slightly chilly to the touch. It was positively frigid.*
*Now, I was no doctor, but could a dead body really turn this cold in such a brief span of time?*
Shiina / Gethel: Wh-What's wrong...?
Sorami: I don't know... perhaps this is one of those cases where things are better left unsaid...
Shiina / Gethel: Tell me, Sis.
Sorami: Um, alright. So I met Professor Kumamoto just a short while back. Then Ada... and his girlfriend.
Shiina / Gethel: Right.
Sorami: And then I had this thought.... basically, aren't their corpses _too_ cold? I know, I'm being silly. It's probably not important.
Shiina / Gethel: ...Y-Yeah. I guess it's not. I mean, look around us. There are real, actual corpses here.
*Shiina nodded in agreement. She was looking at me round-eyed, fear clearly visible in her gaze.*
Sorami: ...I don't want to stay here another second, Shiina. Let's go.
Shiina / Gethel: Okay...
*Shiina turned to slide the classroom door open — or at least she meant to.*
Shiina / Gethel: Huh?
*Her brief whisper of a phrase planted a seed of anxiety in my heart.*
Shiina / Gethel: N-Ngh... huh? Is this a joke? What gives?
*Shiina attempted to force the door open, but it simply would not budge.*
Sorami: What's wrong? Let me take a look.
*I gently pushed Shiina aside to try my luck as well, but I didn't fare any better. The door — almost as if someone was holding it closed from the other side — remained tightly shut.*
Sorami: The hell...? Why won't it open?!
*I tried another door out of sheer desperation — the one at the far side of the room — but none would budge. As a last resort, I turned to try the window as well, but that proved to be wasted effort just the same.*
Shiina / Gethel: ...I just... I can't take this anymore... I wanna go home, Sis...!
*Shiina broke down sobbing, her heart no doubt having buckled under the pressure — I myself was moments away from joining her.*
*In the end, though, my desire to protect her eclipsed the urge to cry. I needed to look after her for just a little while longer.*
Sorami: I guess we have no choice, so... let's just stay here. It's going to be alright, Shiina, don't you worry. Help is coming... I promise.
Shiina / Gethel: Help... is coming? How... how can you even know that...?!
Sorami: I just do. He... he told me himself.
Shiina / Gethel: ...Someone told you?
Sorami: Yup. He knew things would end up like this.
*Shiina stared at me with her mouth agape.*
Shiina / Gethel: Wow... whoever that is, he sounds amazing. Almost like some superhero.
Sorami: I guess so. How do I put it... he sounded a bit odd but dependable.
Shiina / Gethel: Oh, was it a guy? Someone handsome?
*Okay, wait just a second. Was this really the time and place for such a discussion?*
Sorami: D-Don't be silly. This is so not the time.
Shiina / Gethel: It's okay, you needn't be shy about it. So, was he handsome? Did he have a certain alpha feel to him? Or was he a beta? A nerd? Say, how old was he? Does he go to our school? Wait, is he a teacher?
Shiina / Gethel: You said he was a guy, right? Are you sure it wasn't a girl?
*...Okay, wait. Wait up. Hold on for just a second.*
*Shiina launched into one question after another; I needed to calm her down. Something in her just flipped all of a sudden — this was her way of coping with the situation.*
*At this rate, her mind was going to reach a point of no return.*
Shiina / Gethel: Sis! C'mon, tell me, Sis! Tell me! Tell me...!
Sorami: Get a grip of yourself!
*I gave her cheek a loud slap, but she simply went on with an unflinching smile.*
Shiina / Gethel: It's love, Sis! It has to be! Ah, I wish I could fall in love, too...! Aha... ahahaha!
*I could feel the air around us chill.*
Shiina / Gethel: Oh, but I never could because of you! I couldn't fall in love, and it's your fault!
*Wh-What...?*
Sorami: H-Hold up for a second. What is this all about...?
*Shiina glared at me with a pair of crimson eyes burning with hatred as her lips curled into a mocking smile.*
Shiina / Gethel: Don't you remember? Hm? You said you'd never forgive me if I found a boyfriend before you!
*I... I did say that. Numerous times, in fact. But it was a joke, nothing more. I thought she understood.*
Sorami: Th-That was... just a joke. C'mon... I thought you were aware of that!
Shiina / Gethel: Well, I wasn't! What's even a joke, huh?! Maybe it was a joke to you, but it wasn't to me! This is _all_ your fault, Sis! Even the fact we're now stuck here! All _your_ fault!
Sorami: Shiina, that's enough!
Shiina / Gethel: No! You're the one to blame for this, aren't you? This is all your fault, right? So maybe...
*Her sentence ominously broke off in the middle. I took a careful look at her features to find an answer.*
*All that met my gaze was a blank stare. Her lips were moving ever so slightly, but I couldn't quite make out anything.*
*I couldn't notice it at first. No, that wasn't quite right — I did notice, but _chose to ignore it_.*
*No.*
*My heart cried out in protest as a flash of silver lunged at Shiina's throat and buried itself deep in the flesh.*
*It took me mere seconds to realize it was a neatly-ornamented switchblade.*
*That's right, it was... it was a knife. _My_ knife.*
*So why was it buried to the hilt in my beloved sister's throat?*
*Ahahaha. Oh, come on. Even pranks had their limits.*
Shiina / Gethel: S-Sis... why...?
*She groaned at me in a hoarse tone, making it seem almost like I had done something bad.*
*I glanced down at my palms... ...and saw them stained with blood.*
Sorami: Oh, no...
*I staggered backwards. Shiina followed.*
Shiina / Gethel: Sis... you...
*Her voice was the chirp of a rusted flute. Her gaze livid with condemnation.*
Sorami: W-Wait. I didn't...
*My hands were smeared with thick, warm blood. Whose, though?*
Shiina / Gethel: Y-You... killed...
*My mind cracked like a delicate piece of porcelain.*
Sorami: Shiina! Shiina, oh god, no...!
Shiina / Gethel: M-Murd... erer... murderer, murderer, murderer...
Sorami: No! It wasn't me...! It wasn't...!
Shiina / Gethel: A murderer... and a liar...
Sorami: I didn't do it! I didn't! I... I...
*The memories came back to me in vivid detail — how fed up I had been with Shiina's hysterical questioning.*
*I casually pulled out the switchblade from my pocket.*
*Ah, right. I stabbed her.*

*I would have never been able to get this close to her by myself.*
*We had our next break after a mostly eventless class.*

*She found the world to be off. Realizing that there was something positively wrong about it.*

*No student would ever come to such a realization without a certain event to serve as a trigger.*

*She let out another giggle.*
Kurou: Sorry, I didn't meant to confuse you. In any case, let us move on.
*I felt like I was beginning to get closer to the truth about her and would have wished to continue the conversation, but acting too forceful here would only end up hurting her feelings.*
*Please wait here for a second. I'll go get my horse.*

*A moment later, I took notice of something unusual in the corner of my vision.*
Setsuna: Raziel...?

Sorami: Oh, you're right! Razieeeel! Over heeere!

Kurou: In any case, I'll be off, then—
*As Raziel retreated a step, Kurou lightly kicked into the animal's side and trotted off.*
Sorami: Wow... they're so pretty...!

*Once she had completed a full lap, Kurou slowed down and lowered herself from the saddle.*
Kurou: I'll show you to the changing room, then.
*Kurou headed off, with Raziel following her at a short distance.*
Sorami: Raziel riding a horse, huh...
Setsuna: Is something wrong?
Sorami: No, I mean, aren't you excited to see it, Setsuna?
*Excitement. I savored the word in my mind, wondering what it meant.*
Setsuna: Is there some form of pleasure to be gained from her changing clothes?

*I would occasionally have trouble comprehending what Sorami meant. One could say that was one thing I certainly enjoyed to an extent.*
*Sorami — and most likely all the others — knew things I didn't. That made me a little bit happy.*
Setsuna: I will understand once I see it...?
*What would I do if I failed to comprehend even after seeing it? In other words, if what Sorami was seeing differed from what I saw?*
*Wait. See...?*
Setsuna: Sorami, you said I would understand once I had seen it. Does that have anything to do with your powers?
*As I presented my conclusion, Sorami looked at me like she couldn't believe what she had just heard. It appeared she was left astonished.*

*As I made my position clear, she simply shrugged, meeting it with a sigh.*
Sorami: C'mon, don't be so arrogant...!
*...Hm. She appeared to have taken it as boasting.*

Sorami: The point is, this isn't generally something people say about themselves. ...Huh? Wait a sec. Is it just me, or did you sound kinda different from your usual tone just then?
Setsuna: ...No, I didn't.
*I averted my gaze. I seemingly slipped back into old habits from time to time.*
Sorami: Oh, um, maybe I'm just imagining things, then? I mean, you did sound sort of monotone before, so maybe that's why.
*Sorami shrugged, seemingly not bothered by all this. Hmm.*
Sorami: Ah, there she is!
*Kurou approached us, leading the horse by the bridle. Atop the animal sat Raziel, now in full riding gear.*
Setsuna: ......
*According to Sorami, I'd understand once I saw it... Hm. Much as I had expected, I was still having a hard time comprehending this.*
*As far as my feelings were concerned, I wasn't particularly happy. Nor was I sad, for that matter.*

*Raziel gently kicked into the animal's side, which set off at a slow trot, rather than full riding speed.*

*Still, Raziel appeared very much satisfied.*

The scene was indeed highly picturesque: Raziel and the horse, both showered by the rays of dusk.
Sorami: I know, right? By the way, that outfit sure fits her like a glove. Don't you think she looks cute in it?
*I considered that for a moment.*
Setsuna: ...I do.
*I gave her an honest nod.*
Raziel: ......
*For some reason, Raziel began nervously fidgeting in the saddle. Could she have heard my exchange with Sorami?*

*Kurou abruptly interrupted, her gaze distant and without emotion.*

*Yet it had become clear that these were her true feelings. Her tone gave no hint of joy, anger, or even sorrow... she simply stated facts.*

*By the time she turned to face us, Kurou was once again back to her usual, cheery self, with a smile faint as moonlight upon a lake surface.*
Kurou: Um... is something the matter? I'm afraid I've been spacing out a bit.
Setsuna: Nothing much.
*Sorami backed up my curt response with a series of fervent nods.*
Sorami: Ah, nope. Nothing at all. We were just thinking how pretty you looked in the setting sun. Stuff like that.
*I heard the grating of metal upon metal, its clangor violating my ears. In the next moment, both Sorami and I found ourselves under the onslaught of bluish-white waves.*
* How beautiful. Ah, how truly beautiful. And how wretched. How utterly, thoroughly wretched.*
* No. The concept of hatred had all but left me. All I feel towards you is repugnance.*
*A maelstrom of turbulent images and sounds enveloped us, violently hurling a certain someone's innermost feelings our way.*
*You despicable monster. You filthy, wretched girl. And you, woman — disgusting beyond words.*
Setsuna: ...!
*I shook my head with conscious effort, successfully dispelling that overwhelming rush of emotions.*
Kurou: Thank you...
*Her words were the afterglow of a tremendous wave tinted in contrastive feelings; hatred and happiness, sorrow and joy all blending into one.*
*They were broken, succumbed to madness.*
*That was how both Lilith and Raziel described the so-called masters. To think how apt that description truly was.*
*They appeared sound in mind and body alike for the most part.*
*Yet a certain traumatic experience — or a certain heart-wrenching memory — prevented them from confronting the damage a part of their hearts had suffered.*
*They would experience something during their pilgrimages _that no sane mind could possibly withstand_ — and so, madness ravaged them, thoroughly and without mercy.*
*At first glance, Kurou Miyako appeared just like any other person. No, not just "appeared" — she was. That, however, only applied to her student self.*
*Out there in Tokyo Babel, the real Kurou Miyako lay in wait, a mere shadow of her former self.*
Kurou: Oh, welcome back.
*Raziel, still on horseback, trotted closer to us.*
*The horse came closer... And even closer...*
*Then neighed right into my face.*
Setsuna: ...Smells of wildlife.

*Sorami pulled out a notebook, scribbled something on its top page, then handed it to Lilith.*

*Before I could finish that thought, though, Sorami loudly interjected, her tone filled with surprise and shock.*
Sorami: They did?! The Red Sea does look kinda reddish, so maybe there's chili in there...
*This was just a thought, but Sorami seemed to be in the middle of being thoroughly deceived.*

*Sorami triumphantly thrust her fist into the air after a single spoonful of curry. So the food was good... apparently.*

*Utterly dejected, Sorami instead turned to me, still in the middle of working my way through the food.*
Sorami: Whatcha think, Setsuna? Yummy?
Setsuna: Um...
*"I am really sorry, but I lack the ability to discern what a 'good' flavor is."*
*Just as I was about say that, Raziel and Lilith kicked me in the shin near-simultaneously, forcing the words back into my throat. I was not in combat mode, so it hurt quite a bit.*

Setsuna: It is... very... good.
Sorami: Really? I'm so glad!
*My ability to discern flavor may have been handicapped, yet I was certain the relieved smile Sorami flashed my way was sweet. I wanted to tell her that; I felt I would've been right, too.*
I had learned something new today: that not all lies were bad. Although, I was certain I told the truth just now.
*With that said, once everyone had finished their post-meal digestion, Raziel chose to speak up.*
Raziel: I believe that the angel Kurou Miyako devoured was Abdiel.

Setsuna: ...Abdiel. His name means "the servant of God."

Lilith: A no-nonsense traitor who refused to ally himself with demons and angels alike.
Raziel: He didn't wish to force his own ideals onto others.

Setsuna: I see. It is the name of her horse.
Sorami: Horse? You mean Abd?
Raziel: That name came from the word Abdiel. I believe the spirit double — after having been left at Pandora — began looking after a horse that she unconsciously named after her own guardian angel.
Lilith: You see, Abdiel seemed to be the type with a soft spot for humans.
Raziel: I heard he had gone missing, but...
*Raziel let out a concerned sigh.*
Sorami: Did you two know each other?
*She nodded.*
Raziel: He was an old friend of mine. We did fall out of touch following his rebellion, though...
Sorami: Well, I guess you would.
Raziel: He would often visit small corner pubs to drink his frustrations away.
Sorami: Ugh, he sounds like a total geezer! Shouldn't an angel act more like... y'know, an angel?!
Setsuna: Sorami. You must not take Raziel's jokes seriously.
Sorami: Wait, so it _was_ a joke! I mean, I did kinda see it coming, but...
*Raziel went on, her expression showing no sign of concern.*
Raziel: Abdiel was an angel who confronted the world at large, "rejecting" everything. I would assume the stratum under his control had also transformed into something to reflect that mentality.
Sorami: Now that I think about it, wasn't Miyako excessively wary of being touched by others?
Lilith: It's hardly rare for a person to be assigned a guardian angel who matches their personality. Could all be God's will.
*God. What could he have been doing in Heaven right now? At this point, I wasn't even certain he existed up there at all.*
Setsuna: Which left us with one remaining question: how strong Abdiel really was.
*Yet upon hearing those words, Lilith irritatedly bit into her own fingernails.*
Lilith: Plenty strong, trust me. He was powerful enough to have defeated both Ariel, the Lion of God, and the demon lord of vengeance Arioch himself.
*A fallen angel and a demon lord — a powerful pair indeed.*
Raziel: However, what truly sets him apart from the rest is his sheer courage. An angel who rebelled against the twin-powers of Heaven and Hell simultaneously is hardly an event we will likely experience ever again.
Lilith: What's more, he used to be a simple guardian angel, tasked with the protection of one human. Yet he climbed up the ranks at a staggering rate during Lucifer's war, eventually ascending to the position of a Seraph.
*And in the end, he still threw it all away.*
Sorami: Wh-Whoa, hold the phone for a second. Setsuna, can you beat this guy?
Lilith: Who knows. But I'm guessing he's going to need "that," at the very least.
*Lilith pointed at the blade once wielded by Gethel — the Sword of the Seven Deadly Sins.*
*While the sword was incapable of engraving a sin upon angels, it could still very much summon the beasts corresponding to the seven deadly sins.*
*Its very blade was soaked deep in powerful sorcery.*
Lilith: Have no illusions, though: you won't beat Abdiel with that sword alone. To make matters worse, you'll have to face him on his own turf.
Sorami: We'll have to fight Miyako...?
The words sluggishly trickled forth from Sorami's lips. Her astonishment was only natural: after all, we would need to fight and kill a person we'd just befriended.
Lilith: Sorami, the Kurou Miyako you talked to earlier and the one we'll eventually meet are two different people. The latter is a stray hound gone mad with bloodlust, biting every hand it sees.
Raziel: Exactly. Which is all the more reason she must be defeated.
*Raziel balled the hands she had been resting atop the table into fists.*
Sorami: And, um, if we kill the real Miyako... what will happen to the one living here?
Lilith: Nothing at all. She'll continue living her life until either Heaven's gates are opened or Tokyo Babel itself is destroyed. Well, whether or not you'd call this a life is another matter, though.
*Sorami exhaled a relieved sigh, seemingly having accepted the situation.*
Raziel: The bigger problem we face is Abdiel and Kurou Miyako's raison d'etre. At the very least, we ought to find out what it is.
*Their raison d'etre...*
Sorami: Setsuna, you still haven't found yours, right?
*She was right. I had yet to discover my very own raison d'etre.*
Sorami: Oh, almost forgot. We still gotta check up on the other two students, right? Uh... Hinoue and Oshiba, if I remember correctly.
Lilith: Yeah, why?
Sorami: Well, in that case...
*Sorami offered to take care of those two students while I focus on finding my raison d'etre.*
*The other girls agreed. And so, I spent the following two days in Raziel's company in an effort to try and discover my raison d'etre.*
*Unfortunately, the following day's weather was mostly dominated by rain.*
Sorami: Huh... so it rains even at Pandora.
Lilith: Well, we basically just created rainclouds through magic, but yeah. I mean, how weird would it be if it never rained at all, y'know?
Sorami: Well then, we're off to the classroom to do a lil' investigation!
Raziel: Take your time...
*Sorami and Lilith left the room, leaving me alone with Raziel.*
Setsuna: What will you do, Raziel?
*She returned my question with a puzzled look, almost like she didn't entirely comprehend why I even asked.*
Raziel: Shouldn't that be self-evident? I'm helping you.
Setsuna: Helping me...? The fact of the matter is, not even I am sure what I ought to be doing.
Raziel: Well, how about we start with meditation?
*Meditation, huh...*
Setsuna: I have a feeling I know where this is going, but let us do it, nonetheless.
Raziel: Good. All right... I first need you to sit on your knees. Then close your eyes.
*I did exactly as I was told.*
Raziel: Now take a deep breath.
Raziel: Relax yourself... yes, just like that. Pretend your body's about to melt into the very air. That's right... good... just like that... zzz...
Setsuna: ...I knew it.
*She dozed off right before my very eyes. With little other choice in the matter, I decided to contemplate matters on my own.*
*I was "created" for the sole purpose of serving mankind. That was my reason for being.*
*Was there nothing more to it, though? I had a feeling that alone would not be enough.*
*Conversely, that very line of reasoning in itself could very well have been a mistake.*
*"Serving mankind" had an amiable ring to it, true. Yet what I had done was undeniably a deed befitting the most wretched of villains.*
*If I closed my eyes, I could still recall it. A world where man devoured man, where people from all across the globe spilled the blood of their brethren, driven to near-insanity in the wake of overwhelming despair.*
*I was created to save that world, to stand as a beacon of light in the darkness. Yet ultimately, I took mankind's hope for the future... and crushed it in the palm of my hand.*
*I embraced my raison d'etre, only to strangle it to death with my own two hands. Was I, if not a savage to be abhorred, a sinner to be judged?*
*And so I continued to exist, shouldering the resentment of billions.*
*Hmm. In which case...*
Setsuna: Could it be... punishment?
*My raison d'etre was to be punished, for I had committed sins far too great to be overlooked, far too despicable to be judged even by the law.*
Raziel: I don't think so.
*The abruptness of her voice pulled me away from my introspection. Raziel sat neatly in front of me, staring deep into my eyes.*
Raziel: It is true that punishment needs to be meted out, but it's only the means, never the end. You ought not mistake the two. The true meaning of your life is not like that, trust me.
Setsuna: But my entire world was destroyed.
Raziel: And you're still alive.
Setsuna: I... would not call this living. By the time you and Lilith found me, I had most likely already died.
*Raziel shook her head in silence.*
Raziel: The dead can't talk. They can't tell tales, nor can they do anything to change the present. There is a clear difference between someone who's dead, _and someone who leads a life of un-living_.
Setsuna: But...
*She poked me on the forehead right as I was about to present a counter-argument.*
Setsuna: ...?
*Raziel gave me an intense glare. She went on immediately, giving me no opportunity to question what she was doing.*
Raziel: You're a fool, Setsuna. And a dummy and an idiot and a worthless blockhead.
Setsuna: Wh-What brought that on?
Raziel: Dunce, coward, chicken, insect, dimwit, trash, loser, hack, octopus, squid, tuna, salmon...!
Setsuna: The latter half of that is just a sushi recipe...
Raziel: Silence, foolish mortal.
*I felt somewhat lost, but it appeared she had qualms with certain parts of my argument.*
Setsuna: Sorry.
Raziel: This isn't the kind of issue an apology can resolve. Take Kugutsu Sorami, for example...
Setsuna: What about her?
Raziel: What would have happened to her if it weren't for you?
*She probably meant exactly what would have happened to her without me. After analyzing the possible outcomes of a situation in which I wasn't present at the time, I concluded that she most likely would have been killed.*
Raziel: Exactly. It is no exaggeration to say that you essentially saved her life.
Setsuna: Is... that so...
Raziel: The rescuer and the rescued must both acknowledge the value of life. Neither will find happiness otherwise.
Setsuna: ...I have never once considered my own life to hold any value.
*Raziel nodded, then clutched my hand.*
Raziel: I understand. And we have a name for people like that — "heroes." They reject honor and glory, turn their backs on the grace of God, and live only to save other lives.
*Raziel shook her head, sadness palpable in her tone.*
Raziel: Those who see no value in their own lives cannot possibly have a higher reason for their being.
*She once again shook her head, firmly condemning what she had just said.*
Setsuna: Despite that, I still—
*_I still wished to be of use to everyone_.*
Raziel: The fact that you're still without a raison d'etre leaves me uneasy, but we have no choice here. You must proceed to the second stratum and fight in your current condition.
Setsuna: Can we not wait?
*It was a naive thought, something Raziel confirmed by shaking her head.*
Raziel: As far as I can tell, no. As long as you remain here at Pandora, you will never discover your raison d'etre.
Setsuna: So the only option left... is to fight.
Raziel: You may end up discovering your raison d'etre in the heat of battle — everything hangs upon that possibility.
Setsuna: I understand.
Raziel: No, you do not. Remember that you won't go to the second stratum alone. Kugutsu Sorami will accompany you as well.
*Words failed me, but not because I had forgotten about Sorami. I merely took the time to once again savor the sheer gravity of that fact.*
Raziel: Neither I nor Lilith are supposed to aid you on the second stratum. If we did, we'd only be postponing the problem.
*Raziel's gaze showed no trace of emotion.*
Raziel: In other words, if you happen to be defeated on the second stratum, Kugutsu Sorami will die with you.
*I froze up, completely overwhelmed by the revelation that Kugutsu Sorami's life was so closely interwoven with mine.*
*She could no doubt survive, even if I died.*
*That was the conclusion I arrived at. After all, Sorami's eyes — Gethel's eyes — were of critical importance to both Lilith and Raziel.*
Setsuna: Wait. Hold up a second. She has nothing to do with this.
Raziel: She does. You saved Sorami. Her life is your responsibility. Otherwise—
Setsuna: Wait...!
Raziel: Answer me this, then. What would she do if you died?
Raziel: As far as I can tell, Sorami has a very strong sense of responsibility. She would go as far as continue the pilgrimage on her own. How far could she go without you, her guardian, at her side?
*I had no answer to give. Naturally, I could advise Sorami not to consider continuing her pilgrimage in the event of my death.*
*But in that case, Lilith and Raziel could convince her of the opposite, claiming that Gethel's eyes were of vital importance to them.*
*In fact, they wouldn't even need to convince her. Kugutsu Sorami would readily continue her journey across Tokyo Babel without as much as a second thought.*
Raziel: You are responsible for the lives you've saved. You must realize that saving a life is a deed of tremendous gravity.
*Her words pierced my heart like the sharpest steel or the swiftest bullet.*
*Ten billion lives.*
*I recalled the time when I wished to save that many people, yet ultimately collapsed under the weight of that responsibility. Was I truly desperate to help others of my own volition?*
*Or was I merely acting upon someone's orders?*
*In which case... did I abandon them because I was ordered not to save them?*
*I fell deep into thought.*
*Had _I_ been mistaken? Or the ones who created me? The ones who worshipped me?*
*Despite my best efforts, the answer remained vague, locked in darkness. I began to doubt if there even was an answer at all.*
*I kept mulling things over, completely oblivious of Raziel and the outside world.*
Raziel: ...?
*After a short while, I felt the touch of someone's hand on my cheek. Raziel gazed at me with a frown, her expression that of profound compassion.*
Setsuna: Stop that, please.
*That was the first thing I could blurt out. I did not react well to pity or sympathy; if anything, I preferred to be scorned and detested.*
*I'm sorry, I'm so sorry. I was powerless. I couldn't do a thing. Please forgive me, I'm sorry, I'm sorry.*
*Ah, the miserable, poor man! How my heart bleeds for you!*
*I recalled the days when I still lived as my old self. When I was showered by such words.*
Raziel: Why?
Setsuna: Because I hate it.
*Raziel briefly nodded.*
Raziel: I have never in my life hated a person. I looked upon Adam's lament and gave him my book, teaching him of the importance of technology, knowledge, and information.
Raziel: But everything is starting to lose meaning. God has forsaken us. Heaven, Hell, and the mortal realm are lost. All that remains is Tokyo Babel, half-refuge, half-battlefield.
Raziel: May I speak honestly for a moment?
Setsuna: ...Go ahead.
Raziel: It's tough. Unbearable. Sad and frustrating. I wish I could destroy, go on a rampage. I want to cry, to scream at the top of my lungs...
*Raziel's expression mirrored the complexity of her turbulent emotions.*
Raziel: Were we mistaken?
Setsuna: ...?
Raziel: Were the demons correct? Or the angels? How should mortals live their lives? Is complete destruction truly His will?
Setsuna: I... I truly do not know.
*Silence.*
*Plenty of time must have passed. I began counting the sounds of raindrops against the earth to the best of my abilities. 13834, 26567...*
Raziel: My book. My book will surely hold the answer.
*The Sefer Raziel. The book she had lost. The tome with all knowledge contained within.*
*I abruptly realized something.*
Setsuna: Raziel. Is that book your raison d'etre?
Raziel: Yes. The Sefer Raziel means everything to me. It's my very being. As long as it's not with me, I'm unable to confirm my very self.
*Raziel's shoulders drooped forward. She, too, had yet to find her own raison d'etre, in a manner of speaking.*
*Or rather, she had lost sight of it. Neither of us had value to our current lives.*
*I had yet to find it. She had already lost it. That was the only difference.*
Raziel: By the way, the reason I'm prone to falling asleep regardless of the time of day is precisely because I lack my book, which turned my raison d'etre vague and uncertain.
Setsuna: That is not true and you know it.
*I replied immediately.*
*Raziel broke out in sweat. She most likely did not expect me to deliver that line, considering the circumstances.*
Raziel: How did you...?
Setsuna: According to Lilith, your tendency to fall asleep at a moment's notice had been famous even before you lost your book.
Raziel: Gyhu-myhuuu...
*Raziel sunk to her knees while letting out the strangest of moans.*
Setsuna: Also, I would prefer if you did not fall asleep in the middle of an important conversation.
*My follow-up sentence delivered the final blow, and Raziel, albeit reluctantly, got back up on her feet.*
Raziel: As important conversations drag on, I always find myself getting sleepy...
Setsuna: I would say the same could apply to me, but you are generally not the type who can read the mood, either, right?
Raziel: Oh, come now. I can always read... the mood... I read it... like a lullaby... and... let myself...
*I felt it best to whack Raziel on the head, yet she simply went on in the same, tragically spaced-out tone.*
Raziel: My book... gotta go... to the library...
Setsuna: Hm.
*It appeared she wished to reach the library. I knew the place and could have easily taken her, but she was still asleep. This was quite the conundrum.*
*I picked the only option I had.*
*Letting out a resigned sigh, I slipped my arms beneath Raziel's knees, lifting her up into my embrace.*
Raziel: Mhm...
*She had switched to full-on sleep mode, which meant I couldn't just piggyback her.*
*Still, carrying her around like I was helping an injured comrade on the battlefield would have most certainly qualified as "this is really dodgy," even by my standards.*
*With that in mind, I concluded this form to be the most appropriate, given the situation. Our appearance drew a number of gazes from fellow students, but I doubted it would cause too much of a stir.*
Belial: Pardon my thoughtless remark, but what _exactly_ are you doing, hm?
*Belial called out to us in an uncharacteristically polite tone.*
Setsuna: She told me to take her to the library.
Belial: She did...?
Setsuna: She did.
*After a few seconds of silent contemplation, Belial left, vanishing behind a corner.*
*...But not before he peeked back from beyond said corner to say one final thing.*
Belial: Take your time, you two...
*Take our time with... what? Either way, I hurried onwards to the library.*
*The sheer majesty of the place left me in awe; the way it appeared from the outside certainly did not do its interior justice.*
*A series of unnaturally tall bookshelves lined its halls, towering above us like colossal spires.*
*The Dantalions gently drifted from bookshelf to bookshelf, making certain that each volume was in its rightful place.*
*Dantalion was a demon possessing multiple personalities, all of which had now gained a body of their own here at Tokyo Babel.*
*They all turned in my direction the moment I entered the library.*
Dantalion / Male: You agai— Wait, what are you doing?
Dantalion / Female: And why is that angel asleep?
Setsuna: She told me to take her to the library.
Dantalion / Male: I see. In that case, the section she had been investigating is over there.
Setsuna: Much appreciated.
Dantalion / Female: Don't forget to put the books back once you're done.
*I took off, flying towards the direction the Dantalions had just shown me.*
Dantalion / Female: Far be it from me to criticize, but you certainly have some guts, carrying her around in a princess hold like that.
Setsuna: A princess hold?
*Was that the name of this position?*
Dantalion / Male: Oh, pay us no heed. Despite being an angel, she certainly reminds me more of Belphegor...
*Muttering under their breaths, the Dantalions promptly returned to their work.*
*Once I arrived at the designated bookshelf, I gave Raziel's cheek a light pinch.*
Raziel: Mhm... do I smell... books?
*Raziel's eyes flickered open as she sniffed the air. Indeed, the smell was unmistakably that of ancient books.*
*Not the most pleasant of scents, though.*
*However, once Raziel had fully awakened and took in her present situation, I decided not to say another word.*
Raziel: ...By the way, how come I'm in the library?
Setsuna: Well, you see, I carried you here.
Raziel: I remember the last time I asked Lilith to take me to the library when I grew too sleepy to walk. She responded with "sure thing, Raziel, but don't come crying to me if you land at the wrong place!", then kicked me into the air.
Raziel: I wondered if you had done the same this time...
Setsuna: I did not. I most certainly did not.
*I wasn't quite sure what to think of Raziel, after hearing she would prefer someone launch her into the air as opposed to giving in to sleep.*
Raziel: This position is comfortable, though.
*She latched onto my neck.*
Raziel: We should keep going like this.
Setsuna: ...Understood.
*I could have refused, yet found no reason to do so. On the other hand, I got the feeling I really should have.*
Raziel: Oh, the books come to me just by pointing at them!
Setsuna: Raziel, you are an angel, you know. Do you not at least have the strength to take out the books yourself?
*My question made her throw a confident glance my way.*
Raziel: God frowns upon idleness!
Dantalion / Male: Tendou Setsuna, you have our permission to whack her. In fact, we implore that you do.
Dantalion / Female: Witty comebacks are a fundamentally important element in Japanese communication. You needn't hold back.
Setsuna: But I think Raziel was serious.
Dantalion / Male: That makes things even worse.
*A fair point. In the end, I felt it my duty to deliver at least a light flick to her forehead.*
Raziel: Ow. Why do you resort to violence? God condemns such actions, you know!
*She wasn't being particularly persuasive, though.*
Setsuna: Either way, you should first look at yourself before talking of harmful idleness.
Raziel: ...?
*Raziel cocked her head to the side, her expression one of puzzlement. She was aware of it.*
Raziel: I wouldn't call being comfortable "harmful idleness."
*Her expression once again turned tense, eliciting two simultaneous sighs from the Dantalions.*
Raziel: Oh... they're in complete awe...
Setsuna: More like in complete shock.
*Ultimately, Raziel's position remained unchallenged, forcing me to carry her around in a princess hold during the entirety of our stay at the library.*
Lilith: ...I think I got the picture. Raziel tired herself out again and fell asleep, right?
Sorami: We worked our butts off talking to the other two candidates...
Lilith: While you two spent the day being all lovey-dovey in public.
The Two: We weren't being lovey-dovey!
*We replied in unison, which only made Lilith and Sorami glare at us with renewed contempt... for some reason.*
*Well, to be fair, I had an idea as to why.*
*Because until just recently, I was still carrying Raziel around in a princess hold. Sorami and Lilith ultimately forced us to sit on the tatami, though.*
Lilith: So... you crossed the hallways to come back here all the way from the library, right? Do you have any idea how many humans, angels, and demons bore witness to this little trip of yours, hm?
Setsuna: I do recall encountering a number of different students and teachers, now that I think about it.
Sorami: I never knew a duo of airheads could be such a force to be reckoned with, but thanks for the reminder! Y-You... big fat idiot, you!
*Sorami had been persistently raining down a number of low kicks on my back for a while now. Her technique was solid enough to put me in pain just a little bit.*
Lilith: Sorami, could you kindly give that a rest? Thanks. He's gonna be here any minute now.
The Two: "He"?
*Who could she have been talking about? I would have given that some thought, had our door not been violently flung open as Camael leapt into the room with an expression of profound fury.*
Camael: Any naughty kids around...?!
Raziel: Gyaaaaaaaaaaaa...!
*Raziel screamed at the top of her lungs as she sprang up into the air, all the while maintaining her sitting position.*
Setsuna: I cannot help but wonder: why did one of the most outstandingly belligerent angels — the commander of over twelve thousand angels of destruction — burst into our room dressed as a Namahage?
*He went so far as to don a massive Namahage mask and brandish a considerably lengthy cleaver. A fearsome entry, all things considered.*
Camael: Found ya, naughty boys and girls...!! Is it you, eh?! The two miscreants who dared disrupt law and order?!
*Lilith and Sorami both pointed at us.*
The Two: It's them.
Camael: Alright then! Get ready for one hell of a spankin', ugly ducklings!
*I had a hard time placing his accent. His voice was entirely too loud, with a murderous glint in his eyes. A fearsome look, all things considered.*
*Ultimately, Camael, the unlikely head of the Public Morals Committee forced us to sit through several hours of his lecturing.*
Camael: Blah-blah-blah! Blah-dee-blargh! Blargggh!
Raziel: All I hear are blarghs...
Camael: Blaaaargh?!
*I hastily covered Raziel's mouth with my palm as Camael eyeballed us with a curious gaze.*
Setsuna: She misspoke. By all means, please continue.
*I threw a bitter look at Lilith and Sorami, both of whom were sitting at the dining table. The moment our eyes met, they turned the other way in a sulky huff.*
*They still appeared to be furious over the fact that I carried Raziel around in a princess hold.*
*Oh. Wait a second.*
*In other words, if I carried them off in a princess hold as well, this entire issue could be resolved.*
*Urged by that conclusion, I began to stand up, only to be met with a dual strike of teacups right into my face.*
Camael: Huh?! What's gotten into you two all of a sudden?!
Lilith: Oh, nothing much. That buffoon over there was plotting to do something extremely rude to us is all.
Sorami: What she said.
Raziel: ...?
*Another sort of pain assailed me then, one different from what the teacups had inflicted upon me. Still massaging my cheeks from that attack, I looked to the side to discover a pouting Raziel pinching me in the side.*
Camael: I've no idea what's going on here... but you have my heartfelt sympathies.
*I ended up earning Camael's sympathy, of all people.*
Camael: Anyway, I'm done lecturing you guys, so let's move on to the other matter at hand.
*Camael removed his mask, once again becoming the angel we all knew.*
*Raziel and I exhaled a sigh of relief as both of us were given permission to stop sitting in one place.*
Raziel: ...! ...!
*Raziel collapsed onto the floor, her legs having gone entirely too numb. For the record, I had no such problems.*
Raziel: H-How come you're fine...?
*I turned towards the astonished Raziel, explaining that I had been able to avoid the same fate as her by forcing my veins to pump blood into my legs.*
*It was all made possible through the power of nanomachines. As I declared that, Raziel glared at me with a gaze that could kill.*
Raziel: That's... so unfair...
Setsuna: I am surprised this is giving you, an angel, so much difficulty.
Raziel: You...
Setsuna: All right... I shall give you a hand.
*I promptly grabbed hold of Raziel's thumb, then pulled on it with all my strength, ignoring the creaking noises it made.*
*It didn't take long until her blood flow returned to normal. Raziel moved her legs around a bit, looking at them in sheer amazement.*
Raziel: They're healed.
Setsuna: Glad to hear that.
Raziel: I'm still a bit mad, but... thanks.
*I uttered a quick "you are welcome" in response, then turned my attention back to Camael.*
Camael: May I, uh, continue now?
*There was a certain timidity in his tone I couldn't quite explain. Either way, I did want him to continue.*
Camael: Your request has been evaluated. I hereby grant you permission to begin your pilgrimage and head towards the second stratum of Akihabara.
*The moment the words left Camael's lips, a palpable wave of tension washed across the room.*
Lilith: Cool!
*On the other hand, it may have just been my imagination, as Lilith jumped forward with her fist casually thrust into the air.*
Camael: I've read your report. Abdiel ought to be somewhere between the second and fourth strata... is that correct?
Lilith: Hm... well, yeah. Probably. On the other hand, we can't rule out the possibility of the masters killing each other off, either.
*Nonetheless, we would need to operate with the assumption that Abdiel was alive, just to be on the safe side.*
Camael: So we're up against Abdiel...
*Camael wore a mask of contempt mingling with nostalgia as he uttered the words.*
Setsuna: Do you resent him?
*Camael considered my question for a moment, his face contorting into a stern frown.*
Camael: I can't say for certain. That man was... how do I put... difficult to understand.
Lilith: Well, I'm not surprised a jock angel like you wouldn't find common ground with him...
Camael: He didn't even get along with the intellectuals!
Sorami: Wait, the angels had jocks and intellectuals...?
*This new piece of information left Sorami utterly perplexed.*
Lilith: By the way... does Abdiel have any trademark weapons or stuff?
Camael: Hm? Let me think. As far as I know, he became a mere foot soldier after leaving Lucifer's army, with only a shield and a longsword at his side.
Lilith: And during his rebellion?
Camael: Good question... You'll have to forgive me, but I didn't directly partake in the battle. Based on what I heard, though, he didn't appear to wield any blades of high renown.
*He could have wielded a nameless weapon, but we had no way of knowing its power.*
Lilith: Hm... honestly, that makes me even more uneasy. I prefer things to be straightforward, like with the Laevateinn.
Camael: Keeping the nature of one's weapon a secret from friend and foe alike is the ironclad rule of a soldier's life. A commander would be another story, though.
*That made sense.*
*A commander would need to wield a famed holy blade, lest he cease to be a commander.*
*Yet for Abdiel, who fought at the front lines, revealing his weapon's true nature would only spell his doom.*
Camael: Wouldn't his former comrades know something?
Lilith: Lucifer's best men headed out of Tokyo Babel to search for him... and then they up and vanished.
Camael: Right, that did happen...
*Camael's shoulders slumped forward.*
Lilith: As for his raison d'etre... we're pretty much in the dark, I guess.
Camael: A traitor's reason for being is hardly what I could ever hope to understand. Traitor or not, Abdiel was not one to be comprehended easily.
Lilith: Thanks, anyway. Guess we'll be leaving in about two days.
Camael: Very well. And try not to end up as masters yourselves, all right?
Lilith: Hear that? An angel's rooting for me! Oh, just you wait, we'll be singing Kumbaya together in no time!
*Camael shook his head, meeting Lilith's enthusiasm with a brief "enough with your jokes."*
Camael: No, I mean, I'd rather avoid seeing you succumb to madness like that. This doesn't have anything to do with strength, though. The very thought just sends a shiver down my spine.
Raziel: I am in complete agreement. On both accounts.
Sorami: I dunno what he meant, but I agree, too...
Setsuna: No comment.
Lilith: ......
*Lilith gave each of us a knock on the head.*
Setsuna: Why did you include me?
Lilith: Ever heard of collective responsibility? Well, that's why. Besides, a "no comment" is basically like staying silent because it's obvious you agree with the rest!
*I couldn't exactly deny that I had something along those lines in mind.*
*Lilith also let us know that they would only be observers, neither stopping, nor aiding Sorami on her pilgrimage.*
*I let out a sigh.*
*Her life was in my hands — hands that once failed to protect ten billion lives.*
*Yet what astonished me even more was Sorami's response.*
Sorami: Oh, okay. Guess that's that, then! Let's do our best!
*The discussion ended before it even had a chance to start.*
*Her declaration left Lilith and Raziel dumbfounded, both of whom went on to repeatedly remind her of the journey's dangers.*
Lilith: So if Setsuna falls, you'll likely end up dying yourself.
Sorami: C'mon, Lilith. That's the third time you're telling me that. I get it, okay?

??? / Uriel: ......

Setsuna: You must flee! There should be time until the next shot!

Raziel: No...! I won't, I won't... I won't!

Setsuna: N-Not yet...!
*Blood rushed up my throat but I gulped it back down. I struggled to my feet — my ankles still in ruin — while enduring unimaginable pain.*
*Unable to maintain my balance, I collapsed back onto my knees.*

*God.*
*Through mankind's desires, I once bore that name. But no longer.*
*I stood here today as a mortal man; as weapon, machine, and slave.*
*My mission was to protect Lilith, Sorami, and Raziel — a duty I carried out as best I could.*
*But now... it was no longer within my capabilities.*
*Uriel's strike had put me on the verge of death, and I would be struck down by a blow truly befitting one of the four master angels.*
*My heart would soon beat its last. My mind had comprehended its impending demise.*
*A reason for being.*
*I once thought that accomplishing my mission, or keeping my companions safe would stand as my raison d'etre.*

*Uriel was a veritable monster. A fatal deficiency in my own analytical capabilities prevented me from conjuring up armaments that could surpass his strength, or protective equipment that might withstand his fury.*
*There existed several requirements before I could truly become invincible.*
*Requirements I had yet to fulfill.*
*And the one thing that could serve me best in this situation were legs that would carry me beyond space and time.*

*All I had to do was apprehend the dimensional theory, and construct a mechanism that could function within its framework. Everything I required was right here. If not, I simply had to force it into existence.*
Setsuna: Dimensional...

*In order to live. To survive. To protect.*
Setsuna: Dimensional leap... Hermes!
*Space itself had been distorted, a number of thin cracks running along reality, light seeping in through their slits. I chose one and grabbed Raziel by the arm.*
Uriel: What...?!
Raziel: Setsuna!

Lilith: Setsuna!

Uriel: Come back here, you bastard...!!
*Screaming various obscenities our way, Uriel leapt inside the tear in pursuit... but that was as far as he could go.*
Uriel: Wh-What...?!
*This place was merely a narrow rift existing within the crevice of reality.*
*Its very existence crawled and coiled in the form of a shapeless slime, lacking an earth and a sky, its coordinates fickle at best.*
*Without a focused mind, it became difficult to tell whether one was even advancing or retreating through this realm.*
