Uriel: Raziel needs to die! She must perish while still being ignorant to the truth! Why can't you understand?
Setsuna: If you think I'm going to understand, keep on dreaming.
*Uriel had cast aside his rationality and became a master.*
*The manifestation of that very same rationality said something similar. That Raziel sheltered a certain secret. A cruel, terrifying secret.*
*Yet Raziel herself was ready to face it. No matter how cruel the truth could prove to be, they were nonetheless all part of her treasured memories.*
*At the very least, her life was most definitely not in Uriel's hands, even if he was the manifestation of God's divine flame and one of the four master angels.*
Uriel: Mark my words: Raziel will die by my hands!
Setsuna: Not until I'm here to be her shield.
*Our objectives were polar opposites. Clashing in battle would be the only way to settle this.*
*I had no weapons to wield, though even if I did, I would not rely on them.*
*Similarly, the arcane arts were at my disposal, yet a fledgling magic-user like me could never hope to match the prowess of the so-called Flame of God.*
*Be it physical strength, stamina, speed, cunning, or willpower, an angel like him far surpassed me.*
*My situation felt beyond hopeless, with only terror and despair to await me.*
*And yet—*
Setsuna: ...!
*As I considered my options in vain, Uriel mounted an attack.*
Uriel: To my side, Gluttony!
*The beast came lunging at me through the power of the Peccati Sword, crudely baring its fangs like it always did.*
Setsuna: That won't stop me...!
*I leapt straight into the abomination's colossal jaw, piercing through its neck to exit through the back of its head before it could crush me with its rows of massive teeth.*
Uriel: ...!
*Uriel was right in front of me.*
Setsuna: Ahhhhhhhhhhhhhh...!!
*Howling at the top of my lungs, I let my fist crash clean into the angel's face. Although my strike did make him recoil ever so slightly, Uriel smiled — things were apparently going his way.*
Uriel: Come forth, Golden Sloth!
*A moment later, I saw my arm enveloped by a mass of molten gold...*
*...summoned with the kind of inhuman swiftness that left little to no room or time for any sort of counter-plan.*
*And while the amount he summoned was by no means enough to cover my whole body, the speed of Uriel's incantation was most certainly terrifying.*
*So this was the way to utilize this particular beast...*
Setsuna: Kh...!
*As the sharp hiss of sizzling gold echoed in the vicinity, I felt myself assailed by pain of unbelievable intensity. My immediate reaction was to reach out with my right hand and tear off my left arm by the elbow.*
*The shock I experienced upon losing an arm remained miniscule at best.*
Uriel: Hahahaha! Ehehehehe!
*Uriel howled with laughter, his expression the very epitome of complete madness, devoid of even the faintest trace of rationality.*
*What next?*
*The question was painfully simple, yet finding an answer to it would prove a difficult task. My situation here was in no way comparable to what I had gone through with Abdiel or Gethel.*
*A raging blizzard to freeze everything solid? Or a thunderstorm to blow away the flames and everything else along with them? Or perhaps an earthquake that would swallow the entire district whole?*
*I soon abandoned all three options, realizing they would likely end in failure.*
*If one were to measure the amount of magic each of us commanded, the answer would be clear as day.*
*If my magical capacity was a hundred, Uriel's approached eighty thousand. Not eight hundred — eighty _thousand_.*
Uriel: Divine punishment! St. Elmo's fire!
*Sharp pain shot through my body as the whip of fire summoned by Uriel bit into my flesh.*
Setsuna: Gh...!
*With my eyes wide open and mind completely paralyzed by pain, I forgot to even breathe for a moment.*
Uriel: No one withstood a hundred lashes from this whip and lived to tell the tale! Tell me, Setsuna... how long do you think you'll last?
*No ordinary man could endure this level of crippling, otherworldly pain.*
Setsuna: Ah... gh...!
Uriel: All right... will you do me a favor and stand down, Tendou Setsuna?
*Uriel's words rang in a tone soft and soothing, yet unmistakably belonging to a madman. In the far distance, I could see Raziel lying on the ground.*
Setsuna: Not as long as I live...
Uriel: Ah, right, now I remember. You won't give up unless I end your miserable life. I'm real sorry, okay? I tend to be forgetful, you see!
*Another lash from the flaming whip tore into my chest.*
Uriel: I'm so sorry! So eternally sorry! No, I mean it! I'm seriously feeling bad right now!
*The whip continued its terrible work without a moment's rest, ravaging my entire body.*
*My chest, shoulders, abdomen, legs, neck, and face all felt the scorching pain as the attacks rained down on me without mercy.*
*I would not even be granted the small mercy of blacking out — the pain, in its inhuman intensity, would jolt my consciousness awake.*
*I had heard of the unimaginable heights of pain a whipping could inflict on a person. That was especially true in the case of a punishment meted out by a master angel.*
Uriel: This is punishment! Divine punishment against a wretched sinner! Punishment! Punishment! Punishment!
*As Uriel continued his work in a lunatic frenzy, his expression contorted to a complex blend of fear and ecstasy.*
*However, he seemed entirely too preoccupied with punishing me, to the point of losing himself in a trance of sorts.*
*Even in the hands of a mortal, his whip was said to be swift enough to transcend the speed of sound. As it came crashing down on my body, I successfully read its movements and grabbed the end of it with my left hand.*
Uriel: Let... go... of.. my... whip!
*Uriel howled like a spoiled child. The fiery whip scorched my skin as the stench of burning flesh filled my nostrils.*
Setsuna: Gh... ahhhhhhhhhhhhh...!!
*Mustering all my strength, I pulled the whip my way, then charged at the now-unbalanced Uriel.*
*Using the same momentum, I smashed my head clean into his face.*
Uriel: Gah...!
*The impact was powerful enough to make me see stars for a few seconds. With my left hand clutching the whip and my right torn clean off, the only weapons left to me were my legs and head.*
*I stretched out my neck... and struck again!*
Uriel: You... you miserable impostor...!!
*The whip coiled about my arm, ready to tear it off.*
Uriel: I know all about you! You wear the skin of man, yet sought to transcend humanity!
*Uriel's whip rapidly grew in length, smashing me into the asphalt road and the nearby buildings over and over again.*
*As my consciousness drifted farther away, the pain would drag me back into reality, tormenting me with its relentless assault. The fact my left arm was still in place felt like a miracle in itself.*
*Possibly realizing that I no longer resisted, Uriel banished his whip and took to the skies.*
*His wings clad in azure fire glimmered in vivid hues, birthing a scene straight out of a delirious daydream.*
Uriel: Behold, ladies and gentlemen! I shall now carry out divine punishment! May his death be exquisite in its blood-curdling grimness!
Uriel: Tendou Setsuna! Yaldabaoth, the False God! I will pulverize your very soul and grind it to dust!
*I could not defeat him.*
*The realization came swift and sure. I looked upon the skies and saw it blotted out by the shape of Uriel, the maddened angel.*
*All I could do was writhe in agony. Robbed of all weapons and an arm, my mind teetered on the brink of collapse, my strength all but spent.*
*Uriel was unbelievably powerful — that simple fact had finally begun to sink in.*
Uriel: Come forth, beasts of the seven deadly sins!
*The beast of Gluttony. The molten gold of Sloth. The azure flames of Wrath.*
*The decayed chains of Envy. The silver lion of Pride. The mirror knight of Lust.*
*And finally... The chimera of Greed.*
Uriel: I'll first kill you. Then Raziel. Afterwards... the whole world will burn! The Sefer Raziel, the entirety of Pandora, all will succumb to divine fire!
*All seven beasts embodying the deadly sins came lunging at me at the same time, displaying power far surpassing what Gethel or I could each call forth. Uriel's magical capacity was simply that vast and expansive.*
*His next attack would end my life, no question about it. The pain gradually subsided as a sudden feeling of drowsiness washed over me.*
*My senses slowly but surely ceased to function, my heart and soul yielding to that ceaseless chorus. I felt myself at the jaws of death, both mentally and physically.*
*I would die. Perish. Cease to be. At the same time, however, death would bring release from suffering.*
*That obvious truth lingered in my mind. It had worn me down. The battles, the struggle to protect others... life itself had worn me down.*
*Why not shed that burden? Time and again I felt myself ready to yield to that temptation. This time, I would certainly make that step.*
*But what exactly made me weather that storm? Why did I continue to cling so desperately to life?*
*I was a sinner, the contempt of billions soaked deep into my very soul. So why would I need to keep living?*
Setsuna: (I... I see!)
*The realization came as a bolt of blinding light. _So that was the reason_.*
*I was a sinner, a wretched criminal who should have been denied life.*
*Yet still I lived. My veins pumped blood. My lungs drank air, aching for oxygen. I wielded steel, my howl echoed in the skies as I fought to destroy my foes.*
*This was not yet the end. Far from it.*
*As the seven beasts of each deadly sin closed in on me, I took to introspection, leveling a myriad questions at myself.*
*Who was I? Tendou Setsuna. A mortal man. And before that? Someone who aspired to be God. Could I emerge victorious here? I needed to.*
*See through to his core. Uriel once howled the following words...*
Uriel: My name proclaims my raison d'etre! In short... I live as the Flame of God!
*The fires of God, born from a volcano said to be located at Tartarus.*
*His duty was to judge its sinners, to mete out punishment with unfaltering composure and cruelty.*
*To him, that duty meant the world. Its composure, its cruelty... his divine fury.*
*Unbridled rage, burning brighter than a firestorm. He would toy with and scorn all men indiscriminately, the core of his very essence remaining unchanged.*
*Which is precisely why he could so overwhelmingly surpass me in sheer prowess. The gravity of my sins only served to fuel his strength.*
*In my foolishness, I caused the deaths of ten billion people. Uriel had no doubt come to judge a far greater number of souls during his existence. In his eyes, I was a sinner, clear and simple.*
*I would not prevail. No matter how fiercely I struggled. Uriel's raison d'etre was that strong, that clearly articulated.*
*Could I display a raison d'etre to surpass his?*
*My fate had been set in stone since birth. And even after that, I had simply been like a reed in the wind.*
*When I fought to protect others, I did so because I had been ordered to. That was how I viewed it. I knew that now — all too well.*
*I needed to calmly recall the first time Uriel and I met in battle.*
*When my very life was on the line.*
*The pulse of my heart echoed in my chest, its every beat proof that I was alive.*
*Its rhythm signifying my will to live.*
*Live, survive, prevail, protect, endure, struggle, think, see, hear, touch, and smell—*
*Life, in its unmatched complexity, required a myriad of actions to be maintained.*
*And so, I — and countless other people — would nurture a wish in our hearts. A desire to see someone capable of overthrowing all adversity.*
*Someone to face the jaws of despair and emerge victorious. Someone to turn the cruel tides of fate.*
*Despite knowing no such being existed and realizing we yearned for the impossible... still we desired to see that wish fulfilled.*
*At times, it manifested itself through the might of God. Unfortunately, no such creator existed here.*
*Even if it did, God would be an enemy to us — after all, here I was, taking up arms against one of the Lord's angels.*
*_There is no God_. No messiah to save us.*
*The words rang almost as if spoken by someone from my home world.*
*Ten billion rejected the existence of God, yet found themselves yearning for His salvation. They wished for someone to save them. Someone to help them.*
*Like a valiant hero. A protector of all that is right and just. _A conveniently omnipotent God_.*
*Indeed. I was created for that purpose. To save ten billion lives edging towards the precipice of despair.*
*My raison d'etre. Had it been simply to act as ordered? To carry out what was desired of me? Was that my reason for being?*
*No.*
*I committed a sin. I felt guilt welling up in my chest. I believed I had no right to live.*
*And yet... I met an angel who willingly took my hand. An angel who, despite her occasional coldness, nurtured a loving heart.*
*An angel who felt at peace as she held my hand. _It was all for her sake_.*
*If I perished here, Uriel would swiftly kill Raziel just the same.*
*To prevent that cruel fate—*
*I needed to survive, no matter what. Survive... and prevail.*
*What exactly did I require in order to accomplish that?*
*To prevail. To emerge victorious. To reign as the sole victor.*
*Visualize what you need for victory. Draw up a conclusion. Bring it forth from the depth of your mind in less than a second.*
*What I needed... what I truly needed...*
*...was to first rise on my own two feet.*
Setsuna: ...!
*Grasping the asphalt with my left hand, I pulled myself erect once more. After picking out Gluttony — the largest of the seven beasts — I grabbed the abomination by the nose...*
*...and sent it flying.*
Uriel: Wh—?!
*The other six ended up being mowed down by Gluttony's colossal body.*
*I had finally managed to gain a momentary advantage — I would not let it slip through my fingers.*
*I picked up the right arm I had lost, clumsily — yet with great force — reattaching it, without even bothering to sedate myself.*
*I would endure all my pain. Once my arm had been fully rejuvenated, I held it up before my eyes.*
*Tendou Setsuna. Proclaim your reason for being — _let the world tremble at the echo of your raison d'etre_.*
Setsuna: The world turns through the cogs of an intricate mechanism.
*I first needed to utter the words.*
*My raison d'etre would clash with the world, invading it, permeating it — each syllable like a poem chanted. And in the end, I would summon _the exact being I needed_.*
Setsuna: There is no God. I shall not revere Him. I shall not pray to Him. I shall not believe in Him. I shall not crave His blessing.
*Next, I needed to make my proclamation, mustering the willpower to declare my mind liberated and detached from God's dominion.*
Uriel: What in the...?
*I felt the whole of my body brimming with magic, forces once elusive now flowing freely at my command.*
*My magical capacity was a mere hundred. Uriel's a vast eighty thousand.*
Setsuna: And yet... men need a God to believe in. They need someone to revere. They need someone to save them! And so I...!
Uriel: S-Stop it! Enough! I'm begging you... stop, whatever this is! I'll end you! I'll end you right this instant!
*He brandished his steel, but it was far too late.*
*_I shall create God_. To give birth to something powerful enough to turn the tide in the face of overwhelming odds...*
Setsuna: In order to suppress all adversity through devastating power...
Setsuna: I shall create God. I shall mold Him into being. That is my raison d'etre — Tendou Setsuna's reason for being!
Setsuna: I summon you, Universal Machine, Guardian Spirit of Time!
*With all the magic I could muster at my disposal, I opened the gates. And in that moment, the world itself came to a halt.*
Uriel: ......
*Even the maddened Uriel found himself at a loss for words when faced with a proclamation that no sane man would dare utter in the presence of the Flame of God.*
*The angel clenched his teeth in rage, instinct ordering him to meet my words with righteous fury.*
Uriel: Kn—
*"Know your place, mortal, else I'll put you out of your misery." I could not tell for certain if Uriel meant to utter such threats. Nor did I care, for that matter.*
Setsuna: The time has come.
All beheld the descent of the ultimate machine: a kingdom of amalgamated metal and steel.
*A soaring bastion of an island, its terrible shape blotting out the heavens above, a myriad pieces of scrap metal forming its ramparts, walls, and cogwheels.*
*Its realm gave home to no living beings — only I stood in the middle, a messenger to that colossal leviathan of steel.*
*For I stood here to proclaim my own desires, my own ambitions.*
*Its engines whirred to life, their booming roar celebrating the advent of the machine kingdom.*
Setsuna: Your name is Uriel, a manifestation of divine retribution; an angel of light with a duty to punish the wicked.
*The construction of the ultimate machine had come to its end, the birth of a weapon needed to crush Uriel now complete and finished.*
*A divine instrument. An arcane vessel. A sacred treasure.*
*Or something even more supreme — something that transcended our meager imagination.*
Setsuna: Hark, sinner! For we stand present to condemn thee!
Uriel: Wh—?
*The word "sinner" made Uriel recoil. To have himself — an angel bereft of sin — be condemned as such was unimaginable.*
*Hearing the words from the lips of a mere mortal must have only added insult to injury. Yet I went on regardless.*
Setsuna: Thou hast sinned when madness tainted thy heart.
Setsuna: Thou hast sinned when its poison crippled thy mind.
Setsuna: We condemn thy frailty, O brittle, ravaged soul!
*The kingdom of metal responded to my words.*
*Condemn him! Let the trial begin like in days of old, when witches and werewolves alike burned at the stake!*
*Hear the death throes of the supernatural! The complete rejection of the arcane!*
*The kingdom's blacksmiths all set to work, creating weapons and armor.*
Setsuna: Gavel of Judgement and Retribution!
*I may have called it a gavel, yet in reality, the handle itself was ten meters long, its tip boasting an otherworldly shape akin to a colossus' foot.*
Setsuna: Ha...!
*One terrible swing sent the seven beasts back to the void they emerged from.*
*Power befitting a sacred treasure, a divine instrument and _something unique, freshly-created_. A weapon birthed for the sole purpose of defeating Uriel.*
Setsuna: Uriel. I find you a miserable creature worthy of pity. I may even believe your actions to have been inevitable.
Uriel: How dare—
Setsuna: However. Or should I say, _precisely because of that_... you must perish here. Embrace your sins and know oblivion!
*Uriel once again summoned his tremendous door bolt forged of steel.*
Uriel: Sheol of Tartarus!
*Uriel lunged forward, his body clad in divine fire.*
*Our battle had begun anew.*
*Uriel and I spiralled downwards, piercing through the clouds during our descent.*
Uriel: How dare a mere human judge _me_, an angel! Know your place, reprobate!
*My steel met his weapon with a thunderous roar of an impact, birthing a multitude of sparks dancing in the vivid crimson of a meteor shower.*
Setsuna: I shall judge you! Condemn you! As long as you are an angel... as long as you dare hurt her!
*I screamed back at him, allowing myself to believe I could overturn the impossible, no matter what shape it might take.*
*No, I was not merely convincing myself.*
*My raison d'etre did make that very thing possible, elevating me to monstrous heights in order to trample over even the most overwhelming of odds.*
*I would become the monster they call omnipotence.*
*Uriel's bolt clashed with the colossal gavel in a violent impact.*
*This battle was no longer a competition of raw strength; instead, it evolved into something akin to a sword duel.*
Setsuna: Shhhyaaaaa...!!
Uriel: Ryhaaaaa....!!
*My war cry filled me with confidence, further amplifying the speed of every action I took. We exchanged blows again and again in the air, biting into each other in an awesome display of inhuman prowess and skill.*
*Building after building fell victim to the violent shockwaves of our ongoing struggle. Uriel's bolt and my hammer stirred a series of gales ferocious enough to devastate the cityscape — any ordinary human caught in the blast would have perished in a heartbeat.*
Setsuna: In that case...!
*I swung the gavel in a wide arc — like a golfer would his stick — propelling a mixture of rubble and dust into the air.*
*Uriel had lost sight of me.*
Uriel: Where are you...?!
*Uriel looked in both directions, then naturally lowered his gaze to glance below. After all, that was where I had been moments before.*
*However, I approached Uriel from above, hiding behind a veil of dust and debris.*
*Using this to my advantage, I lunged at him from an elevated position.*
Uriel: Found y—
*Just as Uriel was about to prepare a counter-attack after spotting me, my colossal gavel smashed into his head.*
*The impact sent the angel — once dominating the skies like a bright star — spiralling downwards in a blaze of fire, almost like a meteor.*
Uriel: You son of a bitch...!!
*Uriel climbed out from beneath a heap of rubble, looking back up at me with an expression twisted by unbridled rage. I remained in the sky while he stood on the ground.*
*That situation in itself made the angel positively livid.*
Uriel: Don't look down at me! Don't stare down at me from above! I am the iron fist of judgement! My place is among the clouds!
*In terms of sheer skill, Uriel did indeed surpass Tendou Setsuna, overwhelmingly so.*
*However, that advantage did not last long. Uriel, too, had finally realized it.*
*The angel leapt back into the skies.*
Uriel: RRRRRRrrrraaaaaaaaaaaa...!!
We each swung of our respective weapons: bolt and gavel met in the middle, their clash booming like thunder, sending violent shockwaves in the air.
*We both staked our very souls in this battle, neither of us willing to yield as we continued to exchange blow after blow.*
*Uriel was an angel. I was a mortal man.*
*He was eternal and unaging, robbed of the very concept of growth.*
*I was neither immortal, nor unaging. If anything, my life span was far shorter than any ordinary man's.*
*Which is why... to me, the concept of growth was a power terrifying enough to move the world.*
*A single strike. Uriel's eyes shot open in surprise; the angel could barely believe what he was witnessing.*
*I was growing, adapting before his very eyes. With each attack I received, each counterattack I launched, and with every single occasion where I escaped death by a hair's breadth, I continued to grow.*
*I began to understand Uriel's strategy and combat techniques. However, my body could not withstand the burden of it.*
*The moment that thought crossed my mind— I felt the density of muscles grow.*
*My raison d'etre was to overthrow the impossible, to turn the tide against overwhelming odds. And if I happened to lack the power to do that—*
*I would be granted said power, even by force. My already brief life span would be eroded even further in the process, yet my mind focused not on a distant tomorrow, but the here and now.*
*I sent my hammer in a horizontal arc, utilizing momentum to swing it in a full circle and finally crash it into Uriel's liver.*
Uriel: Wh-Why...?
*Uriel's frenzy grew ever fiercer with every passing second. The sight unfolding before him was out of this world; he could hardly believe his eyes.*
*At first, he could easily overpower me. But gradually, I managed to fight him on equal footing. And now... I was beginning to turn the tables.*
*I lacked the angel's volcanic fury. All I had was a will cold as steel, intent on crushing this obstacle.*
*The polar opposite of love. After successfully figuring out what Uriel did not wish to befall him, I acted without hesitation to carry out that very thing.*
*I swung my tremendous hammer, aiming for his jaw and the wings that once were the pride of the angels.*
Uriel: Gh...!
*I missed his wings, but his jaw was slightly slower — my weapon grazed it. His gaze grew hollow for a moment, his body slightly wavering.*
*I would crush him without missing my mark...!*
Uriel: Oracula Sibyllina!
*As the massive door bolt in his grip split to numerous fragments in a second... I lost sight of Uriel.*
Setsuna: ...?!
*I could no longer predict where he would lunge from.*
Uriel: To the depths of Hell with you!
*Before I could react, Uriel appeared behind me.*
*Using his fiery wings like a jet thruster, Uriel moved in a straight, horizontal line to rapidly make his way behind me.*
*He moved faster than I could turn around to face him, my mind struggling to register what had just happened.*
*Uriel sent me flying with a ferocious kick with each fragment of his door bolt hot on my heels like a swarm of missiles.*
*I could neither dodge, nor survive their attack by amplifying my defenses. One moment of hesitation would spell my doom.*
*In other words... I needed to launch an attack of my own.*
*I analyzed the missiles' trajectory and calculated their speed.*
*I made a myriad calculations regarding distance, the time and direction of impact, and numerous other factors.*
*I drew up a conclusion, determining whether or not this was the correct course of action.*
*I acted with impeccable timing...*
*...and knocked back a fragment!*
*The fragment I knocked back diverged from its course, hitting another one and causing a chain reaction.*
*If my calculations proved correct, I did not even need to move. If I did, I would only be putting myself in unnecessary danger.*
*The fragments, like a collage of volcanic projectiles, soared past me in the blink of an eye.*
*I turned to face Uriel. The angel watched in silent astonishment as his projectiles plummeted to the ground below.*
Uriel: How...?
*How did you do that?*
*I held up my gavel, ignoring his question.*
*I would be aiming for his right hand — constantly clad in flames, this part of Uriel's body was a vulnerability surpassing even his heart.*
Setsuna: Fire, water, earth, and air. In the name of the feathered serpent, I chasten thee!
*In order to defeat Uriel, I called upon the name of another world's god, each word brimming with sorcery that further amplified the speed of my swings.*
*Go on, Tendou Setsuna. Let the world quake in terror at the coming of your steel!*
*The hammer struck, blasting Uriel's right arm clean off.*
Uriel: Ah...?
*Uriel's wings flapped powerlessly, finally buckling under the pressure, sending the angel plummeting downward.*
*Wasting no time, I chased after him in pursuit. Uriel crashed into a rooftop water tank, drenching his whole body.*
*The angel found himself robbed of a body part more vital than his heart — his right arm.*
Uriel: What...? I... I lost...?
*Uriel's tone reflected not a shred of despair. Instead, he spoke up in a meek tone, his expression that of confusion.*
*I stepped up to the angel, supplying him with the answer.*
Setsuna: Exactly. You can no longer stand. Your defeat is clear.
Uriel: I can't stand... so I lost?
*It took a few moments for the realization to finally sink in. When it did, Uriel responded with a faint smile.*
*I went on in a solemn tone.*
Setsuna: The time has come for you to be liberated, Uriel. The flames you ignited will soon be extinguished. Word of your deeds will never reach God.
*For a short while, Uriel stared blankly at his missing right arm before finally speaking up in a melancholic tone.*
Uriel: Ah... I see it now. I had long since perished, haven't I?
Setsuna: Perhaps.
*Uriel leveled his gaze with mine, the fire of contempt burning unmistakably in his eyes.*
Uriel: Why do you continue to protect Raziel?
Setsuna: Because...
*Not out of duty. And certainly not because I had been ordered to.*
*I merely wished — from the bottom of my heart — to protect her, to keep her safe. The angel who, in order to help mankind, once handed them a book she valued more than her own life.*
*Yet I couldn't quite put that into words. Uriel chuckled to himself.*
Uriel: I was quite fond of her myself. But the fact remains that she sinned. And sins must be punished.
Setsuna: She sinned?
Uriel: The reason I ended up like this was only partly because of the chorus. That book was also to blame.
Setsuna: The Sefer Raziel...
*Uriel let out another chuckle, his expression — quite fittingly — that of a young boy fond of pranks.*
Uriel: But I won't tell you what's written in it.
*The angel's body began to wither away — in his current state, he was like a mortal with his heart stabbed...*
*...indescribable despair and anguish his only companions.*
Uriel: Tendou Setsuna. I do hold you in contempt, yet I must also express my gratitude.
Setsuna: Your gratitude? Why?
Uriel: No longer shall my past deeds haunt me in eternal death. Make no mistake: I dread whatever it is that awaits me. I do feel suffocated by that fear soaking into my very soul.
Uriel: But the fact remains... that I have been liberated. And for that, I owe you gratitude.
Setsuna: Uriel. What in the world happened in Heaven?
*He sluggishly shook his head, his prior smile returning.*
Uriel: Have I not been clear? I despise you, who claimed my life. As such, _you won't learn a thing from me_.
Setsuna: Stubborn till the very end, I see...
Uriel: Oh, I am. You may recall that I used to be an angel punishing the wicked. This is my punishment for you.
Setsuna: I see. Not much I can do about it, then.
Uriel: Yup. Just accept it.
*The angel smiled with a child's innocence, his body withering rapidly, soon to be nothing but dust and ash. His soul, too, will cease to be for good.*
*Uriel began muttering to himself.*
Uriel: I see. I see! It's all very clear now. So this is the concept of "death" unique to mankind. It truly is... terrifying. Terrifying beyond belief.
Setsuna: ......
Uriel: At the same time, it fascinates me to no end. To completely vanish and expire... not once have I experienced such a thing.
*Uriel glanced up at the drifting clouds above, his expression rather that of calm acceptance than of dread. A few moments later, his gaze lit up with realization.*
Uriel: Ah, I see... no one truly wished to die, did they...
*After a lifetime of passing down judgment on a myriad different mortals, Uriel had finally come to realize that simple, enduring truth.*
*The angel closed his eyes. His body began to fade.*
*I was more than ready to kill or be killed in this battle. It goes without saying that I should have anticipated an outcome like this.*

*I couldn't tell whether she was trying to revive the angels or simply put a stop to the mechanism that bound them in place.*
*I had no choice but to have faith in Raziel.*
*However, I knew next to nothing about her.*
*The thought gripped my heart for a brief second. No, that was not true. I knew her well.*
*I shot down the suggestion of my own inner voice, forcefully suppressing the surge of anxiety and doubt welling within my heart as I launched into a discussion of sorts.*
Answer the following, then: why did Uriel wish to see her dead at all costs?
*What secrets lurked in her lost memories?*
*And what was written in the Sefer Raziel's Book of Heavens?*
*I could answer none of those questions.*
Memories were just that: memories. Hear me, my lost memories. Heed my call and answer my prayers.
*What exactly have I done?*
*"Raziel. Raziel."*
*I heard a gentle voice calling out to me.*
*What business could they have with me, who wandered heaven and earth alike in search of a book?*
*I found your book.*
*Was that true? If so, why had it eluded me until now?*
*Your book was in the possession of the dead souls of Hell.*
*Lies. All lies. I don't believe it!*
*Only the purest and most virtuous of mortals were allowed to lay their hands on my book. I know not who you are, but show yourself.*
*Responding to my plea, she abruptly peeked out from a separate dimension, riding her basilisk as usual.*
Samael: Long time no see, Raziel. Still looking for that book of yours?
Raziel: The angel of venom and death, Samael... You certainly have some nerve to talk to me here, being the exiled turncloak that you are.
*Noticing my alarm, Samael threw her arms up.*
Samael: Look, I surrender! I'm not here to fight you. Tell me, Raziel, does that book of yours contain all your knowledge?
Raziel: Yes, but what of it?
Samael: _And did you include knowledge you yourself lacked?_
Raziel: ......
*I fell silent.*
*True to my name, "the secrets of God," I included all the divine secrets privy only to the Lord when penning that book.*
*However, only I could understand its encryption. As for the keywords required to unravel it... I forcefully erased them from my memories.*
*I couldn't tell what made me do that back then, but looking back on it now, I believed I had done the right thing.*
*To record. That was my raison d'etre. My reason for being. A power fierce enough to encroach upon reality.*
*To think there existed a taboo even I wished to seal away...*
Samael: Ah, so you did write it down.
Raziel: ......
*Keeping silent was a foolish choice, yet I had no option but to hold my tongue.*
Samael: Don't you want your book back?
Raziel: I do. And I want you to hand it over.
Samael: Sorry to burst your bubble, but I don't have it. I just told you, remember? It's fallen to the depths of Hell.
Raziel: Then—
*I barely stopped myself from recommending a trip to Hell. Going to Hell would mean... becoming a fallen angel.*
*Still, there had been precedent for angels visiting Hell on official business.*
*However, the search for my book was an endlessly personal matter. It would never be approved.*
Samael: Relax. Just come with me. If you can't go to Hell, we can still meet up at Purgatory.
Raziel: Purgatory...?
Samael: A place once used to purify the sins of the wicked. No one's gonna question an angel being there, let alone consider it a sin.
*Was that truly so? Taking off to a place like that without prior consent... wouldn't that, in itself, be a sin?*
*In the end, though, I accepted her suggestion.*
*Tempted by Samael's honeyed words, I set out towards my new objective. According to Samael, she would wait for me at the top of the hill serving as Purgatory.*
*"Oh, you came." "Welcome, Raziel."*
*As I turned around to face both of them, I found myself frozen in place.*
*But my memories... please, give me time. And let me think.*
*The reason I froze in place. A being who had no business showing up at a place like that. Just... who was it, exactly?*
*Whose presence startled me to that extent?*
*"Will you read this book for me?" "Read it."*
*What was I forced to do? _What was I forced to read?_*
*"Well now, ladies and gentlemen. Allow me to educate you on—"*
*I found my consciousness dragged back to reality once more.*
*I saw Tendou Setsuna fight back a swarm of steel angels behind me, showing no compassion for his mechanical foes.*
*Gabriel and Raphael.*
*Both their appearance... as well as the sensation I experienced upon touching them made me realize that both of them were the real thing.*
*They were not dead. Though not alive, either.*
*They drifted vaguely between the boundaries of the two.*
*Existing as this grotesque, peculiar "thing." Yet the magic they released was certainly no imitation.*
*They were powerful enough angels to be able to release vast amounts of magic energy simply by existing.*
*In other words, turning them into this hideous object would effectively grant the protective barrier of that building an infinite supply of magic.*
*Whose twisted mind could have hatched such a plan? Either way, we needed to free them.*
Raziel: Initiating structural analysis. Structural ID code appended. A838861, alias AAM.
Raziel: Access denied. Located isolation program. Initializing self-replicating worm to disable isolation program.
*I would transform the very magic they exuded into something resembling a computer virus to establish a link.*
Raziel: Scanning emotional structure and personality data... no files found. They were all deleted...?
In other words, Gabriel and Raphael could never be revived. They were no more than mere objects now: still alive, but as good as dead.
*I had expected this outcome, but it still pained me deeply.*
Raziel: Magical emission order... detected. Overriding order, changing it to suspension.
*The moment I did that, I felt my consciousness drifting away — I was separated from reality and thrown into the depths of their memories.*
*It would appear that any tampering with the magical emission settings would result in said person to be recognized as an intruder, their consciousness spirited away.*
Raziel: This place is...
*Having become a dimly glowing astral body, I found myself gently drifting along in an infinite stream of blue.*
*And moments later, I ended up arriving at a place all too familiar to me.*
Raziel: The grand assembly hall of Heaven...
*The spacious assembly hall once filled with the booming echo of angels fervently discussing the words of the Lord... now fell into complete silence.*
Raziel: Anyone!
*Two angels responded to my yell.*
Raziel: Gabriel... and Raphael.
Gabriel / Man C: We stand here to address the one transferred to this memory.
Raphael / Woman C: The right of viewing this memory... is granted only to the one who suspended the magical emission. However, we do not know who you are.
Gabriel / Man C: With the emission halted, we are powerless to stop you. To avoid the exploitation of our bodies, we would enter a state of complete suspension once the memory reconstruction had terminated.
Raphael / Woman C: You may head for Heaven. We cannot tell what you may witness once there, nor what choices you would make.
Gabriel / Man C: However, if your soul is not completely bereft of compassion, you shall listen to our one request.
Raphael / Woman C: The disaster we call the Divine Calamity originated with the distinguished angel known as the "Secret of God" — Raziel.
Raziel: ...?
*A sensation akin to falling head-first into Tartarus overcame me.*
Gabriel / Man C: Hear us out, O kind soul. Spare the angels any further bloodshed... and kill Raziel.
Raziel: Wh-What are you talking about, Gabriel?! Why? Why...?!
Raphael / Woman C: We hold no grudge against her. However, _her continued existence may very well lead to further disaster_.
Raziel: You're wrong! Raphael, I... I have no idea what you're talking about! I didn't cause any of this!
*I lashed out at the pair, completely forgetting the fact that they were only memory fragments, not the real angels.*
*I howled at them in dismay, forgetting all pride and dignity.*
Gabriel / Man C: Hear us out, O kind soul. Spare the angels any further bloodshed...
Raphael / Woman C: ...and kill Raziel, the culprit behind the Divine Calamity who dared reveal God's secrets.
*Despite being pulled back to the real world, I continued to scream, unable to let go of the memory.*
Raziel: Tell me! Please, tell me! What have I done?! How... how did I cause the Divine Calamity?! I'm begging you... please, tell me!
*Gabriel and Raphael only met my pleas with a pair of silent gazes.*
*It had to be a lie. It couldn't be true! I would never do anything like that! But then... why did I lose my memories? Why couldn't I remember a single thing about what happened during the Calamity?*
*Because... because _I did not wish to remember it?_ I suppressed the painful memories of what I had done, what my actions led to.*
*I erased them. No, I couldn't have — after all, such an action would run counter to my raison d'etre of "recording."*
*I instead sealed them away in the very depths of my own heart.*
*However, in order to live, I needed to "record."*
*Somewhere deep in my soul, I still continued to yearn for it. Unable to bear the thought of lacking memories, I struggled desperately to reclaim them.*
*I feared it. Dreaded it. I wished to flee from it, to avert my gaze, to seek help. But at the same time, _I wished to see it, remember it and record it_.*
*The strong desire of wanting to record my sealed memories most likely warped my heart.*
*Moments before my consciousness returned to reality, I caught a brief glimpse of myself reflected in a mirror.*
Raziel: N-No...!
*And the face I beheld... ...belonged to a monster obsessed with the act of recording. A devilish smile was plastered on its face.*
*Every single one of the mechanical angels I had been fighting froze in place in the blink of an eye. After a few seconds of convulsing in one place, each of the ones that still soared in the skies plummeted to the earth below.*
*I had also noticed that the constant emission of magical energy had come to a halt. Raziel must have been successful.*
*I turned around and saw Raziel collapsed onto her knees, her vacant gaze fixed on the object before her.*
Setsuna: Raziel!
*No response. I called out to her again, this time causing her to turn around and look me in the eye.*
Raziel: Setsuna...
Setsuna: What happened—
*Before I could finish the sentence, Raziel leapt into my arms, calling my name in a trembling voice.*
Setsuna: Raziel...?
Raziel: Setsuna... I'm so afraid... so, so afraid...!
*Afraid?*
Setsuna: What brought this on all of a sudden...?
Raziel: Tell me! What have I done?! Did I cause the fall of Paradise?! Did I... did I exile everyone to Tokyo Babel?!
Setsuna: Raziel...
*I hadn't the faintest clue what Raziel had meant. Once I had managed to calm her down, I decided to inquire further.*
Raziel: I... I...
*In brief, disjointed bursts of words, Raziel revealed all she had learned upon entering that memory fragment of the object that once was Gabriel and Raphael.*
*"Kill Raziel."*
Raziel: Am I... someone to be hunted down? _The culprit behind the Divine Calamity?_ I don't know...! This is all too much for me...!
*She looked up at me teary eyed, waiting for an answer. It would be easy to say I could console her; far more difficult to actually do it.*
*However, I still had a duty to dry her tears.*
Setsuna: Raziel, I don't know what you did in the past... and I most likely couldn't understand it. But this much I can say: I'll stay by your side for as long as you want me to.
Raziel: You... will?
*Her voice came out as a faint whisper, nearly melting into the air.*
Setsuna: I will. I swear I will. So... please don't cry.
Raziel: You swear?
*Rubbing her eyes clean of tears, she once again posed a question to me.*
Setsuna: I do.
Raziel: And... what will you swear it on?
Setsuna: Hm.
*What would be appropriate in a situation like this?*
*To swear it on the name of God? Or the lives of my parents?*
*Neither would work, I felt. God was nowhere to be found, nor did I have parents to call my own. Even if I did, it would only be a single mother.*
Setsuna: O-On the sun.
Raziel: The sun?
Setsuna: I swear it on the stars, the moon, and the skies above.
*It all felt rather, um... embarrassing, if I did say so myself.*
Raziel: ......
Setsuna: I didn't really have anything else to swear on, you see...
Raziel: Haha...
*Raziel smiled as she let her forehead rest against mine.*
Setsuna: I can feel your skull pressing against mine.
*And a thin layer of skin.*
Raziel: This is a bit weird... I wish you would've said something romantic, the way people do in some of my books...
*She let out a brief chuckle.*
Setsuna: And this isn't romantic?
Raziel: Not one bit.
*I didn't expect her to go that far. I mean, I had _some_ confidence in myself, at least.*
*Seeing my expression turn sour only made her smile broaden.*
Setsuna: Raziel. I want to reclaim your memories.
Raziel: But—
Setsuna: It might be hard for you. Unimaginably terrifying, in fact. But... I think it's still better than having them perish completely.
Raziel: I feel that way, too. No matter what my memories may hold, a sin must be punished accordingly.
Setsuna: And I'll be at your side to shoulder the same punishment. I want to be there for you in both hardship and joy.
Raziel: Thank you, Setsuna. Even if those words were a lie... they made me happy. More so than you think.
*It was no lie. I would stay by her side, no matter what.*
Raziel: Thanks. Let us go then to Heaven... to face my sins.
*We left Kabukicho and soared towards the rooftop of the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building.*
*We encountered no obstacles, no enemies. With the flow of magic halted, a calming silence fell upon the entirety of the seventh stratum.*
*We landed at the helipad. Neither me, nor Raziel had to search for anything, for our objective appeared magically before our very eyes the moment our feet touched the ground.*
Raziel: Jacob's Ladder...
Setsuna: Incredible...
*The sheer majesty of it left me in complete awe.*
*A stairwell bright as the stars, its steps climbing far into the distance, piercing the clouds. At its end, beyond the boundaries of Tokyo Babel, stood the Gates of Heaven.*
*The stairwell proved wide enough for us to walk side by side.*
Raziel: ......
*Raziel cast a terrified gaze at the steps below.*
Setsuna: Let's go, Raziel. We'll reclaim your memories.
*Her memories of the Divine Calamity. Memories of the sin she had committed. Nonetheless, she needed them back.*
Raziel: Okay... let's go.
*We began our long ascent up Jacob's Ladder. The moment we took our first steps, I immediately felt separated from the Tokyo Babel I'd come to call my home.*
*The canvas of the heavens stretched far and wide above the stairwell, its steps leading ever upwards in a straight line.*
Setsuna: ......
Raziel: ......
*For some reason, flying never occurred to me. And I didn't feel like I could've done it even if it did.*
*We continued onwards at a leisurely pace, taking one firm step after another. The brightly shining sun above showed no sign of movement.*
*I was going to keep track of time through my internal clock, but eventually forgot about it.*
*The very concept of time had seemingly been erased here. We felt no fatigue as we pressed on, nor did we ever begin to sweat.*
Not even boredom would rear its ugly head. Only one thing mattered: climbing the stairwell before us. That sole action...
*_...filled my heart with pure bliss_.*
*I forced myself to stop, prompting Raziel — who had ascended a step further than me — to turn around and look back at me with confusion. As we were still holding hands, she could advance no further like this.*
Raziel: What's wro—
*I pulled out the Peccati Sword from a pocket dimension, took a firm hold of the sharp end of its blade and squeezed with all the strength I could muster.*
Setsuna: ...!
*I forcefully amplified my senses, causing myself to experience a particularly acute jolt of pain. This served to distract my mind from the wicked illusion of bliss that assailed me a moment before.*
*The way to Heaven had to be filled with hardship — a journey bereft of joy. For man must ascend as he shoulders the heavy burden of his cross.*
*I balled my wounded hand into a fist, forcibly preventing the blood from coagulating.*
*This was the pain of mankind. The very pain that made us human.*
*I continued to ascend, taking step after step.*
*Discarding all but the pain... and warmth of her palm in mine.*
*The mental contamination had grown increasingly severe, forcing me to eventually discard even my past memories of Tokyo Babel.*
*My training session with Belial. The time I first met Camael and Astaroth.*
*The day I met Lilith and Sorami. All the time we spent together.*
*I deemed each memory redundant, discarding them without hesitation.*
*I sighed in relief as the blank region of my mind expanded once again. All my memories save for those of Raziel had been reduced to mere data profiles.*
Setsuna: I...
Raziel: ...?
*As I continued to climb the stairwell, I found myself uttering a phrase that had never left my lips before.*
Setsuna: I think I'm in love with you.
*Crippling anxiety ravaged my heart, coupled with the precise fear that eventually, the ever-advancing mental contamination would erase even Raziel from my mind.*
*Which is why I felt I should say the words while I still had the chance.*
Raziel: ...I knew.
*A faint smile crept onto her lips. It may have seemed like I was trying to act mature.*
Setsuna: I love how beautiful your hair is.
Raziel: Mhm.
Setsuna: I love your eyes, too.
Raziel: Mhm.
Setsuna: And the lovely ring of your voice.
Raziel: Mhm.
Setsuna: I love the way you read your books, the way you sleep, and the way you smile when tasting something delicious. I love them all.
Raziel: Mhm.
Setsuna: I love your heart and soul. I realize this might sound like I'm all talk.
Raziel: ...It doesn't. Thank you.
Setsuna: Either way, I love everything about you. And I wanted to convey these feelings while I still could.
Raziel: While you still could?
Setsuna: Exactly.
*Raziel's expression shifted to one of complete astonishment. She must have realized what I was trying to say.*
Raziel: Setsuna, don't tell me you...
Setsuna: Kugutsu Sorami. Lilith. Astaroth. Camael. Belial.
*All gone without a trace.*
*How we spent our time together, how their words might have moved my heart... I could remember nothing of it.*
Raziel: I'm sorry...
*Raziel spoke up again, her tone coated in sadness. I tried as best as I could to shelter my emotions when I finally responded.*
Setsuna: This isn't your fault, Raziel. It was bound to happen eventually.
*In order to prevent madness from claiming my mind, to protect the one I held most dear... There had to be a price to pay.*
Raziel: Even still... I'm sorry.
*Raziel's voice fell to a whisper, her very tone pregnant with regret. Did she feel that way because this all pertained to her lost memories?*
*We continued to ascend, upwards and upwards and upwards...*
Raziel: We've almost reached the clouds.
*Her words made it feel like we were close to the end. The sun continued to shower us with its light, but I could still catch a glimpse of the stars and the moon.*
*The veil of brilliant, white clouds blanketed Jacob's Ladder. Naturally, we had no choice but to break through, knowing that beyond it lay the sealed gates of Heaven.*
Setsuna: Let's go.
*We passed through the blanket of clouds. The corrupted feelings lingering in them made the experience both suffocating and terrifying.*
*May you embrace eternal bliss.*
Its resounding prayer permeated the very clouds: incessant, aggravating, unnecessary.
*Under constant attack by such sensations, the two of us continued onwards.*
Setsuna: Phahh...!
*Having held my breath for so long, I sounded somewhat awkward when I finally exhaled.*
Raziel: We're here...
*A hint of excitement lingered in Raziel's voice; even I found myself in awe as we beheld the Gates of Heaven towering above us. However, it lasted a mere heartbeat.*
Raziel: It looks the same... nothing's changed...
*She appeared somewhat relieved. If she was right and nothing had changed...*
*...then how would I explain this ominous feeling creeping up on my heart? In all its splendor and divine majesty... something about the gates felt out of place.*
*Nonetheless, we had to press on. Neither of us had any intention to turn back.*
*At first glance, I spotted no keyholes. I suppose we would simply need to push the gates open. I promptly placed my right hand on its surface.*
*In that very moment, I felt like my entire arm was ready to melt away. My right arm reached into the gate until the elbow — almost like it had become one with it — as I uttered a single word.*
Setsuna: Open.
*The gate began to slide open with a heavy creak. And so the door to Heaven was liberated, officially completing the mission Lilith had entrusted me with.*
*Whatever came next would be driven by my will, and mine alone. I wished to stay by Raziel's side as we ventured onwards to reclaim her memories.*
Raziel: ......
Setsuna: Let's go.
*I stepped forward without even waiting for an answer, ready to bear witness to a world showered by light under the gaze of brilliant, blue skies—*
Raziel: ...!
*No...!*
*What... is this?! What is this overwhelming terror in the air?!*
*Before us stretched a rainbow-colored sky, its rich palette inviting madness into the hearts of all those who gazed upon it.*
*In the distance, a lavish field of green. Upon the numerous stakes littering the field groaned not the sinners of the world, but angels.*
*Ooooooooooh...*
*Their moans were not that of anguish and despair, _but pure, unmitigated joy_.*
*Their bodies pierced through, their entrails naked and exposed... yet they gazed down upon the carnage with expressions of genuine bliss.*
Raziel: Ugh...
*We stopped at a field of flowers nearby, with a young girl and a boy _bathing in each other's blood_.*
Boy A / Man A: Have a look at this!
*The boy held up a smiling, severed head and hurled it in the other's direction. The girl caught it, then promptly placed it on the neck of a headless body.*
Girl A / Woman A: No good! It won't move!
Boy A / Man A: Then let's try it with your head now!
*The young boy immediately decapitated the girl with the hatchet he had been holding. The girl's head, a smile frozen on its lips, tumbled to the ground below.*
*They were massacring each other in the most gruesome ways imaginable.*
*In that case, shouldn't this place be called Hell? The problem was... that each and every one of them _seemed to be enjoying it_.*
*Happily drowning in joy, all of them. They might have felt pain, but never despair.*
*This was their bliss, their paradise; angels and mortals alike indulging in their own desires, shedding each other's blood without a care in the world.*
*Mortals who accumulated several virtuous deeds, had their sins purified and thus earned their place in Heaven... as well as the angels who were allowed to reside there through the Lord's pardon. They were both at each other's throats now, spilling blood with smiles unfading.*
*In other words... ...thoughts would only lead to unhappiness. They imagined their future and despaired at the death they saw in it.*
*And here they were now, liberated from its yoke, their minds devoid of reason and no longer able to comprehend death. In such a state, despair would elude them.*
*Pain would transform to ecstasy, dread and despair to unbridled rapture.*
*In short... _This was the true face of Heaven_.*
Raziel: N-No... nnnnoooooooooooooooo...!!
*The other angels all looked up as Raziel's terrified scream echoed across the plains.*
Angel A / Woman A: What's wrong, Raziel?
Angel B / Woman C: Come, join our bloodbath!
Angel C / Woman B: I love you, Raziel! You can kill me anytime you want!
*Without a second of hesitation, I lifted my sword and mowed down all the maddened angels lunging at us.*
*I rushed up to Raziel — who had been crouching on the ground, screaming — picked her up and continued on.*
Raziel: No! It's not my fault! It's not my fault!
*No matter where we ran or flew, a flock of angels came after us in pursuit, each of them flashing broad smiles as they bled from several wounds like a group of living dead.*
I ran — soared — as fast as I could, but there was no end to Heaven: its realm stretched infinitely in all directions.
Raziel: My memories... they hurt... I can't... no... disruption... rebooting... no... error... no! No, no, no! It's not true! This book... no... I can't...!
*Raziel pried herself free from my embrace and collapsed onto a grassy field, convulsing like she was experiencing a seizure of sorts. I hurried to her side and clutched her hand, intent on calming her down.*
Setsuna: Raziel!
Raziel: My... my book. Ah, yes. My book. It has to be here... my book...
*She took a few unsteady steps.*
Angel A / Woman A: Ahahahaha...!
Angel B / Woman C: Ehehehehe...!
Angel C / Woman B: Hahahahaha...!
Setsuna: Out of my way!
*I slaughtered every single one of the angels that caught up to us. After trudging through a heap of smiling corpses, I took off in pursuit of Raziel.*
*And eventually... arrived here. A colossal, majestic building that could very well instill fear in its observer.*
Raziel: Ah, that's right. The assembly hall.
*Raziel bolted off; I followed. I ran and ran as much as my legs would allow me... and then I saw it.*
Raziel: Ah... I knew it. So it was true... my book was the cause of all this...!
Setsuna: Wh-What the...
*I couldn't find the words. We were looking at an entire mountain of corpses, all belonging to angels. This, in itself, hardly differed from the situation outside... except for one notable exception.*
*Their expressions.*
*The angels and mortals we had encountered outside all had expressions of utmost ecstasy and joy.*
*The faces of these angels, on the other hand, were frozen in terror, their expressions violently contorted by anguish and despair. Although we had been spared the stench of decay, the smell of blood in the air was all too prevalent.*
Setsuna: Raziel...
Raziel: It's true. That day, I had learned something terrible. But who told me...? Samael... I remember now. It was Samael who whispered it into my ear.
She gently lifted a book off the nearby desk. It was the other volume of the Sefer Raziel: the so-called Book of Heavens.
Raziel: There's one thing mortals possess that the angels, demons, and God himself lack. Do you know what it is?
Setsuna: ...I don't.
Raziel: It's... the concept of "eternity."
Setsuna: What do you mean? You didn't know what eternity was?
*Raziel shook her head.*
Raziel: That's not it. We knew the meaning of the word itself. But we were designed never to consider exactly what that could entail.
*She held up her book.*
Raziel: It's written here in the Book of Heavens. It has all the design blueprints for demons, angels... and _even God_.
*The design blueprints... for God? Impossible...*
*Ignoring my astonishment, Raziel carried on in a low tone.*
Raziel: And I... opened their eyes to the concept of eternity. In other words—
*Raziel glanced at the terror-stricken faces of the dead angels and shook her head.*
Raziel: _The catalyst of this tragedy was none other than I_.
*I stared at Raziel in silence, forgetting even to speak for a few seconds.*
*"Raziel. Hear me, Raziel, holder of God's secrets."*
*"Why have you opened our eyes to this terrible concept? Why did you make us understand its cruel truth?"*
Raziel: Because... I thought we should know.
*None of us wanted this knowledge. We lived for eternity, all the while liberated from the very concept of it.*
Raziel: But... why would you want to remain ignorant? Why should an angel lack knowledge of something that even mortals can comprehend?!
*Answer me, Raziel. Who implanted this theory into your mind? Whose whispers led you to this way of thinking?*
*Raziel simply cried. Pitifully, heart-wrenchingly.*
Raziel: I was never deceived or instigated. I'm not trying to pin the blame on anyone else. I merely believed... that we should know. And this was the result.
*The angels had understood the concept of "eternity." As they themselves possessed life eternal, that knowledge drove them to insanity.*
*They were forced to live for an eternity. That, in itself, was a maddening truth. A hellish realization.*
*Without the concept of eternity, it didn't matter if today, tomorrow, and yesterday were all the same.*
*However, they came to comprehend... what eternal life truly meant. To them, that realization came as nothing less than a curse.*
*They would live through the downfall of a myriad nations and see the death of entire civilizations... only to remain as mere observers.*
*Even if the winds of change stir the mortal realm, Heaven would remain the same. Even the angels' great war with the demons had been reduced to a distant memory from eons past.*
*Every day, hour, minute, and second would be the same, birthing not a shred of change to Heaven. Even if a change did occur, it would last no more than a day or so.*
*They would never stake their very lives to bring about drastic changes like mortals did.*
*Eternity! A whole eternity! A hundred years, two hundred, three hundred or four!*
*Even if every single mortal in every possible parallel world had forgotten about the angels, they would nonetheless have to continue to exist as observers!*
*Their minds could no longer take it and succumbed to madness, yearning for _happiness_.*
*And so they began to sing. And so the chorus was born. A wicked ode tempting all to embrace bliss, to cast aside knowledge and reason.*

Setsuna: ......
Leviathan: By the way, Raziel. I have something I wish to tell you.
Raziel: It will have to wait a bit. I'm in the middle of some really complex calculations right now.
Leviathan: Hm. Then we shall wait for you to finish. Won't we, Tendou Setsuna?
Setsuna: Y-Yes...
*Um... I had a feeling I sort of knew what he wanted to say. I wondered if I should just avert my gaze altogether...*
*When Leviathan revealed himself to us, I was inevitably caught by a large amount of water that splashed my way.*
In fact, I ended up completely drenched. The problem lay in the following: I wasn't the only one. Raziel, too, was dripping from head to toe.
*In short...*
Setsuna: Wet and wild...
Leviathan: Did you say something, son?
Setsuna: Not a thing.
*Despite what I had just blurted out, I had no ulterior motives whatsoever.*
Raziel: ......
*Raziel appeared to be staring intently at her tablet screen, performing a series of calculations. It felt rude to interrupt her, but...*
*I might just have to. But still...*
*If I pointed it out to her now, she would undoubtedly be enraged by the interruption... and the very fact that I pointed it out. Both seemed very much likely.*
*However, if I only mentioned it afterwards, she would only get mad about the latter.*
*In short, I was better off holding my tongue at the moment. This was the right choice. No question about it.*
*I felt satisfied that I had managed to come to such an unanimous conclusion.*
Leviathan: I believe the sooner we let her know, the better.
Setsuna: Hold up. She'd only get angry.
Leviathan: But still...
Raziel: All right, calculations are all done. I'm ready to hear you out now, Leviathan.
*Leviathan's eyeball darted to me in an instant. It appeared he wanted to push this responsibility onto me. Very well... I would be the one to tell her.*

Raziel: It was quite the shock, wasn't it...

*Raziel cocked her head, her expression gradually melting into confusion.*
Raziel: What of it?

Raziel: ...?!
*Raziel's blank expression flushed red in an instant, like someone had lit a fire in her cheeks. She threw a mean glare at us, her entire body trembling.*
Leviathan: Ah, no! This isn't what it looks like! I was firmly against it! In fact, I urged we point it out to you right away, but this here lad decided not to!

*The sea serpent's colossal eyes widened at my rebuttal. It was a fearsome sight, truth be told.*
Leviathan: How else am I to make an appearance, then? This is oppression! Vile oppression, I say!
Raziel: ...Who cares.
The Two: Hm?
Raziel: I said, who cares. About either of you. The only thing you need to do right now... is die!
*Raziel held out both her hands in our direction.*
Raziel: Property manipulation — fire. Burn to asheeeeeeeees!!

*She didn't. Naturally. I had the top of my head burned, while Leviathan suffered an even crueler fate.*
Leviathan: I can't see a darned thing...
Setsuna: To think she'd actually hit you straight in the eye with those flames... ah, um, nevermind.
*I was sitting on the ground, looking very repentant.*
Raziel: ......
*Raziel hugged her own body, as if to protect it, her eyes misty with tears as she glared at me.*
Leviathan: By the way, how far did you two make it?
Setsuna: The sixth stratum. We then decided to turn back.
Raziel: We even found one of the volumes of my Sefer Raziel.
Leviathan: Ah, that one? I went out of my way to fish it out of the sea for you once, then you go losing it again, hm?
Raziel: U-Um, about that... I'm really very sorry. Truly.
*Raziel rubbed her hands together nervously. Leviathan's nostrils flared, and a moment later, we found ourselves hit by a tremendous gust of wind.*
*Had he done it without holding back, we would not have come out of it unscathed.*
Leviathan: Oh, it's all water under the ol' bridge, as they say. Putting that aside, though... listen, Raziel. How's the state of Tokyo Babel and Pandora right now?

Leviathan: All I do is roam the submerged halls of Hell, if you recall. So no, I haven't heard a single thing.
Raziel: I see. We're going through... very difficult times, to say the least. That's how I see it.
*Raziel went on, letting the sea serpent know about what had transpired at Tokyo Babel.*
*Leviathan nodded diligently at each of Raziel's explanations. When the angel, however, made a mention of Samael, the sea serpent seemed visibly puzzled.*
Leviathan: Samael, you say?
Raziel: Yes, Samael. The so-called Serpent of Death. As a fellow inhabitant of Hell, you must have met her at least once.

*Leviathan had just uttered something quite peculiar.*
Raziel: Odd...? In what way?
Leviathan: As far as I know, Samael... well, _she's already dead_. And considering she perished at Tokyo Babel, her soul is now forever gone.

*What... in the world was going on here?*
Setsuna: Where did you see that...?!

Setsuna: ...?
*Astaroth killed Samael...?*

Raziel: So then... who _was_ the Samael we met?
*We all fell into deep silence, mulling over the issue.*
Leviathan: Samael crawls upon the earth like the serpent she is, able to escape even the jaws of death through continuously shedding her skin. Yet she died. Permanently. I saw with my very own eyes as her soul faded into oblivion.
Setsuna: In that case...
*Just as a speculation...*
*Could it be that Leviathan was lying? The chances of that were not zero, through extremely low nonetheless. The same went for the possibility of him mistaking her for someone else.*
*He and Samael were both dwellers of Hell. She was a fallen angel, and a powerful one at that. Leviathan would never have made such a mistake.*
*He also had nothing to gain from this. We were here on the outside only by pure chance. Why would Leviathan lie to someone he wasn't even expecting to show up?*
*Which left us with only one possible conclusion.*
*If Leviathan's words could be trusted... the Samael we met was a fake.*
*The bigger problem was figuring out what sort of an impostor she was. Could she have been a shapeshifter? Or a clone created by someone?*
Leviathan: As I've never seen this fake Samael, I couldn't give you a sure answer. However, there is one thing I can say with certainty.
*I nodded, continuing where he left off.*
Setsuna: Samael's not our main culprit here at Tokyo Babel. Actually, even if she did act as the catalyst, the one we're up against now is someone else. Someone just as powerful.
Leviathan: Very well said, lad. And our prime suspect is...
The Two: Astaroth.
*The third most powerful demon after Lucifer and Beelzebub and the holder of the highest authority at Tokyo Babel. Not even Camael and his angels dare ignore his commands.*
*And someone like that had apparently murdered Samael.*
*That wasn't the problem, though. After all, Samael was the culprit behind the Divine Calamity. No one who fought and killed her would be questioned as a criminal.*
*However... _Astaroth had not said a single word about slaying Samael_. Therein lied the problem. And a big one at that.*
*He would have no reason to keep Samael's death a secret.*
*She was undoubtedly one of the prime suspects. And if waves of maddened masters showed up even after her death, he would continue his search anew.*
*There was no reason whatsoever to keep quiet about this. Unless...*
*_Unless he wanted to set her up as the culprit_.*
*Abdiel warned us to be wary of Astaroth. I never doubted his words, but with this revelation, my suspicions had only deepened.*
*At the very least, we needed to watch ourselves around him. At the moment, we needed to convey this new information to Lilith as soon as possible.*
Leviathan: Watch your backs around Astaroth, you hear me? If something does happen, you can count on me.
Raziel: Very well. And thank you.
*Raziel had turned pale. I couldn't exactly blame her, either.*
Setsuna: Have you managed to figure out the location of the plate?
Raziel: Yes. Tokyo Babel travels at a fixed speed, so using the coordinates of where Gethel's body hit the water, as well as my memories of the time it took for her to fall, I should be able to more or less pinpoint the location. Follow me.
*Raziel took me by the hand, her eyes alarmingly hollow, almost like they had become devoid of color.*
Setsuna: Raziel, what's wrong?
Raziel: Nothing.
Leviathan: ...Raziel. One more thing before you go.
Raziel: ...?
*Raziel glanced up at Leviathan.*
Leviathan: I sense turbulence in your heart, for it wanders the sea of chaos: the first sea that raged before God ever set to creating the world.
Raziel: I...
Leviathan: Those thrown into the sea of chaos lose sight of themselves. Unable to differentiate between what they had and hadn't done, they continue to chase after that elusive wonder known as truth.
Raziel: ......
Leviathan: However, that truth of yours may only end up being one side of the coin, one aspect of the whole.
Raziel: One aspect of the whole...?
Leviathan: Know this: if you aim to search for the truth on your own, certain things may inevitably elude you. And that is all I can say now.
Raziel: Thank you, Leviathan.
Leviathan: Oh please, save your gratitude and go! Scram! I'll be here all day unless you two start to get going.
*Smiling, we both waved goodbye to Leviathan and continued onwards to the lower strata.*
Leviathan: I believe I'm starting to understand what you might be planning... Astaroth.
Leviathan: However, I cannot pursue this train of thought any further, nor can I convey it to anyone. The clouds blanketing my mind must never lift, _lest I come to the very same conclusion as Astaroth_.
*And so Leviathan chose to forget. There existed things neither angels, nor demons must even think about. Something they had to remain ignorant of, no matter what.*
*Having lived for so many years, Leviathan's unimaginably high level of intellect rivaled that of demon lords and master angels. As such, the chances of his mind comprehending that dreadful concept were exceedingly high.*
*And so he could not talk of its secrets.*
Leviathan: Forgive me, Raziel.
*Once Leviathan had confirmed that the two entered Tokyo Babel, he once again returned to the submerged realms of Hell.*
*We had returned to the all-too-familiar landscape of Ginza.*
We could not tarry any longer: we had to find Lilith and regroup.
Raziel: ......
*Although Raziel had become a touch more optimistic due to Leviathan's words, a dark and heavy shadow still clouded her expression.*
*What could she have been afraid of? Astaroth? Or something else?*
*I recalled Leviathan's words, how he told us that Raziel's heart had been wandering the sea of chaos.*
*She could be hiding something from me.*
*Something not even she could fully comprehend.*
*Was it a truth too dreadful, too overwhelming to be put into words?*
Needless to say, the key to solving all this was Raziel's own memories: particularly the ones pertaining to what happened during the Divine Calamity.
*For instance... And this truly was mere conjecture...*
*What if Raziel caused the Divine Calamity, then proceeded to live her life at Tokyo Babel, oblivious to it all?*
*What if she never forgot? No, that couldn't be true; the fact she accompanied me on my pilgrimage was evidence of that. I was reading too much into this.*
*While I felt ashamed by my own train of thought, the fact I purposefully discarded logic and reason in favor of denying such a possibility similarly made me ashamed of myself.*
Setsuna: Raziel.
Raziel: Yes?
Setsuna: No matter what happens, you need to stay strong. If the waves are about to claim you, I'll be there to pull you out. So... remain calm and always look for a way to survive.

Setsuna: Don't mention it. I love you, remember?
Raziel: ...I do.
*Raziel gave a flustered nod. I attempted to display some level of confidence, but even I found it somewhat embarrassing.*
*We decided to head for Pandora through the door in the clock tower, just as we had done before. In the meantime, I let my mind wander, thinking of the various things that still lay in store for us.*
*We pushed the door open and leapt through, arriving at one of the academy's hallways.*
Setsuna: We're finally here...
*The journey felt both tremendously long and painfully short. Either way, as I was aching for some rest, I headed for the night duty room.*
*...Which was when I first took notice of something being amiss.*
*The silent hallways. The deserted classrooms. And the severe lack of any passer-by.*
Raziel: Something's... not right.
Setsuna: Yeah.
*The campus felt anything but normal. We hadn't been able to spot a single person since we arrived.*
*I felt an electric shock rush through my entire body as I switched to combat mode, pulling out the Peccati Sword from my pocket dimension without a moment's delay.*
Setsuna: Raziel.
Raziel: Got it.
*Raziel tucked her tablet under one arm as we took off towards the night duty room while being constantly vigilant of our surroundings.*
*The night duty room... was empty, but we found a number of things that could be used as clues.*
*Two cups of coffee left out on the table. They must have belonged to Lilith and Sorami. I wasn't certain about Sorami, but Lilith had her own, personal cup for tea and coffee.*
*I brushed a finger against the remnants of coffee at the bottom of the cup, its moisture telling me it had not been a day since these were left here. Could they have been captured shortly after finishing their drinks?*
*Or perhaps they had to leave due to some sort of emergency before they could put the cups away?*
Raziel: Setsuna.
*I felt an undercurrent of urgency in her tone.*
Setsuna: Yes?
Raziel: Someone's coming. Hide your magic!

Raziel: They're heading straight for this room.
*She was right. Through intense listening, I made out the sound of footsteps, belonging to... three people in total. I could also detect that they advanced with slow and careful steps, their alertness hitting Defcon 2.*
*They... they had most likely already taken notice of our presence. They simply did not know our exact location.*
*Still, I could piece together what they had in mind. More specifically, they decided to first investigate the room we used as our base of operations. This room.*
Raziel: What are we going to do?
*Fight. The decision came to me without a moment of hesitation. We would not let them kill us. I had no idea what had befallen Pandora, but for the time being... I would stay and fight.*
*On the other hand, taking lives here could become a problem later on. As such, merely rendering them unconscious would be far more desirable an option. I would have preferred to interrogate someone to learn what had happened, but considering our circumstances, that would prove difficult.*
*I sheathed my steel and suppressed my magic. I had to rely on nothing more than my own physical abilities to overcome the opposition.*
*The approaching footsteps grew louder, the three people in question each marching at their own speed, as opposed to electing a leader to take the front with the other two trailing behind.*
*They had no leader. Which meant the three of them were equal in rank. With their destination clear and set, their stride betrayed no trace of hesitation.*
There was no mistaking it: they were heading straight for the night duty room.
*After giving Raziel a series of hand-waved instructions, I quietly made my way to the back of the room, opened the window and leaned outside.*
Angel A / Man B: Don't move!

Raziel: Property elimination. "Air" — Level 2!
Angel A / Man B: ...?

The Two: And a one, and a two, and a go!
*As the three angels were entirely too panicked to prevail in a hand-to-hand scuffle, we decided to knock them unconcious.*

*Seeing how their primary duty seemed to be patrolling the perimeters, they would no doubt need to give regular status reports. If said reports suddenly stopped, it would inevitably spark a state of high alert.*
*In other words, ours was a race against the clock. We bolted outside to the hallway.*
Raziel: Where do you think they are?
*I had several ideas. One of the classrooms, the student council room, the gymnasium... and finally, Astaroth's office.*

*He had finally put his plans into motion, making sure to first eliminate future obstacles — that is, Lilith and Sorami.*

Lilith: I wouldn't exactly call this "all right." Anyway—
*Lilith's telepathy cut off abruptly. Could something have happened? Either way, we needed to make haste.*
