*We managed to sneak past them. They appeared exceedingly vigilant, no doubt partly owing to them stumbling upon those three angels in the closet.*
*Our foes were no doubt scanning each area for magical activities. Using our magic would only reveal our locations to them.*
*As such, remaining hidden depended solely on my own abilities. What's more, the angels themselves were far more perceptive than mortals. Nonetheless, despite the odds being stacked against us, we managed to make it to the gymnasium without incident.*
*All right.*
*As I reached out to push the gym doors open, I suddenly felt a chill run down my spine. Someone was waiting in ambush on the other side. Someone who felt no need to hide their abundant magical prowess.*
*It was neither Lilith or Sorami. Belial...? No, not him. Naturally, it wasn't Samael, the Serpent of Death, either.*
*Which left Astaroth, or possibly—*
*I felt vaguely confident in my assumption that neither Astaroth, nor Samael, or even Lucifuge awaited me beyond these doors.*
*The flow of magic I perceived from the other side felt clear and vibrant like a forest stream, intense like raging fire.*
*I opened the door... ...and came face to face with _him_, standing there in the middle.*
*The commander of twelve thousand angels of destruction and the living incarnation of the might of God — Camael.*
Raziel: Camael...
Camael: ......
*The angel's expression remained stern and unflinching. Next to him, Lilith and Sorami lay on the ground, their hands tied behind their backs with a group of angels pointing swords at their necks.*
*One word from Camael and their blades would strike — Lilith could possibly survive the ordeal, but not Sorami.*
Lilith: Um.... sorry. They caught us shortly after I called you...
Sorami: O-Owowow! C-Careful there! My arms are famously inflexible, I'll have you know... owowooow!
*Camael sighed, then gave one of his underlings an order.*
Camael: Loosen her bonds.
Sorami: Phew... I think I'm gonna be more diligent with those post-bath stretching exercises from now on...
*As usual, Sorami was still... well, being Sorami.*
Camael: They may be my hostages, but I have no intention of hurting them. ...Well, provided you don't give me any reason to.
Raziel: Why have you done this?
Camael: To stop you, obviously. What other reason would there be?
Setsuna: That's not what I meant. _Why do you want to stop us_?
Camael: Setsuna. I've no quarrel with you. Unless you side with Raziel, that is. Then we have a bit of a problem.
*I felt my heart race fast in my chest, to the point of being painful.*
Setsuna: Explain yourself.
Raziel hugged her own body, her eyes widening in terror. There was no mistaking it: she was trembling with fear.
Camael: Raziel. _You're the cause of all this_.
*His words were like a dagger in Raziel's heart.*
Raziel: I'm... the cause...? Of what...?
Camael: Do I really need to spell it out? The Divine Calamity — you were the one who caused it.
*The very air in the room seemed to freeze over as the angels all glared at Raziel, their expressions heavy with emotions that could be either fear or contempt.*
*Fat beads of sweat trickled down Raziel's forehead, color gradually draining from her cheeks.*
Raziel: What... are you talking about...?
*Camael's expression remained devoid of emotion, while Raziel's reflected deeper and deeper hues of bewilderment with each passing second.*
Raziel: You say I brought about the Divine Calamity...? But I... I have no such power!
Camael: That I won't deny. However, you are the one who knows the secrets of God: the owner of the Sefer Raziel, the one tome that revealed even the mysteries of Creation itself.
Camael: I feel it's only natural to believe that your book was responsible for the Divine Calamity, wouldn't you agree?
Raziel: No! But, I mean... I'm... I was searching for that book! It was never in my possession! I'd spent all this time looking for it!
Camael: Wrong. The Serpent of Death has loosened her tongue, claiming she had given the book to you before the Calamity.
*The Serpent of Death — Samael. But Samael died! That must've been the fake one!*
Raziel: What...?
*Raziel collapsed onto her knees, unable to comprehend Camael's so-called "truth."*
Camael: She herself told me.
Camael: The Serpent of Death found and picked up the book, once discarded within the depths of Purgatory. Seeing how she couldn't puzzle out its encryption, she handed it to you.
Raziel: I...

*Which would mean that... _Camael must have spoken the truth_.*

Camael: Answer me, Raziel. Where were you at the time of the Divine Calamity? And what did you do?
Raziel: I... my book...
*She clasped her hands together, almost as if in prayer.*
Camael: I'm waiting for an answer, Raziel! What did you write in that book?
Raziel: The Sefer Raziel... holds all the knowledge of the world. Everything that I, who bears the name "The Secrets of God," knows...
Camael: I already know that! But I just can't understand! What drove you to do this? Why would you bring about such a nightmare!
Camael: Fellow angels spilling each other's blood as they cackled, decapitated themselves with a smile... reveled in destruction with a song on their lips! That... that living nightmare!
Raziel: I don't know! I really don't! I'm telling the truth!
Setsuna: Camael! Do you believe what Samael claims? Can you truly place any trust in the words of that serpent?!
Camael: I do. Because I made her write it down. The seventy sacred pens of Yaasriel record only the truth. What I have told you was exactly what she wrote down. In other words, the truth.
*Yaasriel's sacred pens were said to be able to write down the true name of God — a name kept hidden even from the angels themselves. Whoever used the pen was incapable of writing anything but the complete truth.*
Raziel: ......
*Raziel was overwhelmed, seemingly having understood just how much power Yaasriel's pen held.*
Camael: Do you see now, Raziel? Why you had lost your memories and whether your amnesia was genuine or a mere fabrication... no longer matters.
*Camael spread his mechanical wings, his frigid expression the noose around Raziel's neck.*
Camael: You committed a sin. If you believe I shall spare your life to allow you to atone... think again!
*Camael spread his arms wide, his cuffs spitting out his twin-weapons, the same ones Raziel had told me about before—*
Camael: Behold "Death" and "Retribution" — a most fitting pair to sing your funeral ode.
*His right hand wielded an executioner's blade, a massive, bulky thing without a pointed tip, its purpose only to decapitate the foes that dared stand in its way.*
*Camael called it "Death." In his left hand rested a revolver with a brilliant, silver glint.*
*The so-called Peacemaker, a famous gun designed by Colt — both the weapon and its name heavily associated with the United States.*
*This was "Retribution."*
Camael: Make your choice, and make it swift! Choose Death, and your head shall fall to dust under its decapitating steel! Choose Retribution, and your body shall know the agonizing sting of its bullets!
*My ragged breathing had already evened out. My heart was calm once again.*
Setsuna: Raziel!
Raziel: ......
*For a brief moment, I had trouble finding the right words. There were a myriad things I should have told her — that I'd be by her side, that I wanted her to flee.*
*But I somewhat knew none of those words would reach the very core of her now-turbulent heart.*
*So I yelled the following.*
Setsuna: Don't flee! Stand and fight! Look straight ahead, into the eyes of reality! Once you've accepted it, think of what to do next!
Camael: I should've known... you plan to oppose us, Tendou Setsuna? Your passion is admirable, but I shall show no mercy!
Setsuna: Worry not, you don't need to. Now then... come!
*Brandishing the Peccati Sword, I lunged forward to split the angel's head open with a single blow.*
*He met my advance with Death and Retribution. Camael swung his terrible blade with all the power he could muster, yet his expression remained frigid as steel.*
*My sword was being repelled farther and farther away from his head.*
Camael: ...Shha!
*His roundhouse kick landed a clean hit on the side of my head and sent me flying all the way back to the wall.*
Raziel: Setsuna...!
*Spin, turn, land; using the wall I had just been blown into as a foothold, I lunged forward!*
Setsuna: Come forth, Sloth! Heed not the call of labor and hoard your unearned riches as you waste away in unending slumber!
*I summoned forth the molten gold of Sloth to buy myself some time.*
Camael: Only a fool would send the beasts of the seven deadly sins into battle against an angel!
*Camael fired from his Peacemaker, right into the blob of molten gold, his six shots pinning its entire mass to the wall.*
*However... This did manage to buy me some time!*
Camael: What...?!
*By the time Camael realized what was going on, I had already freed both Sorami and Lilith.*
*The only purpose of the molten gold was to distract the angels standing guard near the girls. All I needed was one brief moment where their awestruck gazes were directed at the raging battle.*
*The angels had soon regained their composure. Sorami hastily scurried behind my back as Lilith took her stand right next to me.*
Lilith: Geez Louise. I may be immortal and everything, but that doesn't mean I don't feel pain, Camael.
Camael: Lilith. I am in no mood for your nonsense. Hand over Raziel and leave this place. You're another victim of the Calamity, same as us. You have no obligation to protect her.
Lilith: Hmm... Oh, okay. So that's how you see it. Guess it can't be helped, then.
Camael: What exactly are you trying to say?
Lilith: Just a couple ol' things I'd like to correct. First off: I may also be a victim of the Divine Calamity, but it's been kinder to me compared to you angels.
Lilith: Well, I mean, our home's been submerged and all, y'know? I gotta admit, the thought of just getting a nuclear submarine and living in that did kinda cross my mind, though!
Camael: Enough with your nonsense, Lilith!
Lilith: Oh? But I'm _always_ serious! Besides, this old brain of mine just can't seem to shut up about something.

Lilith: Look. Sure, maybe Samael's right. Maybe you really did _accidentally_ cause this whole Divine Calamity. But that's all you did, y'know?
*Lilith took a terrifying revelation about my past, then simply threw the entire thing out the window without hesitation.*
Lilith: Sure, I don't know your motive, whether or not you did it on purpose or with the intention to harm others... Well, I guess those lost memories of yours should have have all the answers.
Lilith: Besides, you think a bookworm angel like you could end the world? I mean, let's be real. If the world's gonna end, it has to be by the hand of a bunch of flashy villains!
Sorami: Way to go, Lilith...
*I felt the same way, unsure if she was trying to cheer me up or simply insult me. Still... it did make me get my act together somewhat.*
Raziel: I don't know any of that. Not even what I did that day. But...
*He told me not to flee. He told me to look reality straight in the eyes, accepting whatever I saw reflected in them.*
Raziel: But I'm doing my best to come up with a solution. I will do the best I can to set things right.
*What I had to do... was hardly anything special, really.*
Lilith: I'd say that's more than enough, dontcha think?
Sorami: It's hard to tell if you stopped caring or just gave up.
Raziel: I will set out for the sixth stratum, then the seventh. And finally, I'll open the gates of Heaven. Do you still wish to accompany me?
Sorami: I do.
Lilith: Sorami, I think it'd be better if you stayed... well, actually, it doesn't matter either way. The mental contamination's getting pretty bad here at Pandora, too. You doing alright now?
*Sorami gave her head a light bonk.*
Sorami: Hmm. Guess I'm not sensitive enough for this kinda stuff. All I'm getting is a light headache, but that's about it!
*From the way she smiled at us, I doubted she was telling a lie.*
Lilith: Huh, so you really are fine. If we had more time I would've loved to take a look at that brain of yours.
Sorami: M-My brain? And how exactly would you do that...?
Lilith: Surgery, duh. We'd open that sucker right up!
Sorami: Ghnyaaa...!!
*Lilith chuckled at Sorami's exaggerated reaction. Somehow... I felt the atmosphere relax a bit.*
*I wished to know the truth. I could not allow myself to die until then. I could never atone for what I did. My only choice for redemption... would be death.*
*And that, in itself, didn't particularly bother me. I would be content with it. Still, I first needed to recover my memories.*
Raziel: Ah...!
*I spotted someone running our way. The moment I did... a surge of joy, like a fire freshly lit, began to brush against my heart in waves.*
*Feeling such a welling of emotions as sinful, I instinctively averted my gaze from him — from Tendou Setsuna.*
*Joy was sin. I had to... seal those feelings away. As insignificant as such an act may have been... this was, nonetheless, worthy of penance.*
*I had finally managed to regroup with the others. Raziel averted her gaze from me, appearing somewhat restless.*
Lilith: Right-o. Now that we got Setsuna back, could you guys hear me out for a bit?
*Lilith produced a short series of claps, prompting all three of us to look at her. After confirming that she had our attention, the demon began to speak.*
Lilith: So, umm. Well, there's no nice way to put this, but basically we're being hunted by the angels and demons commanded by Camael and Astaroth, respectively.
Sorami: Wow, amazing! Just like Mr. Kimble!
*Sorami began to applaud.*
Lilith: Geez, why you gotta be so old-fashioned? Anyway, word on the street is these two have reached the sixth stratum. So... we might as well be off.
*Lilith pointed towards the ceiling.*
Lilith: Our last stop is pretty clear: Heaven. Well, we may end up dead or insane or worse, but if that comes to pass, I'm sure Setsuna here will do what needs to be done.
*Lilith's smile remained unflinching as she said all these relatively extreme things.*
Setsuna: I, too, intended to do just that. I'll travel to the very ends of Tokyo Babel, no matter the cost.
Lilith: Yup. With that said, if any one of you feel like your head's about to split open or get this sudden urge to hurt someone, make sure to let me know! I'll dispose of you lickety-split.
*Lilith reminded us of the grim severity of our situation in her usual, playful tone. That once a mind had been contaminated, the person in question — even if they were a friend or a comrade — had to be eliminated.*
*However...*
*I could still remember Gethel, Kurou Miyako, and Uriel.*
*I recalled how they acted as they surrendered their minds to madness. A gruesome, terrifying sight... even more so should it ever befall one of our own.*
Setsuna: Acknowledged.
Raziel: Understood.
Sorami: Hm... I think I'll manage, though. I mean, it's gonna be just fine.
Lilith: Hm. Sorami, I know your optimism usually burns brighter than the sun, but somehow I'm not convinced...
Sorami: What's _that_ supposed to mean?
Lilith: Well, whatevs. Anyway, time to get going for real. Heaven awaits!
Sorami: Let's gooo!
*Sorami enthusiastically thrust her fist into the air. Urged by a sudden onset of nostalgia, I followed her cue and did the same.*
Lilith: Still... I thought we were being hunted, but there's not an angel or demon in sight.
Setsuna: They didn't bring out their full forces, so Camael was able to repel them.
Raziel: And the demons...?
Lilith: Hm...
Sorami: Oh, they seem to be fighting.
*Sorami lazily cast her gaze at the sky, her transcendent eyes detecting "something" not even angels or demons could see.*
Lilith: Fighting? Who's fighting who?
*In response to Lilith's inquiry, Sorami placed her hands slightly above her eyes, squinting to see better.*
Sorami: It's probably Mr. Astaroth against...
*In the confines of his office, Astaroth found himself face to face with that certain man.*
*He produced a cup of coffee from somewhere, which Belial graciously accepted.*
Belial: Huh. This thing's pretty bitter.
Astaroth: I prefer it this way compared to the sugary mess they serve in Hell.
Belial: That so? Well, I like it sweet myself, so yeah.
*The two carried on their conversation like a pair of old friends.*
*Once he had gulped down the last drops of the coffee, Astaroth set his cup aside and turned to the other man.*
Astaroth: In any event... What brings you here, Belial?
Belial: Oh, nothing serious, really. I took a quick peek at Camael and Setsuna's fight and the boy said some really interesting stuff at the end there.
*Astaroth let out a sigh.*
Astaroth: Tendou Setsuna is a criminal aided by Lilith. Maybe you should have interfered.
*Indeed, the demon lord was right. Belial ought to have interfered.*
Belial: Yeah, I'm sorry. You're right. But who was I to butt into a heated one-on-one battle between two men?
Astaroth: I should've remembered you were that kind of man. However, as you will recall, Japan's laws label duels as a crime.
Belial: Our very existence is pretty damn sinful in itself, get what I'm sayin'? You know, like... _hiding the very culprit behind the Divine Calamity_.
*The truly fearsome part about Belial's declaration was that he uttered it in the same joking tone he had employed until now.*
*The office's tranquil atmosphere never wavered. Belial's coffee, too, remained pleasantly hot. The demon lord displayed not a trace of anger.*
Astaroth: Care to elaborate on that?
Belial: Let's hear your explanation, Astaroth.
Astaroth: My explanation? Very well. Anything else?
Belial: I'm quite the greedy guy, you know. Personally, I'd love to know everything you did these past few thousand years, from beginning to end.
Astaroth: I'm afraid that would take a considerable amount of time.
Belial: Why don't you just tell me how it started, then?
*Astaroth's laugh chimed in the air like a tiny bell.*
Astaroth: Very well. I shall confess. Let us say that I was responsible for the Divine Calamity. That Raziel was merely a cue, nothing more.
Belial: Huh. It's a crime to give a false testimony, y'know.
Astaroth: Oh, but I have committed far greater crimes than that.
Belial: Alright, gotcha. So basically... you're the mastermind behind all this, huh?
*There was a shift in the air then, pushing aside all traces of the room's previously soothing atmosphere; an ominous chill that permeated one's very bones, befitting the lowest layers of Hell.*
Astaroth: Me, the mastermind...? An amusing thought. _Am I truly the mastermind behind all this?_
*Just as his seething bloodlust reached its climax, Belial let out a booming guffaw. To Astaroth, this was a grave sign.*
*Belial's expression may have been a mask of composure, yet a faint glimmer of the demon lord's genuine rage shone through his facade.*
*No — it was, in fact, something more than that. Mere "anger" was no fiercer than a child's sparkler compared to the swamp of dark, murderous contempt lurking behind it.*
*Anger and bloodlust were different emotions. The former abided by instinct, the latter by logic and reason.*
*And Belial's reasoning whispered the following into his ears. "Make Astaroth part with that scheming head of his right here, right now. Then hurl it into the bubbling cauldron of Hell and let it burn alongside his vile ambitions."*
Astaroth: I'm not expecting you to understand.
Belial: Yeah, I wouldn't count on it.
*Belial inclined his head to the side, his neck giving off an audible crack. He then touched his thumb to his middle finger...*
*...and snapped. A moment later, an explosive blast hit Astaroth and room alike.*
*All Belial did was ignite the magical energies exuding from his body.*
*He required no complex incantation, nor a fixed set of movements — he didn't even need to focus his mind on producing the explosion. He simply decided that snapping his fingers would release his magical powers, and that was it.*
*An average demon could produce but a feeble breeze with such a method. In Belial's case, however, its power rivaled that of a small nuclear missile.*
*Naturally, by adjusting the vector of the attack, Belial himself received no damage from the blast.*
*In any event, most angels or demons would have not only died, but been outright atomized by his attack. It was simply that powerful.*
*Similarly, the demon on the receiving end of the attack was no fledgling, either. Far from it.*
Astaroth: Your magic hasn't changed one bit. It still sings a melancholic tune.
*Astaroth came forward, not a single stain blemishing his unharmed clothes.*
Belial: Melancholic, my ass. You sure like to talk shit.
*Belial showed no hint of surprise at this. After all, the man before him was the so-called Crowned Prince of Hell, a top class demon lord heralded as the sovereign ruler of the world.*
*Smiling, Astaroth gave his fellow demon a tap on the shoulder. The whole action took but a fraction of a second.*
*To say it happened _in the blink of an eye_ would be an appropriate way to describe it... if Belial had the time to blink.*
*Astaroth's technique relied on neither teleporting, nor stopping time. He was simply fast enough that his movements remained unseen by the naked eye.*
Astaroth: Would a grand and graceful bout with magic and sorcery be to your liking? Or would you, perhaps, prefer...
*Astaroth thrust his balled fist in front of Belial's eyes.*
Astaroth: ...to brawl like mortal men, fists crashing with bone? I shan't say a word. You decide.
*Belial's lips curled to a broad grin.*
Belial: As you wish! It's gotta be magic... no, forget that, we're using our fists!
*A split-second before Belial could hit Astaroth in the face, the latter responded with a counter, smashing his fist into the other's jaw.*
Belial: Wh-What the...?!
*Belial's technique was nonexistent. A more pertinent way to put it would be to say that in most cases, neither angels, nor demons, possessed skills that relied on their physical bodies.*
*All they needed was magic, as well as the skills their respective weapons granted them. Astaroth, however, dabbled in the art of boxing for a hundred or so years.*
*He was a hardcore enthusiast who followed — and studied — with great interest the gradual evolution of mankind's boxing matches over the years.*
Astaroth: That was a counter. A strike utilizing the incoming power of the opponent in order to multiply one's own. Failure could be fatal, but if pulled off successfully, it ends up a deadly strike. Does it not strike a chord in your heart?
Belial: Sorry to burst your bubble, but I _hate_ gambling!
*Belial lunged at his opponent, raising his fist to strike; Astaroth couldn't help but view his technique as that of an out-of-control dump truck.*
*Belial was about to deliver a punch of considerable strength. Astaroth would once again position himself to prepare a counter.*
*A moment later, Astaroth found his vision clouded by stars, almost like fireworks — Belial had just given him a headbutt akin to getting hit by a freight train.*
Belial: I wouldn't underestimate me, if I were you. I may lack your technique, but I have a millennium's worth of experience with street brawls!!
*Indeed, Belial knew no elaborate fighting techniques. All he did was lower his own physical power to the level of a mortal's as he partook in brawl after brawl for a good thousand years.*
Astaroth: My, my. Hardly a hobby for a jurist!
*Fists flew, crashed into muscle and got repelled. With every vicious exchange, Astaroth felt an electric current of pain ravage his body — yet his heart fluttered with joy, enjoying every second of it.*
*Belial felt the same. His fist cried out in agony every time it tasted the opponent's flesh, yet never once did he consider stopping.*
Belial: So? What made you come up with this bullshit plan, huh?
*Belial cried out as the other buried his fist deep in his abdomen. Even as Belial launched punch after punch, each powerful enough to pulverize a tank, Astaroth continued on with an unfaltering smile.*
Astaroth: First and foremost, my own selfishness. Secondly... a promise I made to a beloved friend!
*Belial lowered his guard for a heartbeat upon hearing the other demon's words, prompting Astaroth to deliver a kick to his head.*
*The attack annihilated a deserted classroom, blowing Belial clean through a wall and outside to the athletics field.*
Belial: (Shit... even without his magic, he sure packs a punch...)
*Angels and demons boasted of physical prowess far exceeding that of mortals. The base of their strength, however, was due primarily to magic.*
*To put it in simple terms, the more magic they possess, the higher ranked they were.*
*At least that was usually the case. Belial himself was a powerful, war-hardened combatant. A veteran warrior and lord of demons who survived battle after battle in their great war against the angels.*
*However, Astaroth's physical abilities were, in a word... abnormal. He may very well possess the strength of a demon lord _without relying on magic one bit_.*
Belial: Man... some fight I've picked...
*Belial had given up on defeating the other demon in a fistfight. That, however, didn't mean he gave up on victory altogether. After a brief sigh, he summoned his weapon.*
Belial: The trident that defies language — Albers' Fork!
*Belial looked over his trident. Astaroth, upon arriving at the athletics field, exhaled a sigh of awe as he beheld the weapon.*
Astaroth: So that is your weapon. I had heard the rumors, but never once did I imagine it to be this terrifying, this beautiful.
*The trident's shape was beyond unordinary, its steel handle covered in inscriptions of both blessings and curses writ in a myriad languages.*
*The real problem, however, were the spikes at its tip. Three in total, true to its name as a trident. However...*
*With each rotation Belial gave his trusty weapon, the number of blades on its tip shifted and changed.*
*From three to two, from two to four — it was impossible to tell. Abiding to no fixed law, the blades continued to change and change ever so subtly, even after Belial had stopped spinning the weapon.*
Belial: This is a weapon in direct correspondence with my raison d'etre. And it's more than enough to carry me to victory in battle.
*Belial's trident was an ever-prevalent mass of contradictions, imbued with both prayers aimed to save another and curses uttered to cause harm.*
*Despite carrying the name of a trident, its sharpened tips freely changed their numbers from one to nine.*
*The rules guiding it were by no means strict or regulated. If anything, it was ambiguous beyond measure, for the law itself was never without a tinge of bias to color its palette.*
*Let us assume that a man had killed another in cold blood. Whether his victim was a child or an adult, the fact that he _murdered someone_ changed precious little.*
*But what if said adult was a wretched blackguard hated by many? What if the child had been killed in a way so gruesome that no man could silence his compassion and pity?*
*The crime of the latter far eclipsed that of the former. The law is never free from the human element, always leaving a trace of ambiguity in its wake.*
*A loose string pulled at both ends, with each side wanting to expand their own territory. Such was the battlefield of the law, its landscape pregnant with elements defying linguistic expression.*
Astaroth: Hm. A splendid weapon indeed.
*After Astaroth gave a respectful bow, Belial gestured with his palm, inviting the other to battle.*
Belial: Come down here, Astaroth.
*A bitter smile crept onto Astaroth's lips.*
*He shook his head, then shrugged.*
Astaroth: May I remind you that I'm a demon? Fighting fair and square isn't exactly my forte.
*A quick glance revealed three demons standing in the window.*
Belial: You bastard...
Astaroth: On another day, I may have savored the idea of dying a glorious death in fair combat. However, I wish to remain here a touch longer, to see with my own eyes the final days of this apocalypse.
Belial: Hah. So you're basically pissin' your pants so hard at the thought of getting your ass kicked in a fair fight that all you can do is send a bunch of braindead cannon fodder thugs my way, huh?
Belial: You can't fool me with your flowery-ass speeches, ya hear me?!
*Belial's roaring guffaw reverberated in the air, earning contemptuous looks from the three demons. Astaroth went on with unwavering composure.*
Astaroth: I take it you're displeased?
Belial: Hell yeah I am. But... I guess I'd do the same thing in your shoes.
Astaroth: See?
Belial: Right then. Baal, Agares, and... well, who cares. You there. I ain't got much time to spare on playing with you, so do me a favor and come at me all at once.
*Astaroth's henchmen — or to be more precise, Lucifuge's own confidants — were called Baal, Agares, and Marbas.*
*Baal had three heads, one that looked like a frog, another like a cat, and yet another like a cowardly king. His lower body was that of a giant spider.*
*Agares was an elderly man with soft features, riding a crocodile while holding a hawk in one hand. Finally, Marbas was a person with a lion's head.*
*Each of them commanded a legion of demons, so it came as no surprise that Belial's provocation would anger them.*
Baal / Man B: How dare you insult us, you rotten excuse for a jurist...!
*All three lunged at Belial in unison, none of them showing any restraint. Baal released all his magical power through his three mouths, Agares sent his crocodile to battle, while Marbas bared his lion-fangs at the demon lord, ready to tear him to bloody shreds.*
*Each demon had their own unique skills to them. They had no intention of unleashing their raison d'etre — their trump cards — right at the start of battle.*
*If all three of them attacked at once, the chances of victory were high. Furthermore, the possibility remained that one demon would engulf the other two in his attack.*
*It was a severe, ultimately lethal mistake. They ended up using conventional tactics against him.*
*The man before them was Belial. A being whose name carried the meaning of "The Worthless One" and was scorned as a demon lord most vile.*
Belial: Love in carnage, friendship in crucifixion, stalwart armor in sharpened steel, future in the past. Sing the victory ode of fleeting reality!
Astaroth: This isn't looking good.
Belial: The 68th of Goetia — Arbiter of Hope!
*Lacking any hesitation whatsoever, Belial had just unleashed his own raison d'etre.*
Baal / Man B: Aiieee...!
*His trident was awash with limitless possibilities, an entanglement of chaotically complex emotions, phenomena, and situations.*
*Fixing that into a momentary "reality" caused an explosion colossal enough to dwarf even the most powerful of magicks.*
*In fact, the word explosion might not even do it justice.*
*The very air visibly trembled in a hundred meter radius as Belial swung his terrible instrument.*
*That very same area had been completely eradicated without a trace, leaving only Astaroth in the background to exhale a tired sigh.*
*Needless to say, his three underlings had completely perished.*
Astaroth: I see... Wonderful! Small wonder they praised you as invincible during the war with the angels. So the idea is the consolidation of potentiality into a singular point in order to evoke a strike of complete annihilation.
Belial: I've shown you my trump card, sure... _but that doesn't mean jack_.
*Belial's words rang true. He may have openly displayed his raison d'etre, but that didn't mean he also revealed how one could effectively combat it.*
*What he did back then was cause a clash between a myriad possibilities — the possible and impossible, the be and not be, the is and isn't — thus birthing a phenomenon of complete annihilation.*
*Reflecting or disabling such an attack was impossible, for when he unleashed it, an enormous volume of data carrying "void" manifested at the same time, purging all existence in its path.*
*The demon lord Belial, jurist of Hell, his position demanding him to stand as judge for the wicked and the just, black and white, hope and despair.*
*Such was his raison d'etre.*
*Belial's faith in his own attack was absolute and unwavering. His weapon struck down countless angels and would be the end of Astaroth as well, he thought.*
*Unfortunately...*
*Belial, a demon lord himself, had ever once fought another demon lord before_.*
*And that was indeed why he failed to take notice of the obvious — the true nature of Astaroth's own raison d'etre.*
Astaroth: You have my gratitude, Belial. I have observed your raison d'etre with great interest... which is precisely why I can declare this. _You will die here_.
Belial: Oh?
*Belial gave a mocking jeer. Astaroth, on the other hand, extended his hand towards the other, almost as if he wanted a handshake.*
Astaroth: Would you be so kind as to show me that technique of yours again?
Belial: You serious?
Astaroth: Why, of course I am. I assure you, the mental contamination has yet to plunge my mind into madness.
*Astaroth did not flinch at all. Even after seeing Belial's attack a moment before, he remained calm and composed.*
Belial: Fine, be my guest.
*Belial was confident that Astaroth had no means of overpowering him or his technique.*
*And even if, by some miracle, he did, it would not be an issue. Not at all.*
*Belial — being Belial — prepared an ace up his sleeve, one that the other demon could never evade.*
*Belial gave his Albers' Fork a handful of spins.*
*With each turn of the trident the heavens shook and the earth trembled as the demon lord's weapon engulfed all around it.*
*The infinite expanses of space. The laws of nature, bound by infinity. The world's most powerful weapons and armor. And he who birthed a false truth, an untrue reality.*
*And so his blade sang, encompassing all contradictions of the cosmos. Belial controlled it through the decree known as "law."*
Belial: Let infinity converge to finity. Let power unbound and wretched weakness be converted to numbers. Let truth and falsehood stand upon an unswerving median.
*With the instantaneous convergence of Belial's magic, the wind itself had died to a calm. Yet all Astaroth did was stand his ground.*
*That wasn't entirely true, though.*
*He was whispering something under his breath. Naturally, Belial heard every single word, but realized they were utterly meaningless.*
*The trident trembled in anticipation, waiting for its master's command. The time for release was nigh.*
Belial: The 68th of Goetia — Arbiter of Hope!
*An attack that would annihilate all and nothing it touched — its next target was Astaroth.*
*Surprisingly enough, Astaroth seemed in no mind to even try to evade. He simply stood his ground, arms crossed over his chest.*
*Astaroth's whisper echoed the following...*
Astaroth: I shall unleash my true form. Be resurrected, O realms of Hades.
*Astaroth and Belial — much like Baal and the other two — possessed a form befitting a true demon, terrifying and repulsive, having once haunted the imagination of mankind.*
*Yet taking such a form made it exceedingly difficult to exist among humans. Here in Tokyo Babel, where one's magical and mental capacity was of vital importance, the vast majority of demons took on humanoid forms.*
*Nonetheless, Astaroth now saw it fit to revert to his original form.*
*Naturally, it held no particular meaning. He did not take this form to become stronger or faster.*
*Nor did he do it in order to intimidate Belial, for what would be the point? The jurist of Hell was a demon lord, same as Astaroth.*
*So why, then, did he transform? Why did he choose to return to his original appearance?*
*It all became clear once Belial's attack had died down.*
*Belial's strike of complete annihilation, the Arbiter of Hope, had completely engulfed Astaroth.*
*It gave him complete, thorough destruction... Or at least it should have.*
Belial: Wh-What the...?!
Astaroth: Belial, you have committed a grave mistake. You are the jurist of Hell — and as such, you believed yourself able to consolidate all that existed under the sun.
*Astaroth had reverted to his original form, one befitting a so-called Crowned Prince of Hell.*
*He rode atop a blue, two-headed dragon. His right arm was clad in a steel serpent, the crimson of blood blotting his six wings while snake-like scales littered his exposed skin.*
Astaroth: Have you forgotten, Belial? We demon lords were once gods — I, in particular, originate from Ishtar, the goddess of love. The majority of demon lords, by their very nature, are vessels of contradiction.
Belial: ...!
Astaroth: The consolidation of potentiality in order to evoke complete annihilation. A strike that gave you invincibility against angels, mortals, and lesser demons alike.
Astaroth: But I'm different. I carry the weight of contradiction upon my shoulders, blessings and curses alike coursing through my very being.
*Astaroth's tone took on a melancholic edge — to a surprising degree, in fact. The dragon's twin heads, as well as Astaroth's own serpent-claw hand were now directed at Belial.*
Belial: I screwed up, didn't I...
Astaroth: Belial. Know that I considered you a trusted comrade, one I would have wished at my side at Tokyo Babel. And yet... my desire to live is greater still.
Belial: So you threw everything away for another ten seconds of this life?
*Astaroth's lips slithered into a snake-like grin.*
Astaroth: I wish to remain true to him... till the bitter end.
*Serpent and dragon roared in unison.*
Astaroth: As a final gift, allow me to reveal my raison d'etre to you. It's "affectionate hate."
*To love someone to death. Yet at the same time, loathe them to the point of murder.*
*Such was his innate duality; a demon lord harboring a fundamental contradiction.*
*The carrier of an ultimate contradiction that no arbiter could ever hope to consolidate. That was the raison d'etre of Astaroth.*
Belial: I see... I'm no match for somethin' like that.
*Belial let a faint smile overtake his features as he accepted the reality of his imminent doom.*
*There was nothing left for him to do. Nothing left to convey. Certainly, he would be left with regret at letting Astaroth live here, but...*
*...as the spiraling blade impaled his body, Belial — still a smile on his lips — uttered the following in a low breath.*
Belial: I got no regrets. The rest is up to you... _commander of angels_.
*Astaroth was rendered paralyzed. Even without turning around, he knew something was being aimed at the back of his head.*
Astaroth: So it's you.
Camael: Yeah. It's me.
*The angel pulled the trigger, propelling a .45 Long Colt bullet into the back of Astaroth's head without missing its mark, thus constraining the demon lord's body.*
*Astaroth's contradiction had been shattered to pieces by Camael's rage.*
Camael: Feel Retribution. You are worthy of Death, demon.
Astaroth: ......!
*Astaroth, once again in his human form, collapsed onto his knees like a prisoner awaiting execution, a bitter smile coloring his lips.*
Astaroth: And will you grant me death?
Camael: I will.
Astaroth: It is a thing I once desired, yet still I know its pain, its terror...
Camael: You desired it?
Astaroth: Camael. Know that slaying me shall not halt the apocalypse. Tokyo Babel will fall, the earth will sink to the bottom of the ocean, while the Gates of Heaven will remain forever closed.
Camael: So I should let you go? Is that it?
Astaroth: Oh, hardly. I merely wished to see the final hours of this dying world. How about you?
Camael: I have not discarded hope.
Astaroth: Oh?
Camael: There will be plenty of time to think about that afterwards.
Astaroth: Hm.
*Smiling, Astaroth exhaled a sigh.*
Camael: Well, then. Farewell, my friend.
*The angel's executioner's blade claimed Astaroth's head, which then slowly tumbled onto the ground.*
Belial: Heh... Got your comeuppance, you did.
*Once Belial had confirmed Astaroth's final moments, he found himself liberated from pain. He closed his eyes, at long last surrendering himself to the embrace of death.*
Camael: So Belial's gone, too...
*The word "gone" wasn't particularly accurate in this case. They did not "go" anywhere — they perished for good, never to return.*
*Camael wondered how far Adam had made it. The angel once believed that Adam opening the Gates of Heaven would bring an end to their hardships, but that train of thought had to be amended.*
*Opening the Gates of Heaven would solve nothing. In a predicament as dire as theirs, the angels were faced with a choice.*
Camael: Raziel. Tell me, Raziel. Can you really do _that?_ Can you?

*I felt so sleepy. At the same time, though, it had been a while since I was left alone with my thoughts.*
*However, I had but one thing on my mind. Only one thing important enough to fill my thoughts.*
*Raziel.*
*Tall and exuding an aura of confidence, yet at the same time, a bit of a crybaby and prone to spacing out.*
*I loved her from the bottom of my heart. Leaving her behind was the single greatest regret of my life.*
*Moments before my eyelids fluttered shut, I had a vision. Or perhaps a glimpse into the future.*
*I believed it to be the latter. I hoped, prayed for that to be the case.*
*For the future I looked upon...*
*...held the promise of a bright and brave tomorrow.*

Sorami: What an awe-inspiring lunch...!
*I knew next to nothing about boxed lunches, or food in general, but the assortment in Oshiba Hagane's box was indeed impressive.*
*Delicious looking chicken teriyaki. Carefully arranged slices of cucumber, carrot, and omelette. Browned sausages and mushrooms. A part of it was likely leftovers of the chikuzenni he had for yesterday's dinner.*
Oshiba: Oh, you can have some if you like.
Sorami: Really? I'll take some teriyaki, then...
*Following her example, I too decided to request something. It would likely give him a bad impression if I didn't show interest in his cuisine at this point.*
*...It wasn't like I was actually curious about the taste. Not in the slightest.*
Setsuna: Can I try some of your chikuzenni?
Oshiba: Sure, help yourself.
*He gave me a nod with a friendly smile. That as my cue, I guided my chopsticks to the lotus root, picked it up, and chewed on it.*
*Salty-sweet taste extended across my tongue as I bit through the pleasantly crunchy flesh of the vegetable. It was indeed quite tasty.*
Oshiba: How was it?
Setsuna: Very good.
Sorami: ...You're pretty good, Oshiba.
Oshiba: Ehehe, thank you. Um, it might be a bit strange for me to say this myself, having prepared the meal and all, but I have a small stomach so you can help yourselves to as much as you want. I couldn't finish this alone, anyway.
Sorami: What a great guy...! Have this rice ball as a token of my gratitude.
Oshiba: Ah, I already have my own rice, so: no, thanks.
*Oshiba Hagane didn't hesitate to turn her down for a second.*
Sorami: Stone cold, huh. Well, I guess I'll just help myself to your things, then...
Setsuna: Did you manufacture all of this yourself?
Oshiba: Yeah.

*...Was that so?*
Sorami: ...Huh?
*Sorami glared at Oshiba Hagane with a dumbfounded expression.*
Oshiba: I mean, it's obvious, isn't it? None of the dishes in this boxed lunch are inexplicable. Everything from how to slice the ingredients to how to brown them can be found in books.
*Oshiba Hagane's face was a mask of nonchalance.*
Oshiba: ...An _established fact_. You don't need past experience to comprehend it.
*I could feel my chest oddly rile up to his words.*
*Past experience was pointless?*
*Wasn't that— Wasn't that an extremely dangerous thought?*
Sorami: ...You're wrong.
Oshiba: Hm?

*Oshiba Hagane stole a glance at us.*

Sorami: That's...
Oshiba: We are destined to live in the future. And the past has no place there.
*He declared it with unwavering conviction.*
Setsuna: Is this related to your mindset of only being interested in the future?
Oshiba: Yes. I only care about living in the future.
*Sorami considered the floor in silence. And I finally understood what he meant. He was only interested in the future, but not dreaming about it.*
*It wasn't the type of vague future you imagine thinking about what you want to be.*
*His was merely a matter of fact time of one second, one day, one year, or even a hundred years after the present. And Oshiba Hagane only cared about living in it.*
*There was obviously something wrong with this idea. People couldn't live solely in the future. We had to constantly face the hurdles of the present to entertain the idea of reaching the point beyond.*
*...However.*
*Oshiba Hagane, nonetheless, decided to live "only" in the future. And... it was more of a delusion than a simple whim in this situation.*
*Was future itself his raison d'etre?*
Setsuna: I have one question.
Oshiba: Go ahead.

*He didn't hesitate for a second.*
Oshiba: To become a correct being.
Sorami: Correct... being?
Oshiba: My dream is to live correctly in a correct world according to correct time as a correct being.
*His answer was neither overly mind-blowing, nor did it particularly make much sense. It was a vague, obscure thing that one couldn't quite put your finger on.*
*After a short pause, Oshiba Hagane suddenly looked up at us and opened his mouth with a hint of proudness about himself.*
Oshiba: Well, I didn't expect you to understand.

Oshiba: Well, thought so.
Sorami: But I'll try my best to think about it.
*Oshiba Hagane's chopsticks stopped moving.*
Oshiba: Think about what?
Sorami: I'll think about what you've said. I can't promise I'll understand, or comprehend it, but I promise I'll think long and hard about it!
*For the first time, a hint of genuine emotion colored Oshiba Hagane's features. He uttered the words through his teeth, as if with contempt.*
Oshiba: Like you ever could.
*After lunch we all returned to the classroom in silence. I spent the remainder of the school day thinking.*
*About Oshiba Hagane. About Kugutsu Sorami.*
*To live in the future. I couldn't say he was wrong, exactly, but his philosophy was too... well, too one-sided.*
*It kind of reminded me of how people, after falling in love, tended to lose all care for the world save for the target of their affection.*
*Incomprehensible. It was the only conclusion I could come up with in the end.*
Sorami: "......"
*Sorami's mind didn't seem to be in the real world, either. She was probably trying to keep the promise she made to Oshiba Hagane earlier today.*
*I kept thinking. Even if I couldn't understand it, couldn't comprehend it... I still tried to swallow it.*
*But it was likely a vain effort. Indeed, there were people in this world that were impossible to see eye to eye with.*
*And Oshiba Hagane was likely one of them. There was no way a being that only lived in the future could communicate with those shackled to the past.*
*Such was my conclusion. And so, I refused to dwell any longer on the matter.*
*Sorami, however, continued to ponder.*
Belial: "Kugutsu Sorami. Kugutsu Sorami."

*At least that was how it used to be in my world.*

*People perfectly understanding each other was a fantasy of the hoplessly naive.*
*Sorami didn't seem too thrilled with my conclusion.*

*She gave me a short but seemingly relieved "I see."*

*We proceeded to stroll towards the night duty room.*
*And once we reached our destination, we found a tracksuit-wearing demon and an angel playing video games.*

*...She was probably brought up in a peaceful world.*
*Well, it surely must have had its fair share of global problems, but the concept of expecting a better future from tomorrow seemed to be a common sense matter there at least.*
*My world was not like that. My world was that of eternal night, a world where morning would never come no matter the amount of time you spent waiting.*
*It was a world where everyone longed for the light.*
*Oh.*

*The celestial hierarchy.*

*Upper Triad was the home to seraphim, cherubim, and thrones.*

*Lower Triad — principalities, archangels, and angels.*

*They looked completely natural together. It seemed like they were already in a world of their own.*
Sorami: Yeah, seems those two are doing quite well.
*It appeared Sorami had spotted the direction of my gaze.*
Setsuna: But all Adam is doing is repeating "yeah" over and over again.
*I did not think he was doing a good job was what I wanted to say, but Sorami's fingers dug into my flesh before I could finish. It hurt very much.*
Sorami: How come you're always so hostile to Adam?
Setsuna: I don't know myself. It's probably something genetic.
*It was like... I couldn't understand it myself.*
Sorami: Hmm... They do say that people tend to hate those similar to themselves.
Setsuna: ...Sorami?
Sorami: Ah, um... Don't be angry, alright? I've just been thinking that you and Adam are kind of similar, you know.
Setsuna: Mhm? How are we similar exactly?
Sorami: Uh... It's just a feeling, you know; you two just kind of feel similar to me. I don't have any concrete evidence or anything if you're asking for that.
*I did not think I hated him exactly. Rather, I simply couldn't acknowledge his existence for some odd reason.*
Sorami: H-Hey, stop glaring at him like that. If you keep doing it he'll—
Adam: Hm? What is it?
*Noticing my gaze, Adam returned it with a quizzical look. ...Now I had to talk with him.*
Setsuna: Don't mind it. I was just thinking if we were similar or not.
Adam: You and I?
*Adam dismissed the remark with a smirk.*
Adam: We cannot possibly be similar.
Setsuna: ...Ah.
*Wait. If you considered the circumstances of Adam's making, and my own origins...*
*I didn't want to admit it... ...but the core of our being might have been, after all, quite similar.*
Setsuna: Yeah. I think you're right.
Adam: Of course.
*Eve was glancing from me to Adam and back with confused eyes. We started talking to each other out of nowhere which seemed to have taken her off guard.*
Adam: That aside, we have been walking for quite a while now. How far is this place of yours?
*We have indeed spent a considerable amount of time walking. I tried recalling Lilith's advice on how I should've done this.*
*Um, first I should— I grasped the air around myself to no avail, until I suddenly remembered Sorami's eyes.*
Setsuna: Sorami. Sorry for asking this out of nowhere, but could you try looking for a boundary line around here?
Sorami: Ah, the loop spot? Roger. Um... Boot!
*As I nodded, Sorami, reacting with "just give me a second," proceeded to activate Gethel's eyes.*
*Her eyes sparkled in gold, and went on to perceive the whole world.*
Sorami: Um... Ah, it's here.
*Sorami poked thin air a few times. After a few seconds of careful observation, I finally spotted a faint membrane of magic stretching across the scenery at the tip of her finger.*
Setsuna: Um... First I should take hold of this space, and...
*I sank the tips of my fingers into the magical membrane, and seemed to have grasped something I could not quite define.*
Setsuna: ...and I should take this off.
*And so, a chunk of space slid apart. As I removed the inner wall's plate, a sight of boundless ocean and sky assaulted my eyes.*
Sorami: Oh, so we are going outside, after all.
Eve: You knew we were going here?
Sorami: Not really, but I guessed Lilith might have meant this place. It has a nice view and all. But, you know...
*Sorami gave me a quick glance.*
Sorami: Don't you find strolling through this place a bit... sad?
Setsuna: According to Lilith, there's someone that should come pick us up here.
*Lilith told me it was going to be all right multiple times, all the while giggling meaningfully. Now that I thought about it, I should have noticed there was something fishy about the whole affair.*
Sorami: Hmm... Someone to pick us up?
Eve: Someone to meet us outside of Tokyo Babel? Oh, could it be?
*We all turned to Eve.*
Adam: You know who it might be?
Eve: Yes, if I recall correctly—
*There was no need for her to continue, as after a booming roar of splashing water, a skyscraper-like structure suddenly emerged from the depths of the ocean below us.*
*Or at least I thought it was a structure; the notion was proven wrong on my second glance.*
*The rough dark green surface of the "skyscraper" looked like the hide of some animal. The thing was so huge its body didn't fit into my vision.*
Eve: The master of primordial seas of chaos currently in charge of the submerged Hell. The dragon — the giant king of serpents lurking in the ocean surrounding Tokyo Babel—
Adam: Leviathan...!
Sorami: The hell is this thing?
*Sorami's tone did not have even a hint of her usual vivacity to it. It seemed the sudden occurrence was enough to positively stupefy even her. Not that I wasn't as stupefied by the display.*
*As we stood at the edge of the wall, carefully considering the thing, a deafening roar from above hit us like thunder.*
Leviathan: Gyahaha! Welcome to my establishment!
The Two: Establishment?!
*The fact that it talked was surprising enough, but the content of its words was even more flabbergasting.*
Leviathan: With that said, allow me to present the location of today's double date: my own humble back!
Eve: Oh, my.
Adam: Leviathan's... back?
*Adam and Eve seemed mildly surprised. Meanwhile, Sorami and I had yet to fully recover from the initial shock.*
Sorami: Eh, uh, um... seriously?
Leviathan: Dead serious, lass. Such was Lilith's request.
Sorami: Uhhh...
Setsuna: Are you sure we can all fit on your back?
Leviathan: I could coil around Atlantis five times if I so desired. You could spend your whole life walking, and still not reach the end of my tail.
Setsuna: Hmph. I don't think you can declare that before we get a chance to try.
Adam: Indeed.
*However terrible a sensation that was, it seemed I was in agreement with Adam on this matter.*
Sorami: What's wrong with you guys?! We are on a _double date_ today. Can you play your games some other time?
Eve: ......
*Sorami placed her palms on my cheeks, and proceeded to force my gaze on her. Eve clasped Adam's hand in her own way to calm him down.*
*...I guessed it was for the best if we postponed our trekking challenge for now.*
Setsuna: So, how are we supposed to get over there?
Leviathan: Hold your horses, son. Give me a moment to ready my back.
*A vast slippery landscape emerged from the depths of the ocean. It was so vast one could easily fit a city or two there.*
Setsuna: Well, let's go, Sorami.
Sorami: Huh? But I can't fly—
*I picked up Sorami without waiting for her to finish.*
Sorami: Uhyah?!
Setsuna: You can if we do this.
Sorami: Th-That was a very sudden embrace, Sir! Do they call this "princess hold" in English?!
Setsuna: I'm pretty sure they don't.
*The suddenness of my act seemed to have sent Sorami into a fit of delirium.*
Eve: Um...
Adam: Yes?
Eve: ......
Adam: Why? You can fly just all right.
Eve: Well, that's true, but... um... you know...
Adam: Hmm.
*I turned back to see Adam take Eve into his arms, mimicking my actions.*
Sorami: I wonder if she insisted on that.
Setsuna: You mean Eve?
Sorami: Yeah... She probably grew jealous.
*With that, Sorami wrapped her arms around my neck, pressing her body against mine.*
Sorami: Being hugged kind of reminds me I'm alive, you know.
Setsuna: If I went all out I could easily crush your bones... Wanna try?
Sorami: D-Don't do that, please!
Setsuna: It was a joke. You didn't like it?
*I thought it was pretty funny.*
Sorami: Your jokes are bad for my heart...
*And so we landed on Leviathan's vast back. Sorami sniffed the air a couple of times, and released a relaxed breath.*
Sorami: Thank goodness. I was worried it would smell like fish.
Leviathan: I can hear you, lass. Mind your tongue.
*Leviathan seemed displeased by Sorami's preconceptions.*
Sorami: Ahh, I'm sorry. It's just that, you know... A date in a fishy-smelling place is a little bit...
Setsuna: What about if you visit a fish market on your date? Or a zoo? Or an aquarium?
Sorami: Those are entirely different.
*Denying my words with utmost confidence, she proceeded to trot on Leviathan's back.*
Sorami: Whoa, this crunchy sensation of scales is cool.
*Indeed. It felt as if I was walking on frost.*
Sorami: The sky's so high. The sea's so vast. But oh crap we're high! It's positively terrifying!
Setsuna: Yes, it feels like we're on a cliff or something.
*We directed our gazes towards the sea of Hell.*
Adam: Do not peer too deep, for that sea is the underworld. A wise man once said that if you gaze long into an abyss, the abyss will gaze back at you.
*Nietzsche. But was Adam sure about bringing up that philosopher of all people here? He was the one who declared God dead after all.*
Setsuna: However, Hell or not, the water's surface doesn't look any different from a regular sea. Wait, if it's rain water, then it shouldn't be salty, should it...?
*The rain that submerged Hell was supposedly of the same kind as the one that fell upon the earth for forty days and forty nights in the days of Noah. It probably wasn't salty.*
Adam: It's said that God cleaved that rain water off the heavens. It's probably just as salty as the sea.
Setsuna: Hmm.
*Most curious indeed.*
Sorami: Hey, _you two_. Let's have lunch already.
*Sorami and Eve had spread a picnic blanket, and were readying boxed lunches already.*
*The display itself made my stomach grumble. Now that I thought about it, I ate very few rations ever since coming to Tokyo Babel.*
*Sorami would prepare our breakfasts, lunches, and dinners pretty much every day. Unfortunately, I could not comment on the taste. These days I truly lamented the fact I did not possess functional taste buds.*
Sorami: Here you go. Since we were going on a d-d-date today, I tried preparing something a little bit special. Wh-What do you think?
*She had trouble pronouncing the word "date," and then her voice fell to almost a whisper. The presence of Adam and Eve must have made her feel awkward.*
Setsuna: Um...
*Of course I knew what was the best course of action here. I had to praise her. I had to thank her. That much was obvious.*
*However, this was a date. I had to find words that would make her feel especially good in this situation.*
Setsuna: L-Looks like a feast, I think.
Sorami: That's it?
Setsuna: Looks delicious.
Sorami: ...One more push.
Setsuna: Fantastic?
Sorami: It's getting further and further from what I wanted. Can you try coming up with something that'd make my heart race? Try one more time.
*"Wh-What does that mean?" was the question I would have liked to ask had her deep gaze not left me speechless.*
Setsuna: Hmm...
Setsuna: I-I feel like you already found the way to my heart?
Sorami: I'm not sure about that question mark at the end, but I'll let you off the hook for today. Help yourself~
I took the boxed lunch she stuck out to me, and opened its lid. ...An apt word to describe it would probably be: _meat_.
*Hamburg steak. Meatballs. Youlinji.*
*Beef seasoned with miso. Boiled pork. Tomato baked chicken.*
*Cold pork shabu-shabu. Roast beef. Bang bang chicken.*
Sorami: Hehe, I managed to get some British spam.
*Spam wasn't actually a British invention, but I couldn't blame her for thinking so; she must've seen that sketch, too.*
Setsuna: Is there anything other than meat?
Sorami: Hehe. Salad is in this box.
*Thank god. The contents of the other box assaulted my eyes with colorful splendor — from refreshing green to enticing red — it was packed with delicious-looking vegetables.*
*Cabbage, lettuce, napa, carrots, tomatoes, cucumbers, eggplant, and much more.*
*This was indeed amazing. Especially the size of the whole thing. Countless vegetable dishes barely fit in the container which was already quite humongous as far as lunch boxes went.*
Sorami: And this here is soup. I brought it in a thermos so it's still warm.
*She was pulling out one dish after another like some magic show (well, a bit of magic was probably involved in preparing some of these).*
Sorami: Phew, I really gave my all today.
Setsuna: It seems so. I'm quite positively awed. I'll make sure to eat everything.
*In the worst case scenario I could have nanomachines accelerate my digestion.*
Sorami: Ehehe. Thanks.
Eve: ......
...Huh? The air on the other side of the sheet seemed to have been overtaken by a dark mood. To be more specific: Eve appeared to be positively depressed.
Sorami: H-Huh...?
Eve: ......
*A dark aura of sorts seemed to be swirling around her as she had her eyes locked on Sorami.*
Sorami: U-Um... Mrs. Eve?
Eve: ......
Sorami: D-Did I do something?
Eve: No. You have not done a thing.
*As Eve's gloomy gaze pierced Sorami, she jerked towards me, clutching onto my arm.*
Sorami: I-I don't know what's going on, but I think we are in a Pattern Blue kind of situation!
*If I could have a word, I'd say Eve's normally blue eyes were actually turning red now.*
*But that wasn't important now. What was driving Eve to direct all this peculiar attention to Sorami? It felt too weak for animosity, too feeble for killing intent, and too pure for malice.*
Adam: Eve.
Eve: ......
Adam: Eve, cut it out. She is herself. You are you.
Eve: I understand that, but...
Adam: And I prefer your cooking.
*His line finally made Sorami and me realize what was going on.*
*In a small lunch box, there rested a plain loaf of bread, some thinly sliced venison, and shredded cabbage.*
*A portion for two. That was the situation of their lunch box. In other words, a sense of inferiority had overtaken Eve as she saw what Sorami had in store.*
*This was most troubling. What were we supposed to do to escape this gloom?*
*For the first time since battling Oshiba Hagane, I was forced to stretch my mental faculties to the limit. What about sharing our lunch box with them?*
*No, that was probably not a very good idea. I got the feeling it had the "I shall bless you with my superior cuisine, lowly wretch, xoxoxo" kind of nuance.*
*How about ignoring them? A sensible strategy, but not very apt for this situation.*
Sorami: Setsuna, open wide!
Setsuna: Aaaanh.
Sorami: Ehehe. How does it taste?
Setsuna: It's delicious!
Sorami: Ahahahaha.
Setsuna: Hahahahaha.
Eve: Boohoohoo...
*Definitely not a good idea. Also, was it just me, or was my personality oddly off in that sketch?*
*Helping ourselves to a quiet lunch while ignoring our guests. ...Could one call that a date?*
*Hoping that Sorami might have come up with something better, I gave her a glance—*
Sorami: ............
*Sorami was trembling; she looked like she was on the verge of crying. Realizing she had hurt Eve's feelings, she herself seemed to suffer a deep shock. I had to do something or this would end in a disaster.*
Eve: ......
Sorami: ......
*As my mind was busy, awhirl with panicky thoughts, Adam suddenly clasped a piece of venison in his chopsticks, and guided it to his mouth.*
Adam: Very good.
Eve: Eh? But... um...
Adam: Tasty things are tasty. You made this, didn't you?
Eve: Y-Yes. Um... I did.
*Eve blinked a couple of times in confusion. But Adam regarded her in serene calm.*
Adam: I do not understand why you would feel inferior. You made this lunch for me, didn't you? That alone is much more meaningful than the most splendid of feasts.
Eve: ......
Sorami: Ohhh...
*Eve turned the color of crimson. Light returned to Sorami's eyes. Adam proceeded to take a bite out of the bread with a blank expression.*
Eve: B-But... But I still could've... tried to prepare something a little bit more...
Adam: Anything turns to the most delicious of feasts as long as you are at my side, sharing the meal with me.
Eve: ...?!
*I exchanged glances with Sorami, and realized we were shaking. Both from being touched, and feeling a bit out of place in this dramatic scene.*
Sorami: (Setsuna, I'm in a pickle. I don't know how long I can withstand the repelling power of their love barrier.)
Setsuna: (Love barrier?)
Sorami: (I just made it up, but it's kind of self-explanatory, don't you think?)
Setsuna: (Well, I guess I can tell what you mean.)
Sorami: (What should we do? Wanna take a walk further away?)
Setsuna: (That would be pretty awkward. Let's just get the lunch out of the way first.)
Sorami: (...I tried my best to prepare it, you know.)
*A lonely expression set on Sorami's features. ...It seemed I chose my words poorly.*
Setsuna: All right. I'll make sure to savor the taste and all that, okay?
Sorami: Yeah.
*Sorami gave me a friendly nod. Well, let's dig in, then.*
Sorami: Open wide.
Setsuna: I can eat myself—
Sorami: Anh?!
Setsuna: My deepest gratitude. I shall then help myself to your generosity.
*I opened my mouth, and Sorami guided a meatball into it. Its salty-sweet flavor was out of this world.*
Sorami: Ehehe. Try more. Aaanh.
Setsuna: Munch. How about you? You aren't eating?
Sorami: ......
*Sorami directed her gaze at my arms. I could tell what she was thinking.*
*Did she really want me to do it?*
*Did I have a choice?*
Setsuna: Sorami. Open your mouth.
Sorami: Yeah! Aaanh... Um, Setsuna, would you mind cutting that hamburg steak into pieces first?
Setsuna: My apologies.
*It seemed the chunks I was used to eating couldn't fit into her small mouth. I divided it into pieces, and proceeded to do the "aaanh" thing again.*
Sorami: Aaanh... Munch. Munch. Oh yeah, it's real good! I did awesome! Yeah, I did awesome...
*The hint of sadness in her tone probably arose from the fact she was forced to praise herself.*
Setsuna: Yeah, it's truly delicious. Where did you learn to cook? Oh, I suppose you can't answer that, sorry.
Sorami: Mhm. I don't remember a thing, so it kind of almost feels like I could do this thing from birth, you know?
Setsuna: Able to cook from birth...
*Very convenient. Though most professional cooks would likely cry at the notion.*
Sorami: Well, but if I continue cooking it might help me remember something, you know. So I'll be sure to make lots more good stuff for you to taste. Aaanh.
Setsuna: Munch. Munch. I'll be looking forward to it.
Sorami: Ehehe.
Eve: ......
Adam: What is it?
Eve: U-Um. Would it be all right if I tried that, too?
*Eve, knitting her eyebrows in an expression of steel resolve, proceeded to guide a piece of her own cooking towards Adam's mouth.*
Adam: Thank you.
*Adam bit into it without a hint of hesitation.*
Adam: ...I would like to try as well. Would you mind?
Eve: N-No!
*Eve quickly shook her head, and promptly opened her delicate mouth, closing her eyes. She reminded me of a baby bird waiting to be fed.*
Eve: Aanh... Munch. Munch.
Adam: ......
Setsuna: ...?
*Did I imagine it? It seemed like Adam's expression changed there for a second.*
Adam: ......
Eve: ...It's a bit embarrassing.
Adam: It was embarrassing for me, too.
*With that, Adam proceeded to eat by himself again.*
Sorami: Adam is so gentle.
*I very much wanted to object that notion, but I couldn't quite find the words, given what we'd witnessed.*
Adam: I am not gentle. I am just trying to be as I should.
Sorami: As you should? What do you mean?
Adam: I have to be Adam. To act as the first man and be faithful to God's design. I might have been assembled by angels, but the blueprint they used was the same.
*Adam declared his origin with an indifferent voice, as if it were no big deal at all.*
Eve: ......
*Eve fixed her gaze on the ground, looking troubled, as if battling with something on her mind.*
Adam: Unfortunately, I have no memories of the original. So the sole option at my disposal is to do what should be done.
Sorami: And what should that be?
Adam: Pilgrimage. I have to reach God's side, and beg for His forgiveness. Such is my role.
Setsuna: I knew about the pilgrimage, but what's this about forgiveness?
*Adam, his face emotionless, opened his mouth, and made his confession in a fashion most suited to someone discussing weather.*
Adam: I shall become a sacrifice. I do not know if He will burn me alive, or strike me down with thunder, but I imagine I will meet my end at the last stage of my pilgrimage.
Sorami: ...Eh?
Setsuna: Sacrifice...?
Adam: I am but a lamb that should seek forgiveness. As long as God does not reject me, I will bestow him my life.
Eve: ......
Sorami: Y-You mean you are going to um... die?
Adam: Yes. What of it?
Setsuna: ......
Sorami: Th-That can't be right! Suicide is—
Adam: It is not a suicide. Do not confuse wasting the life God has given you with bestowing it to His grace.
Sorami: B-But! That's...
*Tears started welling in Sorami's eyes. Adam, observing the phenomenon, cocked his head to the side in puzzlement.*
Adam: Why do you cry?
Sorami: I don't know... but...
Adam: Eve is not crying.
Eve: ...Yes, and I shall never do so.
*She gave Adam a smile.*
Sorami: But... But are you alright with that?
Eve: Yes. If such is Adam's role, I can only see him off with joy in my heart.
*There was not a tinge of hesitation in Eve's words. Madness was the word that swirled in my mind, but I knew that was not the case.*
*They dispassionately accepted everything their given roles entailed. Discarding both hope and desperation in the process, forgetting what it meant to rebel.*
Eve: Such is our destiny. Adam's one of sacrifice, and mine of seeing him off.
Sorami: ...But.
Setsuna: Sorami. Cut it out.
*Reacting to my cold tone, Sorami returned to her seat, and proceeded to awkwardly continue eating the boxed lunch in complete silence.*
*Observing this outcome, I couldn't help but...*
Setsuna: Adam.
Adam: What is it?
Setsuna: I must say I can't stand you, after all.
Adam: ...Hm. I never hoped for you to like me.
Setsuna: I hate the fact that you're making Eve cry from the bottom of my heart.
*Adam cocked his head to the side in befuddlement.*
Adam: What are you talking about? Eve is not crying.
Setsuna: She is.
Eve: Thank you for worrying about me. Unfortunately, I am not currently crying, Lord Tendou.
*Adam gave me an absolutely infuriating "see?" kind of look.*
Setsuna: Before your so-called sacrifice, give yourself a moment to think about what I said.
Adam: There is no need to waste time on thinking about drivel.
Setsuna: ......
*I gave up on trying to communicate with him at this point. He would likely meet his god eventually, and accomplish his sacrifice.*
*I had no right to stop him, nor did I particularly want to. He could do whatever he wished for all I cared.*
*So what if Eve falls on her knees crying once the deed was done? The best I could hope to do was console her after the fact.*
Setsuna: Real men, nonetheless, don't abandon thought till the very end.
Adam: ......
Setsuna: Aren't you a man? The very first one? Try using that head God has supposedly given you for a change.
*I eyed him intently. He, however, took my glare straight on, and looked back at me resolute as if there was truly not a shred of doubt in his soul.*
Adam: I cannot say I like how you make it sound like I have never taken time to ruminate.
Setsuna: Have you ever?
Adam: I... All right, I understand. I shall heed your words and take some time to ponder, even if I already know the conclusion cannot possibly differ.
Setsuna: That's... a wise choice.
*We broke our gazes. As I was about to dig into my chicken leftovers, Adam suddenly mumbled something as if to himself.*
Adam: Tendou Setsuna, I am Adam.
Setsuna: I know that.
Adam: As the first man to grace this earth, it is my duty to love each and every one of my progeny.
Setsuna: Is there a point to that?
Adam: Yes, or at least I thought there was. However, I have to admit: I detest you from the bottom of my heart.
Adam: So much so that your pain would turn to my pleasure. It appears I loathe you.
Setsuna: Don't worry. I'm just the same. There's but one reason I would pray for your safety, and that's because I don't wish for Eve to cry.
Adam: Then I shall pray for your safety, too, so Kugutsu Sorami can escape lament.
Setsuna: ......
Adam: ......
The Two: ...Hmph.
Sorami: ...
Eve: ...
*Sorami and Eve looked at each other for a while, and once content, proceeded to laugh.*
*And so, we gazed at the outside scenery.*
*Outside? I suppose it was outside in a way.*
Eve: Hell below. Heaven above.
Setsuna: Can't we just fly all the way up to the top from here and be done with the whole ordeal?
Eve: Many tried when Tokyo Babel had first been formed.
Sorami: None returned?
Eve: Yes. Back then we hypothesized that Leviathan might be shooting pilgrims down.
Leviathan: Why in blue blazes should I bother with something like that? They went mad on their own.
Eve: It seems none of the pilgrims could resist the potency of the chorus, the cursed siren song currently filling the heavens.
Eve: And we also had the words of Messenger. In the end, we decided against trying to cheat our way into Heaven.
Adam: Both Eve and I were made resistant to the song. We have yet to observe its effect on ourselves.
Sorami: Huh? What about us? Are we resistant, too?
Eve: No, you are not. If the song's taint touches your hearts, you will go mad and plunge yourselves off a precipice like lemmings.
Sorami: That sure was straight to the point! But, mhm... I can't say I like the idea of going mad very much.
Setsuna: Well, we're still all right, aren't we? If it grows worse, we can always turn back.
Adam: Yes. You should do so.
Setsuna: Let's try to go as far as possible.
Sorami: Your phrasing changed from pessimistic to optimistic suddenly, but the overall idea is still the same, right?
*_Don't worry about it. It's a man thing_.*
Eve: Still, you should at least try finding your raison d'etre. It is the best tool to resist the call of the chorus.
Sorami: Reason for one's existence... I tried thinking and looking for it, but... Do you think someone like me would have one?
Setsuna: I'm sure you do. It's just that you haven't realized yet.
Sorami: What about you?
Setsuna: I...
*A blood chilling thought ran through my mind. I couldn't truly deny that someone like me might indeed not have a reason to live after all.*
Setsuna: Have you two found your reasons?
*I couldn't help but ask. The two nodded.*
Adam: Of course. As the first man, I was born as a representative of everyone to whom this earth belongs. My reason for existence is mankind itself.
Eve: Mine is easier. To serve Adam, and his ambition. Such is the reason behind my existence, and my own goal.
*Hmm. Well, I supposed it was, too, worthy of respect, in a way.*
*But with what kind of concept could my own reason lie?*
*Gazing at the light of the distant skies, I wrestled with the question in my mind.*
*We said our goodbyes to Adam and Eve in Ginza. The two thanked us, and took their leave, flying into the sky.*
*Walking through the ruins, I was deep in thought. Sorami, seemingly worried, lightly poked my arm.*
Sorami: Still worried about it?
*I knew what she was thinking.*
Setsuna: Yes. It's bothering me a bit... Quite a lot actually.
*Raison d'etre.*
Sorami: The reason for our existence, huh. It's about time we started looking for it seriously, isn't it?
Setsuna: Yeah.
Sorami: I wonder what kind of things were on my mind in the past — when I still had my memories and all.
Setsuna: I don't think many people go out of their way to ponder such matters.
*The reason for one's existence. I doubted there were many people who could hold their heads high and confidently declare theirs to the world.*
*Not to mention I had to find a raison d'etre so strong it could distort the laws of this world — Tokyo Babel.*
*Sin. Punishment. Misdeed. Redemption.*
*All sorts of negative words would emerge, and sink again in the ocean of my thoughts. Were those indeed the only reasons available to me in the end?*
Sorami: Not quite! Setsuna, I think your raison d'etre...
*Sorami suddenly sprang forward and, extending her arms in a wide arc, turned back to me.*
Sorami: ...is to bring happiness to those around you!
*...... ...... ......*
Setsuna: I don't think that's it.
Sorami: D-Don't deny it outright like that! How do you think I feel now? I cried out with such confidence, too. Can you imagine how embarrassing this is?!

??? / Belial: I see, I see. Seems you just couldn't wait for your time, old fuck!

*Nor could I recall his face or build — all details of his appearance had already vacated my mind.*
*A few more hours, and I'd probably forget I ever met him.*

*Most likely I was more thoroughly expunged from history than the mysterious man himself.*
*For not only was he an angel of immense power, his history must have been as long as that of Earth itself. That was no easy man to forget, I'd assume.*

*I spent what seemed like an eternity curled up in a fetal position, sniveling like a newborn babe.*
*By the end of it, I found myself losing interest in myself, and the whole world for that matter. Thinking to jump down from the edge of the cloud and put an end to it all, I stood up, and wandered into the blindingly white wastes.*

??? / Messenger: I would not recommend wandering away too far.

*I was not here because of fate, but out of sheer necessity. My wishes were never granted no matter how I wished for it. The world would never move according to my will.*
