*That was the kind of lonely angel Metatron was.*
*Letting out a sigh, Raziel closed the book, and ruffled her hair.*
Raziel: I remembered everything. Indeed, for an angel of his power, creating the world should pose no significant hurdle. The one closest to God — Metatron.
*That was how powerful he was.*
Setsuna: I'm not quite familiar with the divine hierarchy in regards to strength. Is Metatron more powerful than Michael?
*Raziel, without a second's pause, gave me a nod. I could hardly believe it. Still, I imagined Raziel would know these things far better than me.*
Raziel: Michael was indeed strong. He wasn't called our supreme commander for nothing. But his strength came with his armies; I highly doubt even he had the strength to oppose Metatron alone.
*That was how absurdly powerful Metatron was in raw might. Once a human, once just a scribe, he attained incredible powers through the countless battles he ended up braving.*
*The one that held the title of the "mightiest" among all of the 31,655,722 angels.*
*That was Metatron. That was _our foe_.*
Raziel: Let me tell it straight — we don't stand a chance. At least, he is not an opponent we could possibly face in a fair fight.
Eve: But if we do nothing, the world will be destroyed.
*Raziel slumped her shoulders, and shook her head. All vigor had vacated her countenance.*
Raziel: If destruction is his will, there is not a thing we can do about it. Well, I plan to resist till the very end nonetheless, but I don't believe it will change anything at this point.
Setsuna: So you're going to submit to the future?
Raziel: ......
Setsuna: Raziel, think. What will happen if we yield here? He'll overwrite the old world with his new one, and become God.
*Vexation crept into Raziel's voice.*
Raziel: I know that much! And he has more than enough power to do it! Creating a new world is child's play to him! But... I don't have the right to deny him!
Raziel: I mean, Pandora has fallen apart. There are barely any angels or demons still living. And I lack the power to create a new world myself. What else can we—
*Raziel lowered her head, her eyes bereft of strength.*
Setsuna: We have to reject that future nonetheless. No matter how you look at it, the future that angel is designing is an abomination.
Eve: I wholeheartedly agree with this sentiment. This world needs no new future.
Adam: One way or the other, if given the opportunity I would rather not perish. I wager we have no alternative but to struggle until the very end.
Raziel: ......
Setsuna: Raziel, Metatron might indeed be great. He might indeed not be an opponent we could possibly defeat. But we still have to fight him.
*Raziel fell silent for a few seconds, then nodded quietly.*
Adam: So with that settled, what do you think we should do from now on? I'd like to continue the pilgrimage if possible.
*To climb Jacob's Ladder from the seventh stratum, and enter Heaven. That shouldn't prove too hard at this point. After all, the master of the sixth stratum had already fallen to our might.*
*I didn't know who lorded over the floor above, but with Adam's strength, I doubted they'd prove that much of an obstacle.*
Eve: The problem is that Heaven might very well be Metatron's realm by now.
*Indeed. Before creating the entirety of the new world, Metatron would likely start by creating a realm where he himself would reside in.*
Setsuna: But what of our Lord, then?
*Raziel grew pale as a ghost.*
Setsuna: Is he already de—
Raziel: Stop it!
Adam: The possibility of him being dead by now is fairly high.
*Adam blurted the statement with complete indifference.*
Eve: ......
*Eve, as if unable to believe her ears, stared at Adam in astonishment. And so did Raziel.*
*The one and only Lord of Heaven was likely an absolute concept to the two of them. And I couldn't blame them, given their upbringing.*
*Meanwhile, Adam was created by angels, and I myself by mankind. Neither of us were exactly of God's design.*
*And so neither of us seemed to feel that absolute sense of veneration towards Him.*
Setsuna: Yeah. The place that Metatron brought me to back then was completely empty; it's possible it was the half-finished new Heaven of his.
Adam: Hmm. Then it would indeed be most wise to travel together.
Setsuna: ......
*Adam shrugged at my surly expression.*
Adam: Don't be so grim. It's not like I like the idea either.
Setsuna: Oh, not a fan yourself?
Adam: Yes. I realized during the earlier fight, but just as it seems like you hate me, I can tell you I hate you just as much.
*Again, he spoke without care or feeling. His face was a blank — I had no idea what emotions swirled behind that mask.*
*Still, his declaration inexplicably cheered me up.*
Setsuna: You have my thanks. Apparently, we're of the same mind. Wait, or would that actually be the other way around?
*Hmph — Adam snorted out a smile. It kind of irritated me, but now was hardly the time for pointless bickering.*
Raziel: At any rate, let's head to the seventh stratum; we currently have no other option but to push forward.
*With these words she closed the book, and stored it into her pocket dimension. Her face was a mask of gloom, but beyond it I could still spot a hint of her will to fight.*
Setsuna: All right, let's go.
*We split up to look for the entrance to the next floor.*
Raziel: And so I found it. You're all welcome to sing my praises.
*Raziel accidentally stumbled upon the door as she slacked off in a nearby bookstore. The world was a very unfair place, as always.*
*Who would've thought a door would open inside the bookshelf. Sighing at Tokyo Babel's lack of common sense, I used my silver key to unlock it.*
Adam: Well then, let us go.
Eve: Yes, Adam.
Raziel: ......
Setsuna: Let's go, Raziel.
Raziel: Yeah... Goodbye, Anafi'el. Goodbye, everyone.
*She took a few seconds to wistfully consider the mountain of old books behind us.*
*No new knowledge would ever descend on this place again. And all the wisdom it already contained would rot and wither away with no one there to taste its fruits.*
*While merely a replica of the real thing that had long vanished from this world, it still doubtless pained Raziel's heart to see it perish all over again.*
Raziel: The library has collapsed, and this town is already withering away. There is no longer a place for knowledge to accumulate in this world.
Setsuna: You can create a new one.
Raziel: I'll consider it.
*A hint of cheer passed across Raziel's face.*
*Something akin to black sludge spun around the walls of the corridor. The chorus assaulted my mind with more potency than ever before, making me wince.*
*Like static. Like a solemn choir. Like an innocent children's song.*
*I could almost hear my brain creak under the pressure of this overpowering curse of bliss the tunnel contained.*
Setsuna: Kh...
*Adam tried touching the sludge on the wall.*
Adam: I see. This is indeed pretty bad — I can feel my head cry in pain despite all of the countermeasures installed. I wonder if these souls-turned-sludge here are to blame.
*Adam was about to unsheathe his weapon, but Eve stopped him.*
Eve: Please stop. Those used to be the dwellers of Heaven. And from the look of it, I imagine there will be no end to them — they are next to infinite as far as we are concerned.
Adam: You think destroying them would be of no use?
Eve: Yes. There is no salvation for them, not for all eternity, or rather, you could say _they have already been absolved, in a way_.
*_To Heaven?_ I tried listening to their words despite myself.*
*Come with us. Come. Come. Come. To eternal bliss.*
*I shut my hearing down as fast as I could. Just listening to the verse made me sick.*
*Their souls had fused with one another, but they somehow still retained parts of their individual consciousness — like hell I'd ever want to become a part of a dreadful substance like that.*
Raziel: ......
Setsuna: Raziel, are you all right?
Raziel: I cannot say I am. ...I feel sick.
*Raziel covered her mouth. The assault of the chorus seemed to cause a sensation similar to nausea from drunkenness in her.*
Setsuna: Let's hurry. It isn't a good idea to stay here for long.
Adam: Indeed. But first, let us have the knaves in the way disappear, after all. Futile it might be, but banishing them for now might at least buy us some time.
*Adam pulled out a weapon from his pocket dimension.*
Adam: Divine Sword Durandal, banish all and everything that means us harm from this world.
*Without giving us a chance to stop him, Adam pointed his sword at the sludge, and a tremendous blast of energy burst out of its tip.*
*The muck of souls seemed to have been exploded to the nether. The corridor returned to its usual silent white.*
Adam: Hmm. It doesn't seem like they're coming back right away. They probably will eventually, but for now I would say we can hurry to the seventh stratum in relative peace.
Eve: Yes... Thank you.
*Apparently, Adam didn't fancy the idea of Eve stepping into the sludge. She seemed to catch on to his sentiment, and gave him an embarrassed smile.*
*Both I and, doubtless, Raziel were very happy the cursed chorus had been silenced for the time being. Still, I couldn't help having mixed feelings about thanking _him_ for the feat.*
Adam: Well then, let us go.
*And so, we finally opened the doors to the seventh stratum. I felt light headed for a moment. Black clouds covered the sky as far as the eye could see, reminding me of the sludge from before.*
*I could make out skyscrapers in the distance, the grandest of them easily discernable from even this distance.*
Adam: So the seventh stratum was—
Setsuna: Shinjuku.
*It didn't take me more than a glance to recognize it. The physical representation of human ambition — a place of top-level vanity even in Tokyo — Shinjuku.*
*I couldn't tell if it was day or night. The depressing gray covered the entirety of the sky. And the only thing that seemed to show any motility in the scenery was the soul sludge material hovering in the distance.*
Adam: Miasma wherever you turn.
*I had to agree with Adam — something dreadful, like madness made tangible, filled the air.*
*Repugnant enough to make one wish to stop breathing. To want to cover all of one's exposed skin.*
Eve: Let us march forward. The sooner we find Jacob's Ladder, the better.
Raziel: I think we should first confirm the condition of the stratum's master.
Eve: Ah, yes indeed.
*We split into two groups — Adam with Eve, I with Raziel — to inspect the surroundings.*
Raziel: I recommend we check the red-light district first.
*I directed my gaze towards Kabukicho. Ahh.*
Setsuna: It does indeed look like the magic is denser in that direction.
Raziel: If you look close enough you can spot that the magic is concentrating there. Someone might be there — let's check it out.
*The sleepless town that never grew empty regardless of time or season had turned into a ghost town for wild wind to howl about. The lavish neon signs blinking all around us only strengthened the feeling of desolation the place gave off.*
*Though our petty sentiments were blown right away as we reached the main square.*
Setsuna: This is—
Raziel: Raphael... and Gabriel?
*Two humongous steel statues, tied up with their backs to each other, loomed before us, looking almost like Ryoumen Sukuna from Japanese folklore.*
*A tough cord-like thing coiled all around them, piercing through their palms.*
*Their posture reminded me of martyrs who sacrificed their lives praying to God.*
Setsuna: Is this really Raphael and Gabriel?
*Raziel gave me a nod, still shaken by the sight.*
Setsuna: ......
*I flew high into the sky to take a better look at the magic flow. It seemed like the energy emanating from the two master angels traveled straight to one of the skyscrapers.*
Setsuna: What on earth is that...?
*An energy field, or maybe a barrier? A tremendous amount of almost palpable magical energy covered the walls of the building like a giant waterfall.*
*I didn't need to look up the name of the structure — it was the most famous structure in Shinjuku.*
*Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building. There was very obviously something important there. And the two statues below me seemed to be protecting that something.*
Setsuna: Raziel, I would like to confirm one more time just in case: are those statues Raphael and Gabriel?
*Raziel had her hand on one of the statues with a vacant expression.*
Raziel: I think so... Yeah, it's definitely them. My guess is that _they turned themselves inanimate_ out of their own volition.
Setsuna: Out of their own volition...? Why?
*Raziel shook her head. So even she didn't know.*
Setsuna: In any case, Raphael and Gabriel are emanating magic that's protecting the building over there. What do you think we should do?
Raziel: For starters, we should stop the magic flow.
*As Raziel said that, the stomach area of one of the angel statues suddenly came open. What the...?*
*I took a careful peek inside the hole, and saw two small lights insi— No, that was...!*
*A bunch of metal angels burst out from the hole with a piercing shriek.*
*The display left both Raziel and myself speechless. What on earth were those things? They didn't look like any living being I ever saw.*
*With a creepy smile that might as well have been painted on its face, one of the metal angels pointed his gatling gun at us.*
Raziel: Property appension! _Fire_ — level 3!
*Raziel reacted slightly faster than the angel could pull the trigger.*
Setsuna: What on earth...?
Raziel: ...! There are more!
*I glanced up at the sky — indeed, there were more, a whole flock of metal angel-like things.*
*Looking like a swarm of insects, they considered us, and cocked their heads all at the same time.*
Setsuna: This doesn't look good.
*I unsheathed my sword, and prepared myself for the incoming attack.*
Raziel: Raphael and Gabriel seem to be giving birth to them.
Setsuna: Can you stop them?
Raziel: It'll take some time; give me a second.
*Raziel promptly pulled out her tablet, and connected its cord to one of the angel statues.*
Setsuna: Here they come...!
*A machine-gun, shaped like a trumpet, spat a volley of bullets at us.*
Setsuna: Silver Lion of Pride!
*I summoned one of the Seven Beasts that repelled the projectiles. A few angels caught in the crossfire fell down to earth. Unfortunately, one or two was hardly a drop in the ocean given that they attacked us as a legion.*
*You could say we were inside a squall of bullets at this point.*
*For now, I concentrated on making sure none of them found their way to Raziel. That was more or less the extent of what I could do, unable to find an opening for a counter-attack.*
*And to make matters worse, I realized my raison d'etre wouldn't work against these things.*
*It only activated against _those stronger than myself_.*
*And it was obvious they wouldn't be that strong in a one-on-one fight; I couldn't unleash my true power unless they all combined into a single giant robot.*
*My raison d'etre wasn't particularly convenient, now that I thought about it.*
Raziel: I'm almost there...!
Setsuna: Adam! Where the hell are you?!
*To tell the truth, I wasn't particularly keen about asking _him_ for help, but I couldn't figure out anything else to do in this situation. Unfortunately, the voice that answered my call seemed to be as strained as my own.*
Adam: Sorry to disappoint you, but I am quite busy. I don't have time for chatting right now.
Setsuna: Did you run into them, too?
Adam: Hm. Now I see why you'd want help. Unfortunately, I cannot move — if I do, they'll shoot Eve down.
Setsuna: I see. I think I can figure out something myself. You do something about your situation yourself, all right? I pray luck is with you today.
Adam: Hmm. Since when are we on terms to pray for each other?
Setsuna: I'm not praying for you — I'm praying for Eve.
Adam: I see, that makes sense. All right, I shall pray for Raziel as well, then. May luck favor Raziel today.
Setsuna: Though I don't care if you keel over or not.
Adam: I share the sentiment.
*With that, we disconnected our telepathic link. For some odd reason, our brief conversation dispelled my stress. In any case, now I had to think about holding out until Raziel was finished with whatever she was doing.*
*I concentrated on repelling the bullets. With all seven beasts assisting me in battle, the angel bodies eventually started piling into heaps.*
*And so, the long battle finally came to an end.*
*All angels suddenly stopped moving at the same time. Locked mid-motion as if their springs had suddenly given out, they proceeded to fall out of the sky.*
Raziel: ......
Setsuna: Raziel?
Raziel: ...!
*Raziel was pale as a ghost. I only let her out of my sight for a minute, but now she looked as if she'd woken up from a most terrifying nightmare.*
Raziel: Setsuna...
Setsuna: Raziel, what is it?
Raziel: I—
*Raziel clutched her chest, her face contorting into a mask of suffering. As if having witnessed the end of the world, she appeared so haggard I though she might collapse any second.*
Setsuna: Raziel, get a hold of yourself! What on earth happe—
Raziel: Nothing!
*She flinched at the volume of her own voice, and then proceeded to squeeze out a few more words in a calmer tone.*
Raziel: It's nothing. It's really nothing. Raphael and Gabriel have already passed away. It seems they turned their bodies into a device of sorts before death.
Setsuna: To surround that building in magic?
*Raziel gave me a nod.*
Raziel: It seems like they were the masters of this stratum.
*So they went as far as to sacrifice their lives to impede others from reaching Heaven.*
*Was it to prevent humans reaching it? Or the other way around, prevent something still in Heaven from coming out?*
*Well, all of our questions would probably be answered once we actually reached the place.*
Adam: Hmm. I see you survived.
Eve: Are they Raphael and Gabriel?
*Adam and Eve landed right next to us. They didn't seem to have suffered a single scratch in their own battle. Well, Adam's clothes seemed slightly dirtier than before. So there was that.*
*He probably dashed all around, concentrating on keeping Eve safe. And now that I thought about it, I did just the same.*
Raziel: Did you find anything?
Adam: A swarm of metal angels — couldn't tell if they were living beings or machines — attacked us. But that's about it.
Eve: Well, the magic barrier around the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building also seemed to suddenly disappear, but, yes, that's about it.
*It appeared the two already realized where we were supposed to head next.*
Setsuna: Then let's go.
*To the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building — the place currently closest to Heaven.*
*Shinjuku's sky didn't show any sign of clearing up; the purple akin to that of sunrise's glow still covered the entirety of its canopy. Though, under present circumstances, it came off as ominous rather than beautiful.*
*As we stepped on the roof's concrete, a set of shining stairs appeared before us, as if through some magic spell.*
*They stretched up beyond, disappearing into the clouds of the distant sky.*
Raziel: Jacob's Ladder.
*The sole pathway to Heaven. Jacob's Ladder.*
*I battled countless angels and demons, harboring little awe towards the divine abode, but still— the majesty of the display overpowered me for a moment.*
Adam: Let's go.
*With nothing else to add, Adam proceeded up the steps with Eve at his side. Not like it was a race, but I didn't want to fall too far behind him.*
Raziel: We can go at our own pace.
*No, we should hurry. It would be terrible if _he_ entered Heaven before us.*
*Not like it was a race or anything.*
*Meeting Setsuna just for a brief moment allowed me to return to my usual carefree self.*
*I astonished even myself with how easy I could be sometimes.*
*Still, seeing him reduced my uneasiness significantly, though I still couldn't quite shake off my feeling of inadequacy.*
*I just existed. The fact that I never really _lived_ still weighed heavy on my heart.*
*Still. Setsuna told me to think for myself.*
*That I had to come up with an answer of my own. And he also confessed his past to me. The memories that doubtlessly brought him nothing but pain.*
*I haven't lived for a single year.*
*That was the truth. So looking for my raison d'etre in the past would likely prove futile.*
*If there was one thing I realized through all this time of pondering, it was that I wanted to be together with him, with Tendou Setsuna.*
Sorami: Mhmfu.
*I couldn't contain the creepy giggle from escaping my lips. Still, the embarrassing display made me feel better at the same time.*
*It seemed that I at least had the right to live. Oddly enough, the fact that I was looking for a reason to live right now made me completely forget my recent wish to die.*
*I would live. And now I had to busy myself figuring out how. I thought such an approach suited me a lot better than silently sulking in the corner.*
Sorami: I mean, the amount of futures is infinite, right?
*I aimed the remark at myself, but a particular angel decided to follow up on it instead.*
Messenger: That is not true.
*Messenger regarded me with a blood-freezing smirk on her lips.*
Sorami: ......
*Unable to utter a sound, I unconsciously took a step back.*
Messenger: Your conversation with Tendou Setsuna seems to have provided you with a reason to live, for better or worse.
Sorami: I... haven't found it yet, though.
Messenger: Well, it's not like you need to look for it yourself.
*I blinked once, and she was no longer there.*
Messenger: We already found a reason for you to live, a long time ago.
Sorami: ...!
*A whisper came from the very tip of my ear. I turned around to see her tracing her hand against my hair with a smile on her face.*
*Overcome with revulsion and fear, I couldn't move an inch. All I could do was watch her face in quiet horror.*
Messenger: You shall define one future, and unify all threads to it alone. Your role is to make sure another multiverse will not come into being.
Sorami: No. I never wished for anything like that.
Messenger: Don't you want to make Tendou Setsuna happy?
Sorami: Eh...?
*Well, of course I do.*
Messenger: He confessed his past to you, but there was one thing he still hid.
Sorami: ......
Messenger: Did you know that he doesn't have long in this world?
Sorami: Eh...?
Messenger: Tendou Setsuna—
*The world in front of my eyes turned black with Messenger's words.*
Sorami: No...
Messenger: Such is his fate.
*N-No! I wouldn't allow it. I _couldn't allow it_. Setsuna couldn't give in to a fate like that.*
Messenger: You want to save him, don't you?
*I want to. I really want to, but—*
Messenger: So let's decide on a future, then. There has to be at least one that you'll find to your liking. We'll cherry pick that one, and crush all of the others.
*But that would be—*
Messenger: Otherwise, he will definitely _perish_.
*Perish.*
*I would survive, but not Setsuna? No, I didn't want that. I refused to acknowledge that.*
*I mean, Setsuna... Setsuna has to have a right to be happy!*
Messenger: Even though he let ten billion men die?
*That was untrue. It wasn't his fault. Who forced all that responsibility on him in the first place? Those ten billion people themselves.*
Messenger: But he himself believes it to be his fault. And so he deliberately avoids happiness. And, of course, he is hell-bent on paying the toll for his crimes.
Sorami: But that's...!
Messenger: No futures offer him salvation.
Sorami: Ahh...
Messenger: But what about the future that had been severed from the past?
Sorami: ......
Messenger: With no past, he would have no need to pay for his sins.
Sorami: ......
Messenger: You should take him with you, as the Adam of the new world.
Sorami: I...
*I felt light-headed. I couldn't tell if her words rang true, or if they sought to trick me to commit a terrible mistake.*
Messenger: It's time you went to sleep. And once you open your eyes again, all will have started — and everything will be past the end.
*Future. A single future that you could not bend. A future where all you could do was walk straight forward.*
*But it was also the only future that blessed him with life.*
*If all that had waited for me was pain, I could've found a way to deal with despair. Maybe I would've chosen death, or endured it gritting my teeth.*
*Yet, Messenger offered me a peaceful future full of bliss instead. A world where even Tendou Setsuna could find happiness for himself.*
*I ended up... wishing for such a future.*
*We walked for three hours straight. The sun, shining faint in the distance, had not moved an inch in the sky.*
*Time remained at a standstill in this world. The clouds retained their shape, immobile as if plastered to the sky. Only the four of us moved under the frozen sight.*
Setsuna: Adam.
Adam: ...What is it?
*Adam turned to face me with a hint of irritation.*
Setsuna: Will your duty come to an end once we reach Heaven?
*I felt like asking just as well.*
Adam: I shall lay down my life.
Setsuna: But that would be the case only if God was alive, wouldn't it?
*Everyone's eyes fixed on me. Not giving in to the pressure, I continued. It was a talk we had to have at one point.*
Setsuna: There's a high possibility that Heaven's already in Metatron's hands. In other words, God _lacks the power_ to stop his rebellion.
Setsuna: If you still think that it's all a part of God's test for mankind, well, go ahead.
Setsuna: But what will you do if your Lord himself is already beyond help?
*Like, if he no longer physically existed in this world. A blasphemy indeed, but also one that was very likely.*
Adam: That's...
*It was the first time I saw Adam stutter.*
Eve: ......
Setsuna: Will you worship the new Lord? Or would you rather choose your fate for yourself?
Adam: I don't know.
*His flat response nearly made my blood boil.*
Setsuna: Know it, Adam. If you don't, there's no point in continuing onwards.
Adam: Then, how about you?
Setsuna: I shall save a girl by the name of Kugutsu Sorami, and do my best to help her lead a peaceful life. After that, it doesn't matter. I'll just live until I die.
*I couldn't end my life right away, for that would cause her sorrow; she would weep for my sorry fate. And I didn't want that. I refused to let my own wretched self bring her any more tears.*
*I knew full well that my life had been but a fleeting moment from the start. But still. Still, I—*
Raziel: ......
Eve: Kugutsu Sorami...
Adam: Hmm. I loathe to admit it, but your resolve rings sound in my ears. Eve, is there anything in particular you would like to do if God is no longer with us?
Eve: ...Huh?
*Eve froze in place — the two of us behind her had to stop our ascent.*
Adam: What would you like to do after reaching Heaven? I thought I would like to grant your wish first of all.
Eve: I—
*It seemed as if she was struggling to find the right words. After a while, she faintly smiled.*
Eve: I don't want anything in particular. All I'd ever wish for would be to spend my time with you in silence. That would be more than enough bliss for me.
Adam: ...I see.
*Adam nodded, his countenance ambiguous, unclear if he found the answer convincing or not.*
*And so we resumed our trek. It appeared like Adam's question had pierced to the very depths of Eve's heart — even us, walking behind her, could tell her mind was no longer here.*
*Jacob's Ladder continued with no end in sight. Adam and Eve, Raziel and I — we all continued our ascent one step at a time.*
*Clouds immobile, sun anchored to the sky — the concept of time had long abandoned us. Neither hunger nor fatigue existed in this world — all that weighed down upon our souls was the most excruciating sense of boredom.*
*Even the chorus seemed to lose its vigor here — even on the third stratum the voices put more strain on my mind.*
*It was most odd.*
*Wasn't it the angels in Heaven that sung that accursed song? Now that I thought about it, ultimately no one could find out the reason why it had the power to destroy the minds of all beings — both divine and mortal — that cared to lend it an ear.*
*In any case, it must have certainly been louder than this to affect anyone.*
*I mean, the song of that black sludge was intense, it tried to ravage both my body and soul. But this—*
*The more we ascended — from the first stratum to the second; from the second to the third — the volume of the voices would grow louder and louder.*
*Yet, once we came here, the song turned barely audible. It hardly bothered our minds. Was this an indication of a change in Heaven?*
*The white clouds were already almost at arm's reach. We took another step up the ladder, and the clouds welcomed us with a gentle chill.*
*Beyond them, finally, lay the end of the road. We need climb no longer.*
*So what had become of Heaven?*
Adam: ...It appears we are finally at our journey's end.
*Now we only had to open those blindingly white gates looming before our eyes to learn everything.*
*The time was nigh to part them.*
*Adam and Eve — one with a golden, another with a silver key in hand — stood in front of the lock.*
*The lock unfastened without resistance. And the gates ruptured with a solemn groan.*
*Behind them—*
Adam: ...Hmm.
Eve: What—
Raziel: It's empty?
*There was nothing there. Only a white canvas, stretching as far as the eye could see. Well, land and sky seemed to vaguely exist, but that was about it.*
Setsuna: Are you sure we're in the right place?
*Raziel slowly shook her head.*
Raziel: We had land, and towns, and trees... and even animals. But this place...
Adam: Hmm, let's go.
*Adam proceeded forward without a hint of hesitation. The ground he stepped on flickered like some garbled video game texture.*
Setsuna: ......
*Concentrating magic to my feet, I tried taking a step forward myself. The soft quality of the ground made me feel like I was walking on a carpet.*
*The floor's data seemed to momentarily go awry with each of my steps — various strange symbols as well as lines of 1 and 0 would manifest and soon vanish again on its surface.*
Adam: Such an odd texture. It feels almost like—
Setsuna: This world is still unfinished.
*Adam shot me an indignant look for stealing his line.*
Raziel: I see. He used an enormous amount of aqua vitae to completely overwrite the whole place.
*Raziel traced her hand along the soft ground.*
Raziel: Aqua vitae can take the shape of everything, even earth itself. Though, with this amount it seems it will still take quite a bit of time for it to properly transform.
Eve: So then this place is indeed Heaven?
Raziel: Yes. This is without doubt the same place you, too, spent your young days at.
Eve: ......
*Eve glanced at the empty sky, then lowered her gaze to the white ground.*
Eve: This is Heaven? I don't want to believe it.
*Aversion sounded clear in her words. I've never seen Eve this obviously angry before.*
Adam: Did Metatron cause this?
Raziel: Only angels and the select few of mankind could dwell in Heaven. I doubt anyone but him had enough power to ravage the holy place like this.
*A grand angel who people had called another God once.*
Raziel: This place is already a heaven of his design. The heaven we once knew exists no longer.
*Everyone fell silent for a while. Neither I, nor Adam knew what Heaven was supposed to look like; the sight of its new form didn't affect us that much.*
*Eve and Raziel, on the other hand, seemed to have been hit quite hard by the sterile sight. Paradise Lost — Eve had once lived, and been exiled from this place as punishment for consuming the fruit of knowledge.*
*While Adam was reimagined anew, Eve, supposedly, survived from those times, living among mortals. She probably still harbored a sense of attachment to her old home.*
*Or was there another reason to cause her ire?*
Setsuna: I would like to go look for Sorami if possible—
Raziel: Wait. We should find our divine father first — he should still be somewhere around this place.
Adam: Your words are sound, but where is that _somewhere_ of yours?
*Adam glanced around the surroundings with puzzled eyes. I couldn't blame him — it didn't seem like the concept of _searching_ could possibly make sense in this hardly corporeal place.*
*With only vacant white surrounding us at every angle there was very little we could possibly do.*
Setsuna: Is God visible?
Raziel: I've never seen Him myself, but I could always sense His presence. Though with all directions looking the same, I have no idea which way we should advance.
*Seemingly at her wit's end, Raziel spun around considering the scenery around us.*
Setsuna: Well, if the old Heaven was overwritten, then He might still be in his old location, spatially at least. Can't you at least guess a vague direction from here?
Raziel: Mhm... I'll try.
*Raziel's memory as our guide, we proceeded to scour the surroundings. According to her, there was some sort of curtain veiling God's throne.*
*Unfortunately, we could find neither a throne, nor anything akin to curtains anywhere.*
Raziel: I think it was somewhere around here.
*Predictably, the sole thing we found was empty space. I couldn't feel a thing, and apparently neither did Adam.*
Adam: What should we do now?
Eve: The Sefer Raziel.
*Eve uttered the book's name. The Sefer Raziel — the book that had all the knowledge of this world recorded by our very own Raziel.*
Eve: Maybe your book can help us, Raziel. The book that had enough power to twist the whole world.
Raziel: That's—
*Raziel's countenance grew pale. What was going on? How could a mere book possibly twist anything?*
Raziel: I'll try it out.
*Raziel moved a few steps away from us. After giving me an eye-signal to take more distance, she opened her book.*
Setsuna: Eve, what's going on here?
*Adam, who also didn't seem to understand the situation, cocked his head.*
Eve: Are you familiar with Raziel's raison d'etre?
Setsuna: No... I'm not.
Eve: Her raison d'etre is _taking records_. Originally she was a very simple angel — her sole role was to simply record the truth on parchment, and share it with the mortals.
Raziel: Sefer Raziel. Boot.
*The giant book flew open before her, lines of blue letters floating up in the air above it.*
Eve: There is no document more special than her book, however. No grimoires or any other writings could ever compare to the knowledge stored within it.
Eve: No one ever questioned it. Adam, Noah, Solomon, Abraham, Jacob — only the knowledge in this book allowed them to overcome God's trials.
Eve: Even among angels, the Sefer Raziel was regarded as the sole word of truth — a tome with power to influence even God. Everyone conceptualized it so in complete unity.
Eve: And Raziel is the one that has written it. The only one that can inscribe new verses into it.
*I gulped at Eve's words. If that was true, and if I understood her right, the true power of Raziel was...*
*_...incredible_. Power that exceeded even that of God's.*
Eve: Truth or not, everything written in that book reverberates back to reality. That is the true power of Raziel and her volume.
Raziel: Raison d'etre variable. Spiral Karma — God dwelleth hither.
*With Raziel's words, a colossal throne manifested out of thin air. And in its wake, giant curtains expanded around us.*
*Atop the throne there was a _thing_.*
Adam: Hmm. Is this God?
*Adam was the only one that showed little surprise at its appearance. I, along with Raziel and Eve, could only stare at the thing, our mouths agape.*
*God made humans in his image.*
*Nothing seemed further from the truth — he hardly looked like a living thing, much less human.*
*A giant object made of carbon tubes. It looked more like some sort of symbol or a logo than an actual being.*
*No face. No neck. No torso. No limbs. Probably no organs, either.*
*A creature defying common sense, its visage devoid of any and all features that could be attributed to a living being.*
*Yet, here it is... right in front of us.*
Raziel: Did this thing... truly create us...?
*Raziel had her eyes fixed on "God," trying to suppress the vomit rising up her throat.*
Eve: Neither beautiful, nor ugly; just dreadfully cold — a being far removed from the concept of an animal. So that's the true face of our Father, our God.
*Eve glared at God defiantly.*
Setsuna: Is this thing alive?
*That was probably the question that swirled in everyone's minds. Through the power of Raziel's raison d'etre, God was finally laid bare in front of the eyes of mortals.*
*If it looked like an animal — a human or a dog — we might have at least felt something. We might have found it terrifying, or it might have impressed us with its divinity.*
*But this thing had none of that. I felt neither dignity, nor holiness, nor terror from the thing sitting — or should I say standing — on the throne.*
*All I felt was undiluted dread. He was too far removed from anything human, anything animate.*
Raziel: He should be alive, at the very least.
*Raziel uttered the words with little confidence.*
Eve: It's alive. Although, now that I think about it, that word should be reserved to beings that used to possess life. It _exists_.
*The thing filled me with dread. How did it move? How did it carry out its life processes?*
Adam: Do you think this being can understand words? Can we communicate with it?
Raziel: We should be able to. I-If that wasn't the case, then God's words we had listened and abided to till now would become mere _hallucinations_ on our part.
*That would be the case, indeed. The notion was ridiculous. ...Right?*
Setsuna: But even if we can communicate with it, are you sure He will help us?
*That was my main fear. Having a chat with God was all well and good, but at the same time, the present apocalypse was doubtless partly caused by... the thing.*
*It would still be all right if it had lost its powers and proved useless. It would still be all right if it had a stance of noninvolvement and would leave us alone.*
*However—*
*Suddenly, a voice reverberated across the white space, making us all flinch in unison. It came from... Huh?*
??? / God: Rebooting. Warning. Currently in the process of rebooting.
*Rebooting? Oh no—*
Adam: What...?!
??? / God: Warning. Hardware intertwined in the lower dimension. Current existential space three dimensional. Physical law influence - high. Five seconds until full system reboot.
*God started moving. Expelling a burst of fumes, it floated upward.*
*This wasn't good. I didn't know why, but I had a very bad feeling about this.*
??? / God: Formatting all devices. Memory error detected. Cut. Initiating Creation script.
*Something akin to spiked tentacles shot out of the thing, sticking into the ground below it. My bad feeling grew even worse.*
Setsuna: Raziel, fall back! Hurry!
*The God kept announcing its condition in an emotionless tone.*
??? / God: Check... Error. Corrupt file. Initiating deletion process... Error. Error. Error.
*There was no way we could get through to that cursed thing...!*
??? / God: Warning. Unable to initiate script due to corrupt files. Proceeding with physical elimination of the error.
*Adam and I glanced at each other, and we sighed in unison — "physical elimination."*
*At least now it was clear. Mad or not, God meant us harm.*
*Not to mention that from what he (?) said, it seemed like his target was the entire world, rather than just us.*
Adam: I do not think we have a choice.
*Letting out a sigh of resignation, Adam pulled his sword out of the pocket dimension. After considering the Divine Sword Archistrategos in his hand for a few seconds, he made a troubled face.*
Adam: Well, let us see if this works.
*Adam swung the sword in a careless manner. The divine flame that escaped its tip blazed towards God.*
??? / God: Initiating dimensional transfer. Complete.
*The burn marks caused by Archistrategos promptly vanished from God's body. Adam clicked his tongue.*
Adam: This will take forever.
*Indeed. While it didn't seem to be immune to physical harm, it healed its wounds at an incredible rate.*
Adam: What do you propose we do, Tendou Setsuna?
Setsuna: Don't ask me. Besides, I doubt I need to explain the one option still left to us.
*Adam cracked his knuckles, and gave me a nod.*
Adam: You need not. In essence, the one who crushes it first prevails.
Setsuna: Exactly. A battle of sheer strength.
*I took a deep breath. A half-baked weapon wouldn't work against that thing.*
Adam: In any case, could you please move aside before I end up accidentally frying you?
Setsuna: ...You can move away yourself, or I'll make sure to hit you too with my next attack.
Raziel: U-Um, could you two please be nice to each other?
The Two: No, thanks.
Eve: ......
??? / God: Forcefully initiating the first line of Creation. Let there be light — fiat lux.
*Finding it convenient to attack as we stopped to chat, God launched a volley of light-bullets at us.*
Setsuna: Tch...!
*I chose to dodge; Adam counter-attacked.*
Adam: Archistrategos!
*The divine flame of Archangel Michael met the light-bullets mid-flight. I myself struck a couple of them out of the air with my Peccati Sword, dodging the rest.*
Setsuna: Raziel! We have our hands full here, so please try to look out for yourself!
Raziel: O-Okay!
*Raziel summoned a wall of mud to protect Eve and herself.*
Setsuna: Come forth, seven beasts! Full Fire!
*The avatars of all seven deadly sins shot forward, some to devour the bullets, some to repel them away. Unfortunately, even they had to eventually give in to the never-ending volley of light.*
Setsuna: Adam, get out of there.
Adam: I'm fine.
Setsuna: Get out of there, goddammit!
*Adam took a step back with a dissatisfied look on his face. Using that as my cue, I flew into the sky. The bullets, of course, followed.*
*I cast my spell, summoning the one armament fit for this situation to my right hand.*
A weapon of mass destruction: the laser-guided bunker buster codenamed "Holy Nail."
*I hurled it like a javelin. Penetrating the volley of bullets like they were nothing, it hit God straight in the middle, exploding in a fiery inferno.*
Setsuna: Go!
*My words as his cue, Adam started towards our blazing foe.*
Adam: Hahh!
*The sword of Archangel Michael split God in two.*
??? / God: Initiate repair protocol.
*With a tone of complete indifference, God proceeded to repair its body (if you could call that dreadful frame a body).*
Adam: ...How ironic.
*Adam threw his sword to the ground. What part of this situation did he exactly find funny?*
*He stuck his right hand out, and pointed his finger straight at God.*
Adam: Don't you find it ironic how I, the original man and your creation, shall destroy you with weapons that were blessed by your own angel servants?
*Adam let out a cry.*
Adam: My raison d'etre is that of a blessing.
*The primordial man reimagined and blessed by a legion of angels.*
*Without hesitation, he declared his existence blessed. And with a blessing of countless angels to back it up, he transformed into the embodiment of justice. In other words, he made all those that opposed him _irrefutably evil_.*
Adam: I condemn you, and request trial by ordeal! You are evil, tainted by the devil. And so it is your irrevocable fate to be felled by the blade of justice.
*The world changed with his words. For God suddenly _turned_ evil. The one in front of our eyes was now a demon, the devil himself, a wicked spirit to be banished.*
Adam: To battle!
*Clutching Michael's sword in both of his hands, Adam sprang forward.*
Adam: Archistrategos!
*God's body split in two again. Adam let the sword fall out of his hands indifferently, summoning another weapon the next moment.*
Adam: Durandal! Curtana!
*Durandal, a sword that Archangel Raphael had entrusted to the hero Roland. With a hilt of pure gold, and a blade that was said to cut through everything in this world, it was easily one of the mightiest holy weapons in the multiverse.*
*Meanwhile, Curtana was a sword of mercy passed in the family of British monarchs. The two swords pierced the hard shell of God.*
Adam: Ascalon!
*The holy sword that served Saint George in slaying the dragon. Its design crude, it looked more like a giant mace than a sword. And so it crushed, rather than severed the remainder of God's carapace that it fell upon.*
Adam: Colada! Tizona!
*The two swords of the medieval Spanish knight El Cid. Colada, a sword made of gold, except for its steel edge, and Tizona, the blade which burned in perpetual flame.*
Adam: Longinus!
*The Holy Spear that needed no introduction, the lance that pierced and killed Jesus Christ himself. The weapon of pure white, only the tip of which had been eternally colored in crimson, pierced through God.*
*All holy weapons, without exception. All born to banish wickedness. And right now, God was indeed _irrefutably evil_.*
*The blessed weapons creaked in unison, obliterating the wicked god. With their saintly magic, they annihilated, crushed, and decimated all _evil_ in their path.*
*He was invincible.*
*Adam's raison d'etre bordered on the inconceivable.*
*His iron will bolstered enough power to condemn even his own creator — God — that, in the end, had no way to oppose such adamant denunciation.*
*It was proof that Adam never was God's puppet. The inexplicable revulsion I felt towards the man had not waned; nevertheless, I couldn't help but admire his gallant display.*
*At the very same time, however, I felt myself overcome by hatred. _Blessing_. I myself had been born under the blessings of billions, yet the path I ultimately walked was nothing but a curse.*
*And so I finally understood. From the very beginning, I had been seeing myself in Adam.*
Adam: This is the end, our divine father. Maker of my flesh and bone!
*I readied the Sword of the Seven Deadly Sins, thinking to help Adam finish the thing.*
*Suddenly, a bolt of electricity shot through my veins.*
*Adam, preoccupied with the ruins of what used to be God, was about to be caught completely unawares.*
Setsuna: Dodge, you damn fool!
*Surprised by the intensity of my own howl, I got a hold of Adam's shoulders and pushed him towards the confused Raziel and Eve behind my back.*
*It was coming!*
*I could tell, with a certainty. Something would fall upon us the very next moment. I had to block it! No matter the cost!*
??? / Metatron: Divine Destruction — the Harbinger of Ash.
*A pillar of light fell on God from the depths of the sky, covering the scenery in crimson flames.*
*A tsunami of fire; a flood of inferno. Needless to say, the flames eventually jumped out at us as well.*
Setsuna: The world turns through the cogs of an ***.
*There was no use trying to block it. Those flames were potent enough to evaporate entire seas in an instant. We could have put the entirety of our magic to defend ourselves, and they'd still most likely turn even our bones to ash.*
*Hence, only the cool-headed touch of science could save us from this predicament. A flock of basketball-sized white orbs surrounded us at all angles.*
Adam: What on earth is this?
Setsuna: Extinguishant.
*The orbs split apart as they came into contact with the flood of fire. After coming apart, however, the orbs turned into bubbles that _stuck_ to the flames, taking their vigor away.*
*Then new orbs would come into being one after the other, repeating the whole process again.*
*The fire couldn't reach us — the narrow space around us remained unaltered, surrounding air somewhat cool to the skin, ignorant of the surrounding flames.*
*Everything else around us, though, seemed like a sight from hell itself.*
Raziel: The pillar of flame. The very one God used to fashion _his_ body.
*Raziel managed to force a few words out despite her stupor.*
*The flames that once split the sea apart to save Moses and his people now consumed Heaven, and the body of God himself.*
*And there was but one angel who could possibly command such power at will.*
Adam: So he finally turns up.
*Raziel gave Adam a nod. Like a receding wave, the flames eventually lost their former vigor.*
Raziel: No doubt about it.
??? / God: Initiating reboot. Illegal operation. Error. Error. Error. Error. Error. Error.
*A single piece of God's carapace still remained, writhing on the ground. Though not for long, as a shape of a man suddenly felt down from the sky, crushing it under its feet.*
*Inexplicable joy assailed every pore of my body as I saw the face of our new guest.*
*I had finally found him.*
??? / Metatron: A wise man once said — God is dead. And with such fitting words I declare this reality absolute. _God has died_.
Setsuna: ...Metatron.
Metatron: God ceased to exist. The dreadful abomination that hoodwinked everyone into believing he and men were of the same image, no longer taints this world.
Raziel: Should I say it has been a while, Metatron? I doubt condemning you at this point bears any meaning, but I'd still like to ask: Why?
Metatron: Why? You ask me questions, Raziel; you, the very harborer of God's secrets? Then answer me first: could you still have continued to revere the Lord after learning of its true form?
*Its true form. A dreadful thing that didn't look like anything living, much less a human being.*
Raziel: You've seen him, Metatron? You witnessed God's true form?
Metatron: Yes, indeed I have. Though it was Gethel who first laid eyes upon it.
Setsuna: Gethel...
Metatron: Having glimpsed God's true form, and comprehending what kind of abomination our Lord truly was, she clung to me. And so I borrowed her eyes to see it for myself.
*Gethel was the first one to see God?*
Metatron: Worthless! Not even a living thing! I vowed to demolish the dreadful thing right there and then!
Metatron: Can you believe a _thing_ like that had the audacity to actually cause the flood that swallowed most of mankind?
Metatron: And then it succumbed to madness. It gave birth to the Divine Calamity, tearing asunder countless worlds of the multiverse, and soiling Heaven itself with blood.
*Overpowered by Metatron's vehemence, no one could bolster the strength to utter a single word till now. But this last remark seemed to have triggered something in Raziel.*
Raziel: Metatron. Just tell me one thing. Was it our Father that caused the Divine Calamity after all?
Metatron: Who else could have?
*Raziel seemed to swallow her next words.*
Raziel: ...Th-That's true, but...
Metatron: This world lives on borrowed time, Raziel. You understand that much yourself, do you not? The multiverse is about to vanish without a trace.
Raziel: No! It... It hasn't ended yet!
Metatron: Yes, indeed. We ourselves have yet to perish. And the future is the sole asylum for us to cheat the end.
Setsuna: But that future's one that had discarded all of its past, isn't it?
Metatron: And what of it, wraith of yore? The future of my making needs no past.
*Metatron considered the four of us coldly for a few seconds.*
Metatron: Raziel, abandon your book. It too is now but a relic of the past.
Raziel: You yourself gained your divine wisdom from its very pages. And you are telling me to throw it away now?
Metatron: It's an article of the past.
Raziel: Aahh—
*Raziel hung her head, shaking it in resignation.*
Raziel: So you couldn't bear it? The torment was too much for you?
*He ascended to Heaven as a mere mortal, and despite being looked down upon by all of its old inhabitants, he kept struggling to improve himself.*
*He struggled to help God, to help mankind.*
*He struggled and struggled, struggled and struggled, struggled and struggled, struggled and struggled, struggled and struggled, struggled and struggled, struggled and struggled, the fruits of his labor disregarded by everyone, he continued to struggle.*
*And the result of his struggle? God went mad, destroying, ruining everything the man had worked for.*
*He realized that he worshipped a dreadful thing that never was truly alive. That he admired, venerated, and served a sham.*
Metatron: Well, now that things have come to this... it no longer matters.
Adam: In any case, I believe it's clear we are at odds with you. Shall we begin our bout to the death or do I need to wait longer?
*Adam took a step forward. Metatron, his eyes fixed on the original man, made a scornful smile.*
Metatron: Adam. Putting aside the other three, I have no reason to quarrel with you.
Adam: ...What?
Metatron: You are an Adam of the future that angels have devised. The old world does not suit you. Join our ranks.
Adam: Absurd.
Metatron: There's nothing absurd about it. You were made by the surviving angels of this world. Raziel, Camael, Remiel, and _myself_.
Eve: Wh-What?!
Metatron: Although I hid myself from prying eyes, I, too, resided in Pandora. Sometimes as an angel, sometimes as a demon, sometimes as a human.
Adam: And so what if you participated in my making?
*Adam gritted his teeth in irritation.*
Metatron: Oh? Will you deny the word of your father?
Adam: Shut your mouth. You said _the other three_ a moment ago. You omitted Eve from those you wished to save.
Eve: ......
Adam: Unforgivable. You will pay for that. The moment you uttered those words, you became my foe. Father or brother — anyone that dares insult _her_ is my enemy.

Eve: Stop... Stop, Adam!
Adam: The time for words is past!
Metatron: Indeed, continuing this one-sided conversation is truly a waste of breath.

*No sound followed. Neither the splatter of rending flesh, nor the clang of the sword having been parried.*
Adam: ...!
Metatron: Adam, did I not just tell you that it was us angels who designed you? Did you truly believe we would have you run free without installing a failsafe device of sorts?

Metatron: You cannot hurt me.
Adam: Gh—
*Gritting his teeth, Adam put all of his strength into pushing the sword forward.*
Metatron: Out of my way, _failure_.

Metatron: Serving Adam is the sole matter Eve is good for. My future doesn't need her. And Raziel, you too — a slave of the past, unable to cast aside your book — have no place in my world.

Messenger: Be a good girl and keep still.

Metatron: Only one remains now.
*Metatron finally turned to me. Oddly, I didn't feel afraid. The situation was simple — kill and prevail, or die and perish.*
Setsuna: How's Sorami doing?
Metatron: The girl is the Eve of the new world. Your name is outdated.
Setsuna: I'm asking how Sorami's doing.
Metatron: ......
*Metatron sighed, and snapped his fingers. The next moment, a girl appeared by his side.*
Sorami: ......
Setsuna: Sorami!

*Her pupils sparkled in gold. Did she boot Gethel's eyes?*
*Metatron whispered something to the lifeless girl.*
Metatron: Kugutsu Sorami, the time has come to initiate your raison d'etre.
*The girl, her expression still a void, nodded.*
Sorami: ...Yes.
Metatron: Open the gates to the future.

Sorami: Oh. Here it is.

*Then she reached out and grasped something that no one else but her could apparently see, pulling it towards herself.*
Sorami: Hope had sprouted, yet so did despair. Evil reigned, yet so did good. They had called it Heaven and Hell.
Sorami: Incorporate countless contradictions. Incorporate countless elements. Incorporate countless possibilities.
Sorami: And erase them all, leaving only one intact.
Sorami: O time that hath to flow. O time that hath to halt. Entrust thine essence to the gates, cast thine nature aside. Sacrifice the world for the segregated future.

*Vision that led to the future. Eyes that had the power to define the future through mere observation. Something from beyond time was on its way to our realm.*
Sorami: Jerusalem.
*Countless strands of light, rending white space asunder, appeared out of thin air. The strands eventually melted into an arc, morphing into something akin to a white door.*
*Sorami collapsed like a puppet with its string cut.*
Setsuna: Sorami.
Metatron: Messenger, I leave her in your hands.
Messenger: Your wish is my command.
*Sorami suddenly vanished from my sight.*
Metatron: The matter is as you witnessed. I shall defeat you all, and pass these gates along with the girl and others deemed worthy of the future. To a place brimming with hope, severed from this worthless world.
*My blood was ready to boil over by the time he ended his speech.*
*Calm down. Calm down, Tendou Setsuna. Focus on defeating the damn angel in front of you right now...!*
*I pulled the Sword of the Seven Deadly Sins from the pocket dimension, and lunged forward. Concentrating my magic to it, I initiated the summoning protocol.*
Setsuna: Reveal yourself, O avatar of Gluttony! Shed pride and cast aside worldly wisdom as you quench your voracious appetite, drowning in pleasures unbound!
*Letting out a deafening snort, the giant boar opened its vast jaws.*
Metatron: Useless...!
*Metatron swung his hand once and the beast split apart. Probably finding the idea of dirtying himself with blood unappealing, he took a step back to avoid the rain of crimson that followed.*
*Skipping over the carapace of the beast in a split second, I launched a drop down kick at Metatron.*
Metatron: ...!
*It did connect, but Metatron managed to guard against it with his steel arm.*
*Though it seemed to have succeeded at upsetting him at least — the blood that flung from my feet as I launched the kick splattered all over him.*
*Metatron shuddered in anger at having himself besmirched with filthy blood.*
Metatron: You insolent...!
*Not listening, I swung my sword downward. Metatron answered by pulling his own sword out of the pocket dimension, and clashing it against mine.*
Setsuna: That blade...!
*A silver blade of incredible length, adorned with strange geometric symbols. Could it be—*
Metatron: Shirayamahime Kabanemaru. It was my present to the boy.
*Exceeding the speed of Oshiba Hagane, he flung Kabanemaru at me. Steel met steel, magic bursting out of the point of contact together with sparks.*
*I imbued my muscle cells with Takemikazuchi, and somehow pushed his future-defining blade away.*
*I proceeded to push my blade diagonally down towards his shoulder, to which he promptly answered with his own swing from below. The attack that defied both time and space reached me before I had time to finish mine.*
Setsuna: Tch...!
*I thought I dodged it, but it seemed that wasn't the case. I avoided a mortal wound by a hair's breadth. Good thing I wasn't too mindful about my spinal cord cracking as I twisted my body, or I would have been dead by now.*
*Now I managed to escape with only my shoulder damaged. Ordering my nanomachines to fix the wound, and imbuing their function with _water_ magic, I proceeded to counter-attack.*
*I chose the seven beasts, summoning them all at once.*
Setsuna: Full Fire...!
*The Beast of Gluttony. The Molten Gold of Sloth. The Azure Flame of Wrath. The Rotten Chains of Envy. The Silver Lion of Pride. The Mirror Knight of Lust.*
*Calling them all at once, I crashed them straight into Metatron. But I knew that wouldn't be enough, not even close to defeat the steel angel.*
Metatron: I exist for the future.
*A stringent sound reverberated in my ears. I jumped back out of reflex, feeling an odd tingle at my right arm. I tried raising it up, and realized it was gone.*
Setsuna: He cut it off?
*It seemed like that sound and tingle resulted from my arm being chopped off. I neither despaired, nor displayed shock at losing the limb — I knew accidents like that were part of battle.*
*As I looked back at Metatron, I spotted some sort of emerald string-like things surrounding him.*
*Enlarge... Decrypt. That thread seemed to have been made exclusively of ones and zeroes.*
Metatron: Electro-twine, a program capable of intervening and reprogramming the space of reality.
*I glanced at my arm lying on the ground. Nothing grotesque like meat stuck out of its cross section; though it turned the color of black, as if coated in coal tar.*
Metatron: I cut off the status of your right arm. You won't be able to repair it easily.
*It seemed he wasn't lying — I tried ordering my nanomachines to regenerate it, but my cells simply refused to listen.*
*For better or worse, I didn't feel pain either. Still, I realized this had put me at a serious disadvantage; I felt the fangs of cold fear begin digging into my heart.*
*I didn't quite know how to proceed.*
*Metatron had yet to activate his raison d'etre.*
*And as long as he didn't, I couldn't activate mine either — understanding the properties of my foe was the core element of my counter-attack spell.*
*What was he living for? What did he expect to find in that future of his? I had to understand him enough to at least find answers to these questions.*
*He was not like Oshiba Hagane. The boy I slayed rejected both the past and the present, but he still acknowledged the future, for whatever it was.*
*The core element of his being was resignation or, in a way, hope.*
*Metatron used to be known as the Righteous Enoch. An angel of supreme power, closest to God, even called "the lesser God" by some.*
*Think. Think. Think. Think. What were the core aspects of his existence?*
*What were the core deeds he performed? He first defied God, then served and revered Him. Then his Lord let him down again, and in response, he trampled over him.*
*Now he was trying to surpass his divine father, become a more absolute existence. He made a new world of his own design, and even prepared an "Eve" for it — Sorami.*
*Discarding both past and the present, he decided to save the future alone.*
*The past of most had been soaked full from shed blood, and the present could at times be as harsh as a winter's gale.*
*But the future, severed clean from the bitter past and the tough present, would be as bright as the sun itself. Without inheriting ill will from the past, Metatron would create a new, clean world.*
*In other words— Hoping to lead him on a little, I parted my lips.*
Setsuna: Metatron, you are an angel, and so lies and deceit are forbidden to you. Hence, I would like to ask you something.
Metatron: ...What is it?
Setsuna: You do not really care about the order of your future world.
*I took a deep breath, and readied my words like a blade.*
Setsuna: You just _cannot stand the past_. The memories of being looked down upon, and then being betrayed by the very object of your worship — your disappointment intermingled with rancor, and you just grew to hate all and everything of the old world, did you not?
Metatron: ......
*I could spot a slight change in Metatron's countenance.*
Setsuna: What is it Metatron? I can feel your killing intent tickling my skin. Did my words hurt you that much? Ehh? You chicken archangel!
Metatron: I see you are a glutton for punishment, insolent wretch...!
*With almost palpable killing intent, Metatron lunged towards me.*
Adam: Use this!
*A ridiculously blunt heads-up reached me through the telepathic link. I vaulted into the sky, catching Adam's projectile in my left hand, letting the Peccati Sword fall down to the ground.*

*The flaming sword of Archangel Michael. The sole weapon that could oppose Metatron's flames.*
*And so the weapon currently in his hands could do little against it—*
Setsuna: That sword belongs to Oshiba Hagane. It isn't for the likes of you to wield!
*The divine flames of the archangel were potent enough to melt down a witchblade like Shirayamahime Kabanemaru.*
*The blade in Metatron's hands turned to a mere unshapely stick of molten steel, only the intact hilt still testified it actually used to be a sword.*
Metatron: You should know it originally belonged to me...
*With that, he threw the molten sword aside. He had no right to brag; all he ever did was hand the blade to Oshiba Hagane, who was the one that mastered and made it truly his own.*
*With a mocking smirk on his face, Metatron readied something akin to a wand.*
Metatron: Then let me show you the true face of the future.
*I felt my back turn to ice.*
Metatron: Harbinger of Ash.
*A beam of blinding light shot out of the both ends of the wand, turning it into something akin to a double-bladed sword. Black threads of indescribable material appeared out of thin air and coiled around its blade.*
*I could tell it was the very weapon that launched the inferno that annihilated God.*
*Having it pointed at me was enough to fill me with a sensation of impending doom, a feeling that my very soul could possibly turn to dust the next second.*
*Still, I had to determine the nature of this weapon. Colored black and white, it could launch all-obliterating pillars of flame — a weapon of divine destruction from the future.*
*The flames that assaulted us back then were vigorous like a torrent. Still, I had already countered them once, and could do so again.*
*For flames, no matter how potent, were still fire, combustion. As long as they obeyed the laws of science, I could find countless ways to neutralize them.*
*My only worry was that they might've contained a sort of alternate spiritual effect that, when unleashed, would unveil some non-scientific power.*
*In the history of men, flame used to symbolize divinity in countless scriptures.*
*For example, after Adam and Eve were banished from the paradise, God assigned cherubs of his legion to keep humans away from the border between the realms. And they were all outfitted with swords of fire.*
*Even among his lieutenants, the name of Uriel translated to "Flame of God."*
*Meanwhile, Anafi'el utilized sixty fiery rods to punish Metatron for his transgressions, the same ones that we'd been running away from on the sixth stratum.*
*Archangel Sandalphon had been so powerful, the flames raging within him burst out of his body, burning another seraph — Hadraniel.*
*And finally, Metatron— Among titles such as the Chancellor of Heaven, or the lesser God, he had also been called a pillar of fire.*
*Apparently, it came from the idea that the flame pillar that guided Moses was Metatron himself.*
*The embodiment of guidance — a pillar of fire. What kind of divine essence could have been hidden in this name?*
*I was about to enter the biggest mad gamble of my life.*
*1. Take Metatron's attack head-on, and survive somehow. 2. Ascertain its nature. 3. Counterattack.*
*I could do it. I could do it. I had no choice, so I had to do it.*
*I gritted my teeth.*
*I steeled my heart to take the hit without trying to run, but also refusing to give in to the sweet call of abandoning sensible thought. As long as life coursed in my veins, I'd continue to think, looking for an opening in his offensive.*
Metatron: Do you have any last words?
Setsuna: I'll tell you later.
*Metatron gave me a confident smile. He seemed to have absolute faith in his weapon.*
Metatron: Harbinger of Ash. Mode: Rejection. The earth had been made for mankind to crawl upon; this is no place for you, mortal.
*The black and white of his blade intermingled to form a spiral, and spun at me like a giant snake.*
Adam: Dodge, you fool!
Setsuna: You don't need to tell me!
*Exceeding the speed of Anafi'el's whip, the monochromal light pursued me like a lock-on missile.*
Setsuna: Tch...!

*A power of untold magnitude pursued me, hell-bent on eradicating me to the very soul.*
Raziel: Setsuna!
*I bent my body at a painful angle to avoid the light, but it promptly turned around and shot at me again. I couldn't dodge this one!*
*I glanced down, and readied Michael's sword to meet the light head-on.*
Setsuna: I'm going to do this...!
*In the end, I didn't learn much. A technique of rejection, launching a light of lethal intensity that pursued its target relentlessly.*
*It definitely had a spiritual factor to it, but I still couldn't tell what it was.*
*I couldn't read his deck. Mine, on the other hand, barely had any cards left. Still, I had to do this. I had no choice but to meet him head-on.*
*I released the magic of the sword, making it explode in azure flames. The Sword of Archistrategos Michael.*
*At this point, the chemistry mattered little. It made no difference whether I met a flame this potent with water, or another flame.*
*The beam closing in on me embodied the full might of an archangel closest to God. The flames at my side embodied the full might of an archangel that led God's legions.*
*And I also added my own power to the mix.*
Setsuna: Nraaaaaaa...!
*I crashed my sword into the light with a howl. Flame clashed with flame, and... ...Huh?*
Metatron: The role of cherubs ordained with the defense of Eden's eastern border was but one: to repel mankind. To make certain Adam and Eve were barred eternally from paradise.
*Metatron let out a scornful snort.*
Metatron: This technique is grounded in that legend. Mankind shall dwell on earth, and nowhere else. We alone shall bask in Eden's divine light.
*I finally comprehended the vileness of his flame.*
*Targeting only humans, pursuing them to the ends of the earth; rejecting, consuming them — it was a weapon custom-tailored for hunting mankind.*
*And so it had no effect on anything else. No matter how strong Michael's Sword was, Metatron's flames would slip past it as it was never their target, crashing into me alone.*
*Flames like a fraud. Still, few things could have been more effective in this situation. I met them head-on just like Don Quixote did the windmill.*
*I felt death breathing down on my neck.*
*Was it the end? Resignation overcame me. After all this... after I had finally seen through his nature...*
*Unable to withstand the fiery embrace, I'd turn to ash in a few seconds. Goddammit.*
Setsuna: God... fucking... dammit!
Adam: How much of a witless fool are you? If you have time to howl, use it protect your life.
*An annoying remark found me mere moments before the flames could consume me. Suddenly, I was flung aside.*
Metatron: Hm?
Adam: Gh...!
*Adam crashed into the flames in my stead. The hands he used to protect his face turned the color of coal, yet the onslaught of fire refused to cease.*
Adam: Nhghgh...!

Setsuna: Adam...

Setsuna: I would like to ask you the sa—
Adam: Shut up, and go already!
*Giving him a quick nod, I dashed forward.*
Metatron: Hmm. I knew it would come to this sooner or later, but, well... Aren't you a nice sacrificial lamb, extinguishing your own life to extend that of another, if only for a few fleeting seconds.
Metatron: I imagine you thought of sacrificing yourself to God in any case — such is your raison d'etre, after all. Aren't you glad I was here to put you out of your misery?

Adam: Shut up.
Metatron: Oh? You're not satisfied?

Adam: ......

Metatron: This ends now.
Setsuna: Indeed.
*Metatron directed his gaze up to the sky and saw Tendou Setsuna floating serenely up there.*
*The magic flowing through his veins turned to ice for a split second. For the eyes of the boy looked like those of the angels that used to look down upon him.*
*Uncontrollable fury took hold of Metatron.*
Metatron: What are you doing there?! Come down this very instant!
*What surprised the angel the most was that the boy seemed to have escaped the jurisdiction of electro-twine — both of his arms were back in their place, fully regenerated.*
Setsuna: Were you this bothered by others looking down on you?

Setsuna: The world turns through the cogs of an intricate mechanism.

*Metatron's true nature.*
*The pride of having attained power exceeding that of Michael, despite having been born a mortal.*
*And at the same time, the feeling of inadequacy for being different, isolated from other divine servants of the Lord. The two conflicting emotions doubtless tortured him to no end.*
*But that was never his true nature. He served God's throne. He felt himself closest to the Lord.*
*And hence he had but a singular dream. To merge himself and God into one.*
*The lesser God. He who is closest to God. He was called so; he acted so. At times he went overboard, getting sentenced to many a lash of the whip.*
*Nonetheless, he had never given up on becoming God. And that was why he schemed to lord over the future.*
*Despite all that...*
*His technique made little sense. If he wanted to become God — absolute — his power should be that of crushing all and everything that opposed him indiscriminately.*
*Yet the flame he launched at me was that of "rejection." Scorching only one chosen target.*
*In other words— In the end, he rejected everyone other than himself.*
*Still, he _had_ to become God, and rule over all that he despised. God can only be God as long as there are others to define him as such. "Let there be light" gave birth not only to the world but also God himself.*
*Wishing for lordship out of pride, and rejecting others out of a feeling of inadequacy.*

Setsuna: Universal Machine / The Guardian Spirit of Time — grant me a blade that carries blessing and curse alike.

*Regular techniques of swordsmanship were no use when wielding giant scissors.*
*As such, I felt as if the peculiar blade controlled my actions, rather than the other way around.*

*Thirteenth... Fourteenth clash... I refused to cease my assault, spinning at Metatron in the fashion of a tempest.*

Metatron: Gh... Mode: Rejection.

Setsuna: Sever the knot, Gordias!

*Pride and inadequacy.*
*The contradictory nature of his inability to stand being surpassed by mortals, yet having his very roots in their flock, coupled with being looked down upon by other angels as _buyo_.*

*Ahh, he reminded me of myself. I tried to become a god once as well; I was designed to become one.*

*I never wished to become a god. For the concept of the Lord was always a painfully plain and simple program.*

Setsuna: Such is the true nature of God! He has to be like that!

*And now his dream of taking his old Lord's place — his very raison d'etre — was on the verge of collapse.*
*The days he spent on earth as the Righteous Enoch; the millenniums he spent as the mightiest of angels, Metatron — all of his deeds, accomplishments were on the verge of returning to dust.*

Metatron: Yet God and I were still worlds apart. I could not lay eyes upon him.
*Whenever doubt sprouted in his heart, it would be promptly dispelled by a whisper directly from the Lord. And so he prided himself on being one of his servants.*
*One day, God left the future in his hands. Past, present, and the future. In Heaven, where the border between these concepts was vague, only God himself had the right to tinker with the future.*
*After Metatron received his divine decree, he proceeded to nurture the new world.*
*Yet it all fell apart with the advent of the Divine Calamity. God banished angels from Heaven, while Hell succumbed to a massive flood.*
*And so Metatron promptly severed the ties between the present and the future. With that, all of the current worlds lost the power to advance forward.*
*And so they withered away. While the ones that somehow managed to hold out for a while longer were eventually destroyed by God's madness.*
*Still, Metatron considered this a temporal measure. He planned to eventually cure God, and resurrect the withered worlds back to their prime.*

*There was no complex reason for it. He didn't feel he _had_ to do it.*
*It was instinct. It was the first and only desire that had ever visited his heart.*
*The question of forgiveness mattered little to him. So what if she betrayed him? All was right as long as he wasn't the one doing the betraying.*
*She could have used and manipulated him till the end of his days, and he would still not have minded.*
*Hence, he couldn't understand the reason behind Eve's tears. He only ever wished for her to smile.*
Eve: Adam.
*With her tears finally dried up, Eve stopped trying to evade the gaze of her husband, and looked him straight in the eye.*
Eve: Adam, are you really my husband?
Adam: Of course I am.
*Eve gave him a deep look. It was probably the first time in her life that she had ever gazed at someone for this long.*
Eve: Then... can I love you, too?
*She felt embarrassed by her own words all of a sudden.*
Adam: Yes.
*She had always dreaded putting her feelings into words.*
Eve: Are you going to love me?
Adam: Going to? I've loved you ever since I came to this world.
*Another teardrop traveled involuntarily down her cheek. Ahh. Everything had finally become clear to her.*
*He had always loved her.*
*And so, she silently asked him for one last wish.*
Eve: In that case, will you perish with me?
Adam: If that is your wish.
*Not a trace of hesitation clouded Adam's voice. Eve chuckled to herself.*
*Joy from having her wish fulfilled. Sorrow from getting him involved in her silly scheme.*
*She poured out everything that had been weighing on her soul. And now she smiled at Adam with a final wish on her lips.*
Eve: Adam, please hear me out. It's my final, selfish request to you. Kill Tendou Setsuna and Kugutsu Sorami. Destroy the world. Please.
*Adam gave her an affectionate smile.*
Adam: If that is what you wish, I will gladly carry it out For I am your husband.
Eve: ......
*Following a few moments of hesitation, Adam placed his hand on Eve's head, stroking her hair with a series of slightly awkward, inepxerienced movements.*
*Once finished, he turned around, facing us again.*
Adam: Messenger, make sure to prevent Raziel from interfering. At least until I kill Tendou Setsuna, that is.
Adam: I know not who your true master is, but I beseech you — heed my words now.
Messenger: Very... well.
*Caught off guard by the sudden request, Messenger couldn't help but nod at the regal tone Adam's voice carried.*
*And so, Adam faced Tendou Setsuna, who still wore a detached look on his face.*
Setsuna: Adam, is this what you want?
*I faced Adam, stealing a glance at Eve clinging to him from behind. Adam, in the meantime, gave me a nod with no hesitation at all.*
*The time for words seemed to be over.*
*A memory of that peaceful day we all spent together flashed through my mind. I exhaled the air from my lungs, dispelling all irrelevant thoughts.*
Setsuna: Sorami.

*The two took some distance from us as told. I picked up the Archistrategos Sword from the ground.*
*In the meantime, Adam picked up the Peccati Sword that lay next to his feet.*

Setsuna: Yeah.
*A sensation akin to anger intermingling with anguish and sorrow took hold of my heart for a split second.*
*Still, I had to defeat him. I had to fight him.*
Adam: Fate's a fickle mistress.
Setsuna: Yeah.
*I imagined there might have been another way, but then promptly discarded the thought. There was no other way for us — at least up until now.*
*Inevitability was the chief force at work here. Adam and I couldn't walk the same path together; it was too narrow for the both of us.*

The Two: Shyaaaaaaaaaah!

Adam: Gh...
Setsuna: Kh...

*I had no time to breathe. Nor did I want to.*
*My only joy at present was landing a hit on him, my only sorrow receiving one in return.*
*I paid no heed to the blood trickling down my skin. Or my ever-growing misty surroundings. Not even my own creaking body on the verge of collapse elicited a moment's reprieve.*
Setsuna: Seven Beasts — Full Fire!
*The seven avatars of sin bared their fangs and jumped at Adam.*
Adam: Petty tricks!
*An inferno of fire erupted from Michael's sword. The divine flame that purified all sins it came in contact with.*
*The defeat of the beasts was imminent.*
Setsuna: Kh...!

Setsuna: ...?!
*I lost him! He vanished from sight! Damnit, where was he?!*
Adam: Up here.
*I glanced up — my blood turning to ice — and was promptly met with another explosion of fire. A double-barrel trick, goddammit.*
*The impact was so fierce I thought my body and soul would split apart. I lost my momentum, and crashed onto to the ground. I could feel aqua vitae soaking my clothes.*
Setsuna: Ahh— Khh—
Sorami: Setsuna!

Setsuna: Silver Lion of Pride!

Adam: <,>———?!
